(وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَزْغٌ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): the wāw is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional, its nūn assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) (ما); (ينزغنك) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the kāf is a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (من الشيطان) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (نزغ); (نزغ) is a delayed fāʿil. (فاستعذ): the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ, and (استعذ) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (بالله) is attached to (استعذ); (إن) and its noun; (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; (السميع العليم) are two khabars of (إن) or of (هو), and [in the latter case] the clause is the khabar of (إن).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا» there is eloquent concision (ījāz), because al-istiqāma (uprightness) is a word that encompasses all the attributes of piety. ʿUmar said: Uprightness is:
that you remain upright upon the command and the prohibition and do not swerve the way a fox swerves. And you know what lies folded beneath "the command and the prohibition" of commands and prohibitions. The slightest deviation from the straight path takes one out of one's uprightness; that is because the straight line is the shortest distance between two points, so it does not tolerate drifting, even if it be less than slight.
In the verses there is ṭibāq (antithesis) and jinās al-ishtiqāq (derivational paronomasia) that is not hidden, so we have sufficed with pointing to them.

dervis-irab:37-39.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رَبَتْ): it swelled and rose before it sprouted; a raised place is called rabwa and rābiya. More explanation of it will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to present four of the signs of Allah the Exalted. (من آياته) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (الليل) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and what comes after it is conjoined to it. (لا تَسْجُدُوا لِلشَّمْسِ وَلا لِلْقَمَرِ وَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ): (لا) is prohibitive; (تسجدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); (للشمس) is attached to (تسجدوا); (ولا للقمر) is conjoined; (واسجدوا لله) is another conjoined element; (الذي) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الله); the clause (خلقهن) is the ṣila (relative clause), and the pronoun refers back to the signs. For that reason the four are expressed with the feminine pronoun, even though three of them are masculine and the custom is to let the masculine prevail over the feminine: because when He said (ومن آياته) and strung the four on the thread of "signs", each one of them became a sign (āya, feminine), so they were expressed with the feminine pronoun. (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ being its noun, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (إياه) is a fronted object of (تعبدون); the clause (تعبدون) is the khabar of (كنتم); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then prostrate to Him".
(فَإِنِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا فَالَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ يُسَبِّحُونَ لَهُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَهُمْ لا يَسْأَمُونَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional; (استكبروا) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis. (فالذين): the fāʾ gives the reason for the omitted apodosis, whose implied form is "then leave them to their affair"; (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ; (عند ربك): the adverb is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of (الذين). The adverbiality here is one of rank and honour; it is an expression of nearness and esteem. The clause (يسبحون) is the khabar of (الذين); (له) is attached to (يسبحون); (الليل والنهار) [Translator's note: i.e. (بالليل والنهار)] are also attached to (يسبحون); the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يسأمون) is the khabar. (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى الْأَرْضَ خاشِعَةً فَإِذا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ): the wāw conjoins to what preceded; (من آياته) is a fronted khabar; (أن) and what falls within its scope is a delayed mubtadaʾ; (انك): (أن) and its noun; the clause (ترى الأرض) is the khabar; and (خاشعة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. dry, with no vegetation in it — more of this discussion will come in the section on rhetoric. You may also take the seeing as cognitive (ʿilmiyya), in which case (خاشعة) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فإذا): the fāʾ is conjunctive and (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause (أنزلنا) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (عليها) is attached to (أنزلنا); (الماء) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (اهتزت) has no grammatical position; and (ربت) is conjoined to (اهتزت).
(إِنَّ الَّذِي أَحْياها لَمُحْيِ الْمَوْتى إِنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): giving the reason for the stirring and swelling of the dry earth. (إن) and its noun; the clause (أحياها) is the ṣila; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (محيي الموتى) is the khabar of (إن); (إن) and its noun; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); and (قدير) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): khushūʿ, which is abasement and shrinking, has been borrowed for the state of the earth in its drought and dryness, just as humūd (lifelessness) is borrowed for it in His saying «وترى الأرض هامدة». The same applies to the stirring (al-ihtizāz) and the swelling (al-rabw): one says ihtazza al-insān, i.e. he moved; and rabat, i.e. it swelled and rose before it sprouted. On this reading there is fronting and delaying in the statement, its implied order being "it swelled and stirred". The stirring and swelling may occur before [the plants] come out of the earth, or after the vegetation has come out onto the surface of the earth, its swelling then being its rising. It has also been said: (اهتزت), i.e. it moved a great movement, so it was like one who works at that by himself; and (ربت), i.e. it split open, its soil rose, the vegetation came out of it and rose up into the air covering its face, and it adorned itself with that vegetation as though it were in the position of one strutting in his finery, since before that it had been like one abased.

* Benefits:
1- The effect of the Qur'an on the soul of ʿUtba:
Quraysh realized that their methods of stopping the Islamic call from proceeding on its way had not succeeded and that they had to resort to some other action. So they consulted together as was their custom and delegated ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa to go to the Prophet ﷺ to negotiate with him about abandoning the call, on condition that they would gather wealth for him until he became the richest of Quraysh, then give him the positions of leadership by which he would become the highest of them in standing and the mightiest of them in dominion, or seek medical treatment for him until he was cured of this thing that came to him and made him utter wondrous speech. The Prophet listened to ʿUtba patiently, and when he had finished he said to him:
"Have you finished, O Abū al-Walīd?" He said: "Yes." The Prophet said to him: "Then listen to me." Then he began reciting to him the saying of Allah the Exalted: «حم تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم», and the Messenger of Allah went on reciting Sūrat Fuṣṣilat to his visitor until he reached the saying of Allah the Exalted:
«ومن آياته الليل والنهار» — the verse. When he recited this verse he prostrated to his Lord a long prostration, then raised his head, sat up in his place and went on completing the sūra, until, when he had finished it, he looked at ʿUtba, and behold, he had put his hands behind his back, listening quietly, and the verses had affected him greatly. The Prophet said to him:
- "You have heard, O Abū al-Walīd, what you have heard; so it is up to you."
ʿUtba did not respond with a word and went away troubled, thinking most deeply about what he had heard. No sooner did Quraysh see their companion than some of them said to others:
- "[One] swore by Allah: Abū al-Walīd has come back to you with a face other than the one he went with." [Translator's note: the source has «فحلف بالله», "so he swore by Allah", without a stated subject.]
When he sat with them they said to him: - "What news do you bring, O Abū al-Walīd?" He said:
- "My news is that I have heard speech the like of which, by Allah, I have never heard. By Allah, it is not poetry, nor sorcery, nor soothsaying. O people of Quraysh, obey me and leave this man alone with what he is about; stay away from him, for by Allah, the speech of his that I heard will have great tidings. If the Arabs strike him, you will have been spared him by others; and if he prevails over the Arabs, his dominion is your dominion and his might is your might, and you will be the happiest of people."
Quraysh said:
- "He has bewitched you with his tongue, by Allah, O Abū al-Walīd!" He turned away from them and said:
- "This is my opinion about you; so do what seems good to you."
2- The place of the prostration:
There is disagreement about the place of the prostration. According to al-Shāfiʿī it is at «تعبدون», because the word for prostration is mentioned just before it; and according to Abū Ḥanīfa it is at «يسأمون», because it completes the meaning.

dervis-irab:40-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُلْحِدُونَ): with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the imperfect of alḥada fī dīn Allāh, i.e. he deviated and swerved; it has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the imperfect of laḥada, of the pattern qaṭaʿa, a dialectal variant of it. In al-Kashshāf he said:
"One says alḥada al-ḥāfir and laḥada when the digger inclines away from straightness and digs into a side; then it was borrowed for deviation, in interpreting the verses of the Qur'an, from the direction of soundness and straightness." [Translator's note: the source does not mark where al-Kashshāf's quotation ends; it appears to end here, and what follows is the author's comment.] Al-Zamakhsharī was not correct in restricting that for which it is borrowed by his words "in the verses of the Qur'an", for in the noble verse it is borrowed for deviation from the direction of soundness and straightness absolutely, not for deviation from it in the verses of Allah; otherwise there would have been no need for His saying (في آياتنا). From here the difference appears between the mulḥid (deviator), the zindīq (heretic), the dahrī (materialist) and the munāfiq (hypocrite).
(أَعْجَمِيًّا): the discussion of this word has preceded, and we add here what they said about its yāʾ. Abū Ḥayyān said: "The yāʾ is for intensification in the description; the relation (nisba) in it is not real." Al-Rāzī said in his Lawāmiḥ: "It is like the yāʾ of kursī." Al-aʿjamī is one who does not speak clearly and whose speech is not understood.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِي آياتِنا لا يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنا): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to explain the state of the deviators. (إن) and its noun; the clause (يلحدون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (في آياتنا) is attached to (يلحدون); and the clause (لا يخفون علينا) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).
(أَفَمَنْ يُلْقى فِي النَّارِ خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ يَأْتِي آمِناً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī); the fāʾ conjoins to an implied element that the context requires; (من) is a relative noun and the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يلقى في النار) is the ṣila of (من); (خير) is its khabar; (أم) is a conjunction; (من) is conjoined to the first (من); the clause (يأتي) is the ṣila; and (آمنا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The context would have required Him to say "or one who enters Paradise", but He departed from what the context requires in order to state explicitly their safety and the absence of fear from them, and that is more soothing to their breasts and more comforting to their eyes. (يوم القيامة) is attached to (يأتي) or to (آمنا).
(اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ إِنَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): (اعملوا) is an imperative verb, and what is meant by it is threatening them; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (شئتم) is the ṣila of (ما); the clause (إنه) gives the reason for the command; (إن) and its noun; (بما تعملون) is attached to (بصير); and (بصير) is the khabar of (إن).
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتابٌ عَزِيزٌ): the clause is a badal (substitute) from the preceding (إن) clause. (إن) and its noun; the clause (كفروا بالذكر) is the ṣila; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking (rābiṭa); (جاءهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. Regarding the khabar of (إن) there are several aspects, the most evident being that it is omitted, its implied form being "they are not hidden from Us". What supports this aspect is that the second (إن) is a badal from the first (إن), so what applies to the first applies to it, the rule being that what is predicated of the badal is predicated of that which it replaces. The grammarians mentioned other aspects, a summary of which we give below:
1- That it is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being "will be punished" or "will be destroyed"; this is also a sound aspect.
2- That it is omitted, and al-Jalāl implied it with his words: "We shall requite them."
3- That it is present and mentioned, namely His saying later «أولئك ينادون».
4- That it is present and mentioned, namely His saying «لا يأتيه الباطل», with the referent (ʿāʾid) omitted, i.e. "falsehood from them does not come to it", like "al-mishmish manawān bi-dirham" (apricots, two manns for a dirham), i.e. two manns of it; and the al stands in place of the pronoun in the view of the Kufans, its implied form being: "Those who disbelieved in the Reminder — their falsehood does not come to it."
5- That the khabar is His saying (ما يقال لك), with the referent omitted, its implied form being: "Those who disbelieved in the Reminder — nothing is said to you concerning them except what was said to the messengers before you."
(وإنه): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (كتاب) is its khabar; (عزيز) is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. it is inaccessible to anyone attacking it, through the protection and guardianship of Allah. This is supported by the saying of Allah the Exalted «إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون», so no one is able to nullify it or make a breach in it. (لا يَأْتِيهِ الْباطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ): the clause is a second naʿt of (الكتاب). (لا) is negating; (يأتيه الباطل) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a delayed fāʿil; (من بين يديه) is attached to (يأتيه); (ولا من خلفه) is conjoined to (من بين يديه); (تنزيل) is a fourth khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; only one khabar (كتاب) has been named, and (تنزيل) would more naturally be a further naʿt or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, "it is a revelation"]; (من حكيم) is attached to (تنزيل); and (حميد) is a naʿt of (حكيم).
(ما يُقالُ لَكَ إِلَّا ما قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): a resumptive statement, brought to console him ﷺ for the harm that reached him from them. (ما) is negating; (يقال) is a passive imperfect verb; (لك) is attached to (يقال); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (ما) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "except the like of what"; (قد) is a particle of verification; (قيل للرسل) is the ṣila; and (من قبلك) is a ḥāl.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ وَذُو عِقابٍ أَلِيمٍ): (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; (ذو مغفرة) is its khabar; and (عقاب أليم) [Translator's note: i.e. (وذو عقاب أليم)] is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً أَعْجَمِيًّا لَقالُوا لَوْلا فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُءَ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ): a resumptive statement, brought to answer their questioning: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down in the language of the non-Arabs?" (لو) is conditional; (جعلناه) is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; (قرآنا) is a second mafʿūl bihi; (أعجميا) is a naʿt; the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e. "why not"; (فصلت) is a passive past verb and (آياته) its nāʾib fāʿil, the meaning being "made clear [Translator's note: the source prints «بنيت», 'built'; evidently «بُيّنت», 'made clear', is intended] in a language that we understand and comprehend". (أأعجمي): the hamza is for the interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and (أعجمي) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Is it — i.e. the Qur'an — non-Arabic, while the one sent with it is Arab?" There are readings in it: with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) of the second hamza, and with a lengthened alif before it; and it is read with a single hamza and fatḥa on the ʿayn, as a relation to ʿajam. It is also permissible to parse (أأعجمي) as a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, its implied form being "Are a non-Arabic [Qur'an] and an Arab [messenger] equal?"
(قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدىً وَشِفاءٌ): (قل) is an imperative verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "you", i.e. say in reply to them; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (للذين آمنوا) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective and was fronted; and (هدى وشفاء) is the khabar of (هو), i.e. it guides them, heals what is in their breasts and suffices in warding off doubts; for this reason it came as an inimitable miracle in their language. A full treatment of this subject will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى أُولئِكَ يُنادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ): (والذين): the wāw is conjunctive and (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the ṣila, the referent being omitted, i.e. "in it"; (في آذانهم) is a fronted khabar; (وقر) is a delayed mubtadaʾ, and a link must be implied, i.e. "from it"; and the clause is the khabar of (الذين). (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (عليهم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl and is not attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) because it precedes it; (عمى) is a delayed mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; with (هو) as mubtadaʾ, (عمى) would be its khabar]. (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (ينادون) is the khabar; (من مكان) is attached to (ينادون); and (بعيد) is a naʿt of (مكان). The meaning of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṭibāq (antithesis):
«أأعجمي وعربي» is a fine ṭibāq that admits two meanings. The first: the denial falls on the Qur'an being non-Arabic while the Messenger is Arab. The second: the Qur'an being non-Arabic while those to whom it is sent, or the one to whom it is sent, are Arab. It came in the singular, although those to whom it was sent are the nation of the Arabs, only because the denial is built on the incongruity between the two states of the Book and its addressee, not on whether the addressee is one or a group; so it had to be stripped down to the purpose it was aimed at, and nothing joined to it that would disturb that with another purpose. Do you not see that, having seen a long garment on a short woman, you say: "The garment is long and the wearer (al-lābis) is short"? If you said "and the wearer (al-lābisa, feminine) is short", you would have produced something faulty and superfluous speech, because the statement is not about the masculinity or femininity of the wearer but about a purpose beyond both. So the ṭibāq is sound.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh):
In His saying «قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء» there is an eloquent simile: He made the Qur'an guidance itself and healing itself, guiding them to the paths of right conduct and healing them of the ailments of madness and confusion.
3- The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): In His saying «أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد» there is a representational metaphor: their state in shying away from accepting the admonitions and proofs of the Qur'an is likened to the state of one who is called from a distant place. Just as he does not understand or accept the words of the caller, so these do not accept the call of one who calls them to right guidance and righteousness, because misguidance has taken hold of them.

dervis-irab:45-48.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَكْمامِها): plural of kimm, with kasra on the kāf, which is the container of the fruit, or what is technically called the calyx (al-kaʾs). In al-Kashshāf: "Al-kimm, with kasra on the kāf, is the container of the fruit." But al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt: "Al-kumm is what covers the hand of the shirt, and what covers the fruit; its plural is akmām." So al-Rāghib's words indicate the form with ḍamma on the kāf, since he made it shared between the sleeve of the shirt and the sheath of the fruit; and there is no dispute that the sleeve of the shirt has ḍamma. So perhaps in the container of the fruit there are two dialectal forms, unlike the sleeve of the shirt — this reconciles al-Zamakhsharī's statement and al-Rāghib's. As for the dictionaries, they distinguish between the kumm of a garment and the kimm of fruit, explicitly stating ḍamma for the first and kasra for the second. In al-Qāmūs he said: "Al-kumm, with ḍamma, is the entry and exit of the hand from the garment; the plural is akmām and kimama. With kasra, it is the container of the spathe (al-ṭalʿ) and the covering of the blossom, like al-kimāma and al-kimma, with kasra in both; the plural is akimma, akmām and kimām." From al-Asās and other major dictionaries the following is taken, for you to reflect upon:
Al-kumm, with ḍamma on the kāf, is the entry and exit of the hand from the garment; its plural is akmām and kimama, with kasra on the kāf. Al-kumma, with ḍamma on the kāf, is the round cap, and any receptacle with which you cover a thing and clothe it, so that it becomes like a sheath for it.
Al-kimm, with kasra on the kāf, is the sheath that surrounds the blossom, the fruit or the spathe and covers it, and then splits open from it; its plural is akimma, akmām, kimām and akāmīm. From that come akmām al-zarʿ, i.e. the sheaths of the crops out of which they emerge.
Akimmat al-khayl: their nosebags hung on their heads; the singular of them is kimām. Al-kimāma, with kasra on the kāf, is the covering of the blossom and the container of the spathe; and al-kimāma, also with kasra, and al-kimāl [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently al-kimām is intended] is that with which an animal's mouth is muzzled so that it does not bite or eat — to the end of this lengthy entry.
(مَحِيصٍ): a place of escape, from ḥāṣa, yaḥīṣu, ḥayṣan, when he fled.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ فَاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to explain that disagreement about the revealed Books is not an innovation, for it is old among the nations. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (آتينا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (موسى) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (الكتاب) the second; the fāʾ is conjunctive; (اختلف) is a passive past verb with a latent (mustatir) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (فيه) is attached to (اختلف).
(وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مُرِيبٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence because of existence; (كلمة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause (سبقت) is a naʿt (adjective) of (كلمة); (من ربك) is attached to (سبقت); the lām occurs in the answer of (لولا); (قضي) is a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil latent, referring back to the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from (قضي), i.e. "the judgement"; (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (قضي), and the pronoun in (بينهم) refers back to the disbelievers among his people. (وإنهم): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (في شك) is the khabar of (إن); (منه) is attached to an omitted naʿt; and (مريب) is a second naʿt.
(مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها وَما رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ): (من) is a jussive conditional noun and the mubtadaʾ; (عمل) is a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (صالحا) is a mafʿūl bihi or a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar — parallels of it have preceded; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (لنفسه) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "it benefits" or "he did [it]"; it may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then the righteous deed is for himself". (ومن أساء فعليها) is conjoined to what preceded and its i'rab is parallel to it. The wāw may validly be circumstantial or conjunctive; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (mā); (ربك) is its noun; (بظلام): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (ظلام) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar of (ما); and (للعبيد) is attached to (ظلام). (ظلام) may validly be a form of relation (nisba), like tammār (date-seller), baqqāl (grocer) and khabbāz (baker), as its details will come in the section on benefits; and it may validly be a form of intensification. On the first, its meaning is "not one possessed of injustice", and more than one of the grammarians preferred it. (إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ): (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يرد); (يرد) is a passive imperfect verb; and (علم الساعة) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
(وَما تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَراتٍ مِنْ أَكْمامِها وَما تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنْثى وَلا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negating; (تخرج) is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb; (من) is a redundant preposition, and (ثمرة) [Translator's note: so in the source, in the singular, though the text heading has (ثمرات)] is genitive by (من) in form, in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of (تخرج); (من أكمامها) is attached to (تخرج); and it has been read (من ثمرات). It has also been said that (ما) is relative, in the position of genitive, conjoined to (الساعة), i.e. "the knowledge of the Hour and the knowledge of what comes out". The first (من) is for comprehensiveness (istighrāq) and the second (من) for the beginning of the extent. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (تضع) is a nominative imperfect verb [Translator's note: the source passes over (تحمل) here and parses (تضع) with (من أنثى), though in the verse (من أنثى) follows (تحمل)]; (من) is a redundant preposition; (أنثى) is genitive in form, in the position of nominative as the fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (بعلمه) is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of states, i.e. "except accompanied by His knowledge". (وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِي قالُوا آذَنَّاكَ ما مِنَّا مِنْ شَهِيدٍ): the adverb is attached to an omitted "remember", so it is a mafʿūl bihi; or it is an adverb of an implied element that explanation falls short of. The clause (يناديهم) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (شركائي) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (آذناك) is a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "We inform You now". The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "This verb is transitive to one object by itself and to another by a preposition, and the negation and what is in its khabar has occurred in the place of the preposition and its genitive noun. Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at (آنذاك) [Translator's note: so in the source; (آذناك) is meant], then begins anew, so the negation has no position." (ما) is negating; (منا) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (شهيد) is genitive in form, in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ.
(وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ضل) is a past verb; (عنهم) is attached to (ضل); (ما) is the fāʿil; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (كان) and its noun; the clause (يدعون) is the khabar of (كانوا); and (من قبل) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَظَنُّوا ما لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ظنوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (ما) is negating; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (محيص) is genitive in form, in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ. The negation suspends (taʿlīq) the operation of the supposing verb in form while it remains [operative] in position, and the negative clause has taken the place of the two objects of (آذناك) [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires "of (ظنوا)"], because it means "We informed You", just as the preceding negative clause took the place of the second object of (آذناك). The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "As for the saying of Allah the Exalted (وظنوا), its two objects have been dispensed with by (ما لهم من محيص). Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at (ظنوا), then He informs about them with the negation."

* Benefits:
Relation (nisba) on the patterns faʿʿāl and fāʿil:
Know that the Arabs formed relation by a path other than the well-known method of nisba, in that they did not bring the yāʾ of relation but built a form that indicates something like what the yāʾ of relation indicates. Examples are their saying, for the owner of butūt — which are cloaks, singular batt —:
battāt; for the owner of clothes: thawwāb; for the owner of fabric (bazz): bazzāz; for the owner of ivory: ʿawwāj; for the owner of camels on which he transports: jammāl; for the owner of donkeys on which he transports: ḥammār; and for the money-changer: ṣarrāf. It is too many to count, such as al-ʿaṭṭār (perfumer) and al-naqqāsh (engraver). They apply this pattern only to what is a craft and a practice, for multiplicity, since the practitioner of a craft persists in his craft; so the form indicating multiplicity was given to him, namely faʿʿāl with doubling of the ʿayn, because doubling is for multiplicity. Whatever of this is "possessor of a thing" and is not a craft that he practises, they brought on the form fāʿil; that is because fāʿil is the base, and it is departed from to faʿʿāl only for intensification; so when intensification is not intended, it is brought on the base, since there is no multiplicity in it. They said for the possessor of a coat of mail: dāriʿ; for the possessor of arrows (nabl): nābil; for the possessor of nushshāb arrows:
nāshib; for the possessor of milk: lābin; and for the possessor of dates: tāmir. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
وغررتني وزعمت أنّك لابن بالصيف تامر
(You deceived me and claimed that you were a man of milk and dates in summer) — i.e. possessor of milk and possessor of dates. If any of these things is a craft, or what resembles it [Translator's note: the source prints «وما شا», apparently garbled; «وما شابهها», "or what resembles it", seems intended], which its practitioner persists in, the relation is formed on faʿʿāl; so one says, of one who sells milk and dates:
labbān and tammār; and of one who shoots arrows: nabbāl. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
وليس بذي رمح فيطعنني به ... وليس بذي سيف وليس بنبال
(He is not a possessor of a spear to pierce me with it, nor a possessor of a sword, nor an archer.)
Sometimes they combined the two words in one thing; al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
دع المكارم لا ترحل لبغيتها ... واقعد فإنك أنت الطّاعم الكاسي
(Leave noble deeds, do not set out in pursuit of them, and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed.)
What is meant is "the one fed, the one clothed". Although this category is plentiful and wide, it is not by analogy (qiyās); rather it is restricted to what is heard (samāʿ). So one does not say, for a seller of wheat (burr): barrār;
nor for the owner of fruit: fakkāh. Many of the meticulous scholars interpreted on this basis, as Ibn Mālik said, «وما ربك بظلام للعبيد», i.e. "possessed of injustice". What led them to that is that [otherwise] the negation would be directed at the intensification, so that the root of the action would be affirmed, and Allah the Exalted is far above that.
[Volume Nine]
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
[Continuation of Sūrat Fuṣṣilat]

dervis-irab:49-54.t:
* I'rab:
(لا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسانُ مِنْ دُعاءِ الْخَيْرِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, to begin describing man in his two states of hardship and ease. (لا) is negating; (يسأم الإنسان) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); and (من دعاء الخير) is attached to (يسأم). (وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَيَؤُسٌ قَنُوطٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional; (مسه) is a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الشر) is the fāʿil; the fāʾ links the answer; (يئوس) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then he is despairing"; and (قنوط) is a second khabar. The difference between al-yaʾs and al-qunūṭ — both meaning the cutting off of hope of mercy — is that yaʾs is of the [states] of the heart [Translator's note: the source prints «منعات القلب», apparently a misprint for «من صفات القلب», "of the attributes of the heart"], while qunūṭ is the appearance of its traces on the outward body. It has also been said that they are synonyms without any difference between them. In al-Mukhtār: "Al-yaʾs is al-qunūṭ. Yaʾisa min al-shayʾ, of the pattern fahima; and there is another dialectal form in it, yaʾisa, yayʾisu, with kasra in both, which is anomalous (shādhdh); and a man is yaʾūs. Yaʾisa also means ʿalima (he knew) in the dialect of al-Nakhaʿ, and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted (أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا). And āyasahu Allāhu min kadhā fa-stayʾasa minhu, in the sense of ayisa." Also in al-Mukhtār: "Ayisa minhu is a dialectal form of yaʾisa, and the pattern of both is fahima; and someone else āyasahu minhu, with the madd, like ayʾasahu; likewise ayyasahu, with doubling of the yāʾ, taʾyīsan." Also in it: "Al-qunūṭ is despair (al-yaʾs); its patterns are jalasa, dakhala, ṭariba and salima; so he is qaniṭ, qanūṭ and qāniṭ. As for qanaṭa, yaqnaṭu, with fatḥa in both, and qaniṭa, yaqniṭu, with kasra in both, that is only by combining the two dialectal forms." The wording of al-Kashshāf: "(فيئوس قنوط): it is intensified in two ways, by way of the faʿūl pattern and by way of repetition. Al-qunūṭ is that the trace of despair appears on him, so he shrinks and breaks, i.e. he cuts off hope of the bounty of Allah and His relief. This is a description of the disbeliever, by the evidence of the saying of Allah the Exalted (إِنَّهُ لا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكافِرُونَ)." (وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هذا لِي): the wāw is conjunctive; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (أذقناه) is a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the protasis; (رحمة) is a second mafʿūl bihi; (من بعد) is a naʿt (adjective) of (رحمة) or attached to (أذقناه); (ضراء) is a muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct), made genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote on account of the lengthened feminine alif. The lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath takes its place, according to the well-known rule. (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ and (لي) the khabar, the lām being for entitlement, i.e. "I deserve it by my work". (وَما أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إِلى رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنى): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negating; (أظن) is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil; (الساعة) is the first object of (أظن) and (قائمة) its second object. The wāw is conjunctive; the lām prepares for the oath; (إن) is conditional; (رجعت) is in the position of jussive as the condition; (إلى ربي) is attached to (رجعت); (إن) and what falls within its scope is the answer to the oath; (لي) is the khabar of (إن); (عنده) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (الحسنى) is the noun of (إن). The clause (إن لي عنده للحسنى) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath, since the oath precedes the condition. (فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِما عَمِلُوا وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ): the faṣīḥa fāʾ, because it is an answer to the disbeliever's saying (ولئن رجعت). The lām prepares for the oath [Translator's note: so in the source; this lām is more usually identified as the lām of the answer to an implied oath]; (ننبئن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; (الذين) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (بما) is in the position of accusative as the second object of (ننبئن), and (ما) may be relative or maṣdariyya (infinitival); (لنذيقنهم) is conjoined to (فلننبئن); (من عذاب) is in the position of the second object; and (غليظ) is a naʿt. (وَإِذا أَنْعَمْنا عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأى بِجانِبِهِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause (أنعمنا) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (على الإنسان) is attached to (أنعمنا); the clause (أعرض) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (نأى بجانبه) is conjoined to (أعرض); and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (نأى) because the lām [Translator's note: so in the source; the preposition here is the bāʾ] is for making transitive. Below is the text of al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this expression; he said:
"If you say: Establish for me the meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted (ونأى بجانبه), I say: There are two aspects in it. [The first] is that 'his side' is put in the place of 'himself', as we mentioned regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted «على ما فرطت في جنب الله», that the place of a thing and its direction are treated as the thing itself; and from it is the poet's saying:
ذعرت به القطا ونفيت عنه ... مقام الذئب كالرجل اللعين
(I startled the sandgrouse there and drove from it the standing-place of the wolf, like the scarecrow.)
— he means 'and I drove the wolf from it'; and from it is «ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان»" — until he says: "So it is as though He said 'and he withdrew himself', like their saying of the arrogant man 'he went off with himself' and 'conceit carried him off in every direction' and 'conceit swept him away'. [The second] is that by 'his side' is meant his flank, and it is an expression for turning away and swerving aside, as they said: 'he turned his flank and turned away with his side.'" [Translator's note: the source does not mark where al-Zamakhsharī's quotation ends; it appears to end here.] In one reading it is (وناء بجانبه), with the hamza placed after the alif. (وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause (مسه الشر) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. (فذو): the fāʾ is linking, and (ذو دعاء) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and (عريض) is a naʿt of (دعاء). The meaning of this adjective will come in the section on rhetoric. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ مَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ هُوَ فِي شِقاقٍ بَعِيدٍ): (أرأيتم), i.e. "tell me about your strange state"; what is to be said about (أرأيتم) has preceded. The first object of (رأى) is omitted, its implied form being "Have you considered yourselves", and the second is the interrogative clause. (إن) is conditional; (كان) is the protasis and its noun is latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. the Qur'an; (من عند الله) is the khabar; (ثم كفرتم) is conjoined to (كان من عند الله); the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then you are more astray than others" or "there is no one more astray than you"; and the conditional clause is parenthetical between the first and second objects. (من) is an interrogative noun and the mubtadaʾ; (أضل) is the khabar; (ممن) is attached to (أضل); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (في شقاق بعيد) the khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ): the sīn is for the future; (نريهم) is an imperfect verb and the first mafʿūl bihi; (آياتنا) is the second mafʿūl bihi; the seeing here is visual, and for that reason it was made transitive to two only; (في الآفاق) is a ḥāl from (الآيات). Al-āfāq is the plural of ufuq, which is the region; it is like aʿnāq from ʿunuq, its hamza changed into an alif. Al-Rāghib transmitted: "One says afaq, with fatḥa on the hamza and the fāʾ, so it is like jabal and ajbāl; and al-afaq is the one who has reached the utmost of generosity, likened in that to one who goes into the horizons. The relation (nisba) to al-ufuq is afaqī, with fatḥa on both. I say: it is possible that it is a relation to the form with fatḥa, and they dispensed with that from forming the relation to the form with ḍamma; and it has parallels." [Translator's note: the source places "I say…" inside al-Rāghib's quotation; it may be the author's or a later commentator's remark.] (وفي أنفسهم) is conjoined to (في الآفاق). (حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ): (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (يتبين) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after (حتى); (حتى) and what follows it is attached to His saying (سنريهم); and (أن) and what falls within its scope is the fāʿil of (تبين). (أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): the hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī); the wāw is a conjunction joining to an implied element that the context requires, i.e. "Has it not sufficed them and not been enough for them"; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (ربك) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the mafʿūl bihi being omitted, i.e. "Has your Lord not sufficed you?"; and (أن) and what falls within its scope is a badal (substitute) from (ربك), so it is nominative in position and genitive in form. It has also been said that the bāʾ is added to the object and that (أن) and what follows it is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil, i.e. "Has His witnessing not sufficed regarding your Lord?" (أن) and its noun; (شهيد) is its khabar; and (على كل شيء) is attached to (شهيد). (أَلا إِنَّهُمْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ أَلا إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطٌ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «فذو دعاء عريض» there is an implicit, imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya): breadth, which is one of the attributes of bodies, has been borrowed for the abundance and persistence of supplication. Length is also borrowed for it, but borrowing breadth is more eloquent, because if its breadth is like that, what do you think of its length? Supplication is likened to something described as extended, and then breadth is affirmed of it; and length is the longer of the two extensions, so if its breadth is of this degree, how much more its length!

* Benefits:
Al-rajul al-laʿīn (the scarecrow): something set up in the middle of crops to frighten the birds. The verse is by al-Shammākh, and before it is:
وماء قد وردت لأجل أروى ... عليه الطير كالورق اللجين
(Many a water I have come to for the sake of Arwā, with birds over it like crushed fallen leaves.)
ذعرت به القطا — the verse.
Arwā is the name of the poet's beloved. Al-lajīn, with fatḥa on the lām and kasra on the jīm, is the leaves that fall, from al-lajn, which is pounding, because the wind or the shepherd strikes it and it falls from the tree. Dhaʿartu, with two fatḥas, i.e. I frightened the sandgrouse there; he singled them out because they are the earliest of birds to the water. Al-rajul al-laʿīn is the figure that is set up in the middle of crops to drive birds and vermin away from it. He says: Many a water I have come to for the sake of my beloved, in the hope that she would come to it and I would see her. He likened the birds around the water to the falling leaves of trees in dusky colour, abundance and scattering. (كالرجل اللعين) is a ḥāl from the poet's pronoun, so it conveys that he preceded the sandgrouse and the wolf and sat there; or it is a ḥāl from the wolf, i.e. in a frightening form. In it there is evidence of the poet's courage and daring.

dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(حم، تَنْزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ): حم is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and تنزيل is likewise the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a sending down"; من الرحمن الرحيم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنزيل. Al-Zajjāj allowed تنزيل to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is His coming saying كتاب, beginning with تنزيل being permitted because it has been specified by the description; al-Jalāl [al-Suyūṭī] and his commentators followed this. What we mentioned first is preferable.
(كِتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ): كتاب is a badal (substitute) of تنزيل, or a khabar after a khabar; the clause فصلت آياته is a naʿt (adjective) of the book, i.e. "distinguished and made into details in various meanings"; آياته is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); قرآنا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of كتاب, and عربيا a naʿt. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed قرآنا to be parsed as accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). لقوم is attached to فصلت, and the clause يعلمون is a naʿt of قوم. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed لقوم by saying: «The better view is that it is a description, like what precedes it».
(بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً فَأَعْرَضَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ فَهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُونَ): [بشيرا and نذيرا] may be two naʿts of قرآنا, or two ḥāls, either of كتاب, or of آياته, or of the pronoun intended in قرآنا. فأعرض: the fāʾ conjoins to فصلت, and أكثرهم is the fāʿil (agent). فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا يسمعون is its khabar.
(وَقالُوا: قُلُوبُنا فِي أَكِنَّةٍ مِمَّا تَدْعُونا إِلَيْهِ وَفِي آذانِنا وَقْرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; قلوبنا is a mubtadaʾ and في أكنة a khabar, i.e. "coverings"; مما is attached to something omitted, i.e. "that prevent us from what you call us to". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It is construed according to the sense, since the meaning of في أكنة is that they are screened from hearing what you call us to; it cannot be a naʿt of أكنة, because الأكنة are coverings, and coverings are not among what he calls to». This is a general statement that does not specify the i'rab; for that reason we inclined to the implied form تمنعنا ("that prevent us"). Close to the view we chose is the saying of Zādah in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: «There is an omission in the expression, its implied form being "in coverings that prevent us from understanding what you call us to"; so the muḍāf was omitted». So what مما is attached to is the naʿt of أكنة. The wāw is a conjunction; في آذاننا is a fronted khabar and وقر a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(وَمِنْ بَيْنِنا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجابٌ فَاعْمَلْ إِنَّنا عامِلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; من بيننا is a fronted khabar; بينك is conjoined to بيننا; حجاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ. فاعمل: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you have understood what we told you and grasped it, then act"; إننا is إنّ and its noun, and عاملون is its khabar, i.e. "so continue in your call, for we are continuing in our religion", which is associating partners [with Allah]. A fuller exposition of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric.
(قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ يُوحى إِلَيَّ أَنَّما إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ): إنما is a restraining particle with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنا is a mubtadaʾ and بشر a khabar; مثلكم is a naʿt; the clause يوحى is a second naʿt of بشر; إلي is attached to يوحى; the nāʾib fāʿil is أن and what follows it: أنما is kāffa wa-makfūfa, and together with what it governs it is the nāʾib fāʿil of يوحى; إلهكم is a mubtadaʾ, إله a khabar and واحد a naʿt.
(فَاسْتَقِيمُوا إِلَيْهِ وَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ وَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; استقيموا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and it contains the sense of "turn (towards)", which is why it is made transitive with إلى; استغفروه is conjoined to فاستقيموا. وويل: the wāw is a conjunction, and ويل is a mubtadaʾ, permitted to begin the sentence because of the sense of imprecation in it; للمشركين is the khabar; الذين is a naʿt; and the clause لا يؤتون الزكاة is the ṣila (relative clause). Conjoining the nominal clause to the verbal one is not incongruous, because the first is renewed — namely not giving zakāt — and the second is continuous — namely disbelief.
(وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ كافِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ; بالآخرة is attached to كافرون [Translator's note: the source has «متعلقان بهم», evidently a misprint for «بكافرون»]; the second هم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first; and كافرون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The verse «وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة» up to His saying «عاملون» contains rhetorical subtleties that deserve to be written in molten gold. In it there are three representational metaphors (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) for their hearts' aversion to perceiving and believing what he calls them to, their ears' spitting it out, and the impossibility of their connecting with and agreeing with the Messenger [Translator's note: the source repeats «وامتناع مواصلتهم» twice].
1- The first of them is the external intervening screen: they likened their hearts to something enclosed, surrounded by a covering that encompasses it.
2- The second is the screen of deafness: they likened their hearing to ears that have deafness, in that they spit out the truth and do not incline to listen to it.
3- The third, and the furthest of them, is the screen that has enveloped the heart — Allah's refuge is sought. They likened their own state with the Messenger to the state of two things between which is a mighty screen preventing either from reaching the other; so the intervening distance between our side and your side is entirely filled by the screen, with no gap in it. So this verse leaves no loose screen without letting it down, and leaves these wretched ones no hope and no helper without seizing it.
Moreover, attention must be drawn to the indications [of من] that it contains: it conveys beginning, and the meaning is that a screen began from us and began from you. As for بين, it has been repeated while its meaning is one. Al-Zamakhsharī erred in making the second بين other than the first, for he made the first on their side and the second on his side. The matter is not as he thought; rather, the first بين is the very same as the second: it expresses the side lying between the two things it is annexed to, and it was repeated only because the conjoined item is a pronoun that must be held, so its holder, which is بين, had to be repeated. The proof of this is that there is no difference between saying "I sat بين Zayd and ʿAmr" and saying "I sat بين Zayd and بين ʿAmr"; mentioning it [again] with an overt noun is only permissible, and with a pronoun obligatory, for the reason we have explained. When this has become clear, the place of من here is like its place in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا»; that is to indicate that the intervening side between them and the Prophet ﷺ, for instance, is the starting point of the screen.

* Benefits:
Withholding zakāt and its secret:
The commentators have all asked: why did the Exalted single out, among the traits of the polytheists, the withholding of zakāt, coupled with disbelief in the Hereafter? They answered with similar questions [Translator's note: so in the source, «بأسئلة»; "answers" is evidently meant], whose gist is that the dearest thing to a person is his wealth, which is the twin of his soul; so if he spends it in the way of Allah, that is the strongest proof of his steadfastness, his uprightness, the truthfulness of his intention and the purity of his inner self. The text of al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this point: «Do you not see His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضاة الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم", i.e. they make themselves firm and show their firmness by spending wealth». Moreover, if we review the meaning of the name zakāt, we find it points to the loftiest and highest qualities: it purifies wealth from impurity and cleanses it from blights, keeps the soul away from the vice of miserliness and raises it in the virtue of generosity; blessing is drawn down by it, and it increases the giver in praise and commendation. Whoever denies it is a disbeliever; those who refuse to pay it are fought, and it is taken from them by force even if they are not fought. From Anas ibn Mālik, who said: «A man from Tamīm came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am a man of much wealth, of family, wealth and a settled household; so tell me how I should act and how I should spend. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: You should pay the zakāt from your wealth, for it is a purification that purifies you; and you should keep ties with your relatives, and recognise the right of the poor, the neighbour and the beggar».

dervis-irab:8-12.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ): a resumptive statement brought to mention what has been prepared for the righteous after mentioning what has been prepared for the ignorant. إنّ and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); عملوا is conjoined to آمنوا; الصالحات is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with kasra; لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and أجر a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); غير ممنون is a naʿt (adjective); and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ. The meaning of غير ممنون is "not cut off"; and it has been said: "not held over them as a favour (mamnūn bihi)".
(قُلْ أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause تكفرون is the khabar of إنّ; بالذي is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكفرون; the clause خلق الأرض is the ṣila; and في يومين is attached to خلق. What is meant is the measure of two days, or in two turns, each turn quicker than what occurs in a day.
(وَتَجْعَلُونَ لَهُ أَنْداداً ذلِكَ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; تجعلون is conjoined to تكفرون; له is in the position of the accusative as the second object of تجعلون, and أندادا its first object; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to الذي in view of His being qualified by what the ṣila indicates; and رب العالمين is its khabar.
(وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ مِنْ فَوْقِها وَبارَكَ فِيها): the wāw is a conjunction, according to the most correct view. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others rejected the conjunction; he said: «وجعل فيها is resumptive, not conjoined to خلق, because if it were conjoined to it, it would fall within the ṣila, and that is not permissible, because He separated them by His saying, exalted is He, وتجعلون… to the end of the verse, which is in no way part of the ṣila». This can be answered by saying that His saying وتجعلون, even though it is conjoined to تكفرون, is like a parenthesis between the two conjoined items, and a parenthesis often comes between them. So the truth about which there is no doubt is that it is conjoined to خلق الأرض and is part of the ṣila. فيها is in the position of the second object, and رواسي is the first object of جعل; or you may attach the preposition and its genitive noun to جعل, taking it in the sense of "created", so that it takes a single object. من فوقها is a naʿt of رواسي — and how beautiful is the placement of this naʿt, lest it be imagined that they are beneath it, holding it and preventing it from swaying; and further, so that the mountains are displayed to the onlookers in such a way that they and the earth need someone to hold them. وبارك فيها is conjoined to جعل فيها.
(وَقَدَّرَ فِيها أَقْواتَها فِي أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ سَواءً لِلسَّائِلِينَ): وقدر فيها is conjoined to what precedes, i.e. the provisions and livelihoods of its inhabitants; في أربعة أيام is attached to قدر, i.e. "in the completion and measure of four days"; سواء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "the four days were equal, an equality neither more nor less". It has been read in the genitive as a description, and in the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. للسائلين is attached to سواء, meaning "equal for those who ask"; or to something omitted, as if it were said: "this delimitation is for the sake of whoever asks in how many days the earth and what is in it were created"; or attached to an implied [verb], i.e. "He measured out in it its provisions for the sake of those who seek them and need them among those who are fed". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed سواء to be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: the source has «حلا», a misprint for «حالا»], after mentioning the preceding views; and it is permissible, as a ḥāl of the pronoun in أقواتها, or in فيها, or of الأرض.
(ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إِلَى السَّماءِ وَهِيَ دُخانٌ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence in narration, not in time; استوى is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; إلى السماء is attached to استوى, from your saying استوى إلى مكان كذا, when he made for it and turned towards it directly, not turning aside to anything. The wāw is circumstantial (of ḥāl); هي is a mubtadaʾ and دخان a khabar. The meaning of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَقالَ لَها وَلِلْأَرْضِ ائْتِيا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً قالَتا أَتَيْنا طائِعِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted; لها is attached to قال; للأرض is conjoined to لها; ائتيا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil; طوعا and كرها are two maṣdars in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. "willing or unwilling". Further discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَقَضاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ وَأَوْحى فِي كُلِّ سَماءٍ أَمْرَها): the fāʾ is a conjunction; قضاهن is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; سبع سموات is the second object of قضاهن, because it has been made to include the sense of صيّر ("made into"). It may be accusative as a ḥāl of the object of قضاهن, قضى then meaning "made", i.e. "numbered [seven]"; it may be accusative as a badal (substitute) of the pronoun; and it may be a tamyīz (specification), to which al-Zamakhsharī inclined; he said: «It may be a vague pronoun explained by سبع سنوات [Translator's note: so in the source; سبع سموات is meant] as a tamyīz». By his saying "vague" al-Zamakhsharī means that it does not refer back to السماء, neither in wording nor in meaning, unlike its being a ḥāl or a second object. أوحى is conjoined to فقضاهن; في كل سماء is attached to أوحى; and أمرها is a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَزَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِمَصابِيحَ وَحِفْظاً ذلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ): زينا is conjoined to what precedes by way of a shift of person (iltifāt), as will come in the section on rhetoric. زينا is a verb and its fāʿil; السماء is a mafʿūl bihi and الدنيا a naʿt; بمصابيح is attached to زينا, i.e. "with stars"; حفظا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding" from the devils' eavesdropping, by means of the shooting stars. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) according to the sense, as if He had said: "and We created the lamps as adornment and as a guard". ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to all that has been mentioned with its details; and تقدير العزيز العليم is a muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; تقدير is the khabar and العزيز العليم the muḍāf ilayhi and its naʿt].

* Rhetoric:
1- The eloquent pictorial simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh al-ṣūrī):
In His saying «ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان» there is an eloquent pictorial simile, because its form was the form of smoke to the eye's view. What is meant by smoke is the vapour from which the atmospheric layers are formed, so there is no conflict with the most recent scientific theories.
2- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
In His saying «استوى إلى السماء» there is an implicit metaphor: the thing borrowed is the "rising/turning directly" (al-istiwāʾ); what it is borrowed from is every body that is level; and what it is borrowed for is the Real, Mighty and Majestic. The details of this metaphor have preceded many times, so reflect on it.
3- In His saying «فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين» there are various devices, which we summarise as follows:
a- Attributing speech to the earth and the sky and directing the address to them belongs to rational figurative usage (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī). The aim of this figure is to depict His power, glory be to Him, and the impossibility of their refusing it — not to affirm willingness or unwillingness of them. It may also belong to the implicit metaphor: He likened them to two living [Translator's note: the source has «حين», evidently a misprint for «حيين»], rational beings, then omitted the thing likened to and affirmed something of its concomitants, to represent them by the command of one obeyed and the response of one obeying — just as you say "the state spoke (naṭaqat) of such-and-such" instead of "indicated", making the state like a person who speaks in indicating and proving; then speech, which is a concomitant of the thing likened to, is imagined for it and ascribed to it.
b- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq) between طوعا and كرها.
c- Giving precedence to the rational masculine over the feminine (taghlīb), or treating them as being in its rank, in His saying «قالتا أتينا طائعين».
4- The shift of person (al-iltifāt):
In His saying «وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح» (the verse) there is a shift from the third person to the first person: He ascribed the adorning to Himself, glory be to Him, to bring out greater care for the adorning mentioned.

dervis-irab:13-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَرْصَراً): Al-Zamakhsharī said: «الصرصر is the stormy wind that تصرصر, i.e. makes a sound as it blows; and it has been said: the cold wind that burns by the severity of its cold — a reduplication of the form الصر, which is the cold that يصر, i.e. gathers and contracts». In al-Qāmūs: «الصرة, with kasra, is severe cold, or cold, like الصرّ in both senses; and the loudest shouting; and with fatḥa: the severity of distress, of war and of heat … and صرّ يصرّ, of the pattern ضرب, صرّا and صريرا: he made a sound and shouted loudly». Ibn Qutayba said: صرصر may be from الصرّ, which is cold; it may be from صرّ الباب (the creaking of the door); and it may be from الصرة, which is a shout, from which comes «فأقبلت امرأته في صره». Al-Rāghib said: «صرصر: its wording is from الصر, and that goes back to tightening, because of the contraction that is in coldness».
The ṣād with the rāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a word, carries the meaning of intensity, and of appearance and clarity. So صرب: he brought a صربة that contorts the face [Translator's note: the source reads «بضربة تزري الوجه»; the lexicons have «بصربة تزوي الوجه», a sour curdled milk that makes the face pucker], and you say: "May Allah reward with a ضربة [sic] whoever brought us a صربة". صرح بما في نفسه (he declared openly what was in his mind); بنى صرحا وصروحا (he built a lofty palace / palaces); قعد في صرحة داره, i.e. in its courtyard; صرحت الخمرة: the froth left the wine. الصراخ: the cry of one calling for help, and the cry of the helper when he goes out with his people to give help. Salāma said:
إنا إذا ما أتانا صارخ فزع ... كان الصراخ له قرع الظنابيب
(When a terrified caller for help comes to us, the answer to his cry is the striking of shins [i.e. swift readiness].)
i.e. the help for him was [that]. And: هذا يوم صرد وصرد, يوم صرد, قد صرد يومنا, ليلة صردة, رجل صرد, and ريح مصراد: cold, intensely cold. صرعته: I left him felled (صريعا), and I left them felled (صرعى); the vicissitude of fate felled them, and nothing is more severe than that; and he spent the night felled by the cup. Muslim ibn al-Walīd, "the one felled by the fair maidens" (Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī), said:
هل العيش إلا أن أروح مع الصبا ... وأغدو صريع الراح والأعين النجل
(Is life anything but that I go in the evening with youthful passion, and rise in the morning felled by wine and by wide eyes?)
And: may Allah protect you from صرف الزمان, its صروف and its تصاريف (the vicissitudes of time). زرع صريم and مصروم: reaped; صرم النخل and اصطرمه: he cut the dates. ماء صريّ: gathered water.
And it is not gathered except in order to appear. Dhū al-Rumma said:
صرى آجن يزوي له المرء وجهه ... ولو ذاقه ظمآن في شهر ناجر
(Stagnant, brackish standing water, at which a man puckers his face, even if he tasted it thirsty in the hottest month.)
And this is among the rare usages that surpass [other] languages.
(نَحِساتٍ): with kasra on the ḥāʾ and with sukūn — both are readings among the seven — i.e. ill-omened for them. As for the kasra, it is an adjective on the pattern فَعِل, whose verb is فَعِل, also with kasra on the middle radical: one says نحس فهو نحس, like فرح فهو فرح and أشر فهو أشر. As for the sukūn, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, like رجل عدل ("a just man"). But its being pluralised is problematic on this reading, for the eloquent usage with a maṣdar used as a description is to keep it singular; it seems that what permits it is the difference of its kinds in origin.

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا فَقُلْ أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وَثَمُودَ): a resumptive statement by way of a shift of person (iltifāt), brought to warn them after their turning away; the iltifāt has an eloquent secret which we present in the section on rhetoric. إن is conditional; أعرضوا is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the verb is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). فقل: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and قل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; أنذرتكم is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). He expressed it with the past, while the context requires the future, to indicate that the warning is certain. صاعقة is a second mafʿūl bihi, and مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of صاعقة.
(إِذْ جاءَتْهُمُ الرُّسُلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) صاعقة, because it means "punishment"; the clause جاءتهم الرسل is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is annexed to it; من بين أيديهم is attached to جاءتهم, and من خلفهم is conjoined to it, i.e. from all their sides; or from the side of the past time with warning and from the side of the future with caution. Some parsed it as attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الرسل, i.e. while the messengers were before ʿĀd and Thamūd and behind them. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred the first in his explanation of its meaning; he said: «i.e. they came to them from every side, exerted themselves with them, and used every stratagem on them; and you say: I went round so-and-so from every side, but I had no stratagem with him».
(أَنْ لا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ): three views are possible for this أن. The first is that it is lightened from the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its origin being أنه لا تعبدوا, i.e. "with [the statement] that the matter and the account is our saying to you: do not worship"; أن and what falls within its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "saying", which is a ḥāl of الرسل; لا is prohibitive, and تعبدوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the Glorious Name is a mafʿūl bihi. The second view is that it is maṣdariyya, putting the imperfect verb in the accusative: لا is negating, and تعبدوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن after the negating لا, for the negating لا does not prevent the governing word from acting on what follows it. The third view is that it is explicative (mufassira), because the coming of the messengers carries [the sense of] saying, and the clause then has no grammatical position because it is explicative.
(قالُوا لَوْ شاءَ رَبُّنا لَأَنْزَلَ مَلائِكَةً فَإِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ): قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle; شاء ربنا is a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, its implied form being "the sending of messengers". It is better that it be supplied from the kind of its apodosis, i.e. "if our Lord had willed to send down angels with the message to mankind, He would have sent down angels to them with it". The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; إنّ and its noun; بما is attached to كافرون; the clause أرسلتم به is the ṣila (relative clause); and كافرون is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The meaning is: "since you are human beings and not angels, we do not believe in you".
(فَأَمَّا عادٌ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to begin relating what is particular to each of the two. أما is a particle of condition and detailing; عاد is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ links the answer of أما; the clause استكبروا is the khabar of عاد; في الأرض is attached to استكبروا; and بغير الحق is a ḥāl.
(وَقالُوا مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً): قالوا is conjoined to فاستكبروا; من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and أشد its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); منا is attached to أشد; and قوة is a tamyīz (specification).
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the wāw is a conjunction; the clause لم يروا is conjoined to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Were they heedless and did they go astray, and did they not see?"; أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of يروا, because it means knowing; أنّ and its noun; الذي is a naʿt; the clause خلقهم is the ṣila; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أشد a khabar; منهم is attached to أشد; قوة is a tamyīz; and the clause is the khabar of أنّ.
(وَكانُوا بِآياتِنا يَجْحَدُونَ): also conjoined to His saying فاستكبروا; the conjoined clause [أولم يروا] and the implied clause it is conjoined to form a parenthesis. بآياتنا is attached to يجحدون, because it contains the sense of يكفرون.
(فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً فِي أَيَّامٍ نَحِساتٍ لِنُذِيقَهُمْ عَذابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; عليهم is attached to أرسلنا; ريحا is a mafʿūl bihi and صرصرا a naʿt; في أيام is a second naʿt or a ḥāl; نحسات is a naʿt of أيام. لنذيقهم: the lām is causal, and نذيقهم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by أن after the causal lām, the hāʾ being a mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا; عذاب الخزي is a second mafʿūl bihi of نذيقهم, and it is an annexation of the thing described to its description — its details will come in the section on rhetoric; في الحياة is attached to نذيقهم; and الدنيا is a naʿt of الحياة.
(وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَخْزى وَهُمْ لا يُنْصَرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is of inception (ibtidāʾ); عذاب الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ and أخزى a khabar; the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا ينصرون its khabar; ينصرون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
These verses comprise various kinds of rhetoric, which we present as follows:
1- The shift of person (al-iltifāt) in His saying «فإن أعرضوا» (the verse). He first addressed them by His saying «أئنكم», but they paid no heed to His address and did not take in His counsel; so He shifted from the second person to the third person, because they committed the turning away, so nothing remains for Him but to turn away from addressing them, so that the harmony is sound and the wording suits the meaning. This is among the loftiest and most refined kinds of rhetoric — and how many secrets the iltifāt has!
2- Turning from the future imperfect to the past in His saying «فقد أنذرتكم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «فقل أنذرتكم»], to indicate that what He warns them of is a realised matter from which there is no escape.
3- Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī) in His saying «عذاب الخزي»: He annexed the punishment to الخزي, which is humiliation; and humiliation and abasement is originally a description of the one punished, but He inclined to describing the punishment with it for intensification. So it is, as we said in the i'rab, an annexation of the thing described to its description.
4- Verbal correspondence [Translator's note: the source has «المشاركة», evidently a misprint for «المشاكلة»] in His saying «ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى»: this time الخزي was made a khabar, for the sake of mushākala (verbal correspondence), in the manner of the poet's saying:
«قلت اطبخوا لي جبة وقميصا»
(I said: "Cook me a cloak and a shirt.")
The discussion of this device has preceded.
5- In His saying «فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened disbelief to blindness, because the disbeliever strays from the right course and goes along the road aimlessly like the blind man; and He likened faith to guidance, because the believer is guided to the highway of the right course and the level path. Then He omitted the thing likened in both and affirmed the thing it is likened to.
6- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq) between العمى and الهدى, which has preceded.

dervis-irab:17-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُوزَعُونَ): the first of them are held back for the last of them, i.e. their forerunners are made to halt until their followers catch up with them; it points to the sense of great numbers. In the dictionaries:
«وزع يزع, of the pattern فتح, and وزع يزع, of the pattern ضرب, فلانا and بفلان: he restrained him and held him back; وزع الجيش: he held back the first of the army for the last of them; one says "I saw him يزع the army", i.e. arranging them, levelling them and drawing them up in ranks for battle». Mention of this root has preceded.
(يَسْتَعْتِبُوا): they seek العتبى, i.e. pleasure [with them] and being returned to what they love, out of anguish at what they are in.
(قَيَّضْنا): We prepared. The root sense of التقييض is facilitating and preparing; and المقايضة is exchange (barter).

* I'rab:
(وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْناهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمى عَلَى الْهُدى): conjoined to His saying فأما عاد. أما is a particle of condition and detailing; ثمود is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause فهديناهم is the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is a conjunction; استحبوا is conjoined to هديناهم; العمى is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and على الهدى is attached to (mutaʿalliq) استحبوا, because it contains the sense of آثروا ("preferred").
(فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ صاعِقَةُ الْعَذابِ الْهُونِ بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذتهم is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi; صاعقة العذاب is a postponed fāʿil (agent); الهون is a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب, or a badal (substitute) of it; بما is attached to أخذتهم, the bāʾ meaning causation, and ما is relative; the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause); كان and its noun, and the clause يكسبون is its khabar; the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "for what they used to earn" of their associating partners and their denying their prophet Ṣāliḥ.
(وَنَجَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكانُوا يَتَّقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; نجينا is a verb and its fāʿil; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; كانوا is conjoined to آمنوا; كان and its noun, and the clause يتقون is its khabar.
(وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أَعْداءُ اللَّهِ إِلَى النَّارِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; يوم is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "mention the day". Abū al-Baqāʾ made it an adverb for what is indicated by what comes after it, namely the saying of Allah the Exalted «فهم يوزعون», as if He had said "they are held back on the day We gather" — and that is not far-fetched. The clause يحشر is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by annexation; أعداء الله is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلى النار is attached to يحشر; the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يوزعون a khabar.
(حَتَّى إِذا ما جاؤُها شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): حتى is a particle of limit; إذا is an adverb for future time containing the sense of condition, attached to its apodosis, which is شهد; ما is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the testimony — the redundant ما emphasises the meaning of what it is joined to in the relation to which it is attached, and here it has emphasised the adverbial sense of the time fixed for the testimony. The clause جاءوها is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; the clause شهد has no grammatical position; عليهم is attached to شهد; سمعهم is the fāʿil; أبصارهم and جلودهم are conjoined to سمعهم; بما is also attached to شهد; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of ما; and the clause يعملون is the khabar of كان.
(وَقالُوا لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنا): the wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; لجلودهم is attached to قالوا; the lām is a preposition, and ما is an interrogative noun, genitive by ما [Translator's note: so in the source; "genitive by the lām" is meant], and for that reason its alif was dropped; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهدتم; علينا is attached to شهدتم; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The interrogation here is for rebuke and for wonder at this matter.
(قالُوا أَنْطَقَنَا اللَّهُ الَّذِي أَنْطَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ): قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; أنطقنا الله is a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying; الذي is a description of الله; and the clause أنطق كل شيء is the ṣila of الذي.
(وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause خلقكم a khabar; أول مرة is an adverb attached to خلقكم; إليه is attached to ترجعون; and ترجعون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil.
(وَما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُكُمْ وَلا جُلُودُكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes. ما is negating; كنتم is كان and its noun, and the clause تستترون is its khabar; أن and what falls within its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تستترون, i.e. "from [the fear] that … would testify against you", because تستترون is not transitive by itself. It has been said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "because your hearing would testify against you". عليكم is attached to يشهد; سمعكم is the fāʿil; ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم is conjoined to سمعكم. I.e. your concealing yourselves was not out of fear that your limbs would testify against you, for you did not conceive of their testimony; rather you denied the resurrection and the requital altogether.
