(وَلكِنْ ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَعْلَمُ كَثِيراً مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); ظننتم is a verb and its fāʿil; أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of ظننتم; أنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يعلم is its khabar; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; مما is a naʿt of كثير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. تعملونه.
(وَذلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ الَّذِي ظَنَنْتُمْ بِرَبِّكُمْ أَرْداكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ and ظنكم a khabar; الذي ظننتم is a naʿt or a badal; بربكم is attached to ظننتم; the clause أرداكم is a second khabar. ظنكم may also be parsed as a badal of ذلكم; or ظنكم is a khabar and the clause أرداكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial). فأصبحتم is conjoined to أرداكم; أصبح and its noun, and من الخاسرين is its khabar.
(فَإِنْ يَصْبِرُوا فَالنَّارُ مَثْوىً لَهُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; يصبروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); النار is a mubtadaʾ and مثوى a khabar; and لهم is a naʿt of مثوى.
(وَإِنْ يَسْتَعْتِبُوا فَما هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ): conjoined to the preceding clause; ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, هم its noun and من المعتبين its khabar.
(وَقَيَّضْنا لَهُمْ قُرَناءَ فَزَيَّنُوا لَهُمْ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ): a verb and its fāʿil; لهم is attached to قيضنا; قرناء is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. they cling to them and take hold of them as the القيض takes hold of the egg — القيض is the dry upper shell of the egg over the egg, or it is [the shell] from which its contents, chick or fluid, have come out, and their place is المقيض. فزينوا is a verb and its fāʿil; لهم is attached to زينوا; ما is a mafʿūl bihi; the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; أيديهم is a muḍāf ilayhi; and ما خلفهم is conjoined to ما بين أيديهم.
(وَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا خاسِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; حق is a past verb; عليهم is attached to حق; القول is the fāʿil; في أمم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being among the number of nations", or "included [among them]", and it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in عليهم. Like this expression is the saying of ʿUrwa ibn Udhayna:
إن تك عن أحسن الضيعة مأ ... فوكا ففي آخرين قد أفكوا
(If you have been turned away from the finest deed, you are among others who were turned away.)
He says: if you have been مأفوك, i.e. turned away and diverted from the finest giving, it is no wonder, for you are among other people who have been turned away and diverted from doing good. [Translator's note: the source prints «الضيعة»; the verse is usually cited with «الصنيعة», "good deed", which the author's gloss follows.]
The clause قد خلت is a description of أمم; من قبلهم is attached to خلت; من الجن والإنس is a second naʿt of أمم, or a ḥāl because it has been described; إنّ and its noun, and the clause كانوا is its khabar; كان and its noun, and خاسرين is the khabar of كان; and the clause of إنّ with what follows it gives the reason for their deserving the punishment.

* Rhetoric:
Allusion (al-kināya):
In His saying (شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُمْ) there is an allusion to a thing described (kināya ʿan mawṣūf) [Translator's note: the source has «موصوب», a misprint for «موصوف»]: He alluded to the private parts by "skins". It has been said that by "skins" He meant the limbs in general, the conjunction being of the general on the specific, so there would then be no allusion in the expression. So "skins" here is explained both literally and figuratively: literally, skins in general are meant; figuratively, the private parts specifically are meant. This is the rhetorical aspect that gives preference to the figurative over the literal, because of the subtlety of alluding to the thing alluded to.

dervis-irab:26-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْغَوْا فِيهِ): an imperative verb from لغي, with kasra, يلغى, with fatḥa. There are two meanings in it. The first is that it is from لغى when one speaks idle talk (اللغو), which is that in which there is no benefit. The second is that it is from لغي بكذا when one throws it away, so في would then mean the bāʾ, i.e. "throw it away and cast it aside". Or it is from لغى, with fatḥa, يلغى, also with fatḥa — al-Akhfash related it; its analogical form would be with ḍamma, like غزا يغزو, but it took fatḥa because of the guttural letter. It has been read with ḍamma on the ghayn, from لغا يلغو, like دعا يدعو. This is what al-Samīn established. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «والغوا فيه, with fatḥa and ḍamma on the ghayn; one says لغى يلغى and لغا يلغو; and اللغو is the worthless part of speech that has no substance to it».

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ): a resumptive statement brought to establish their state and their obstinacy at the recitation of the Qurʾān. قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); لا is prohibitive, and تسمعوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لهذا is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تسمعوا; القرآن is a badal (substitute); الغوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; فيه is attached to الغوا; لعل and its noun, and the clause تغلبون is its khabar (predicate). What is meant by overcoming is making him fall silent from reciting, lest he captivate hearts and win them over by reciting a kind of eloquence they had not known.
(فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَذاباً شَدِيداً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if they relish that and persist in it, then We shall surely make them taste"; the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); نذيقن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, necessarily emphasised; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "We"; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila; عذابا is a mafʿūl bihi; and شديدا is a naʿt (adjective).
(وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَسْوَأَ الَّذِي كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): conjoined to what precedes; أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون is the second object of نجزينهم.
(ذلِكَ جَزاءُ أَعْداءِ اللَّهِ النَّارُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the two matters mentioned, namely His saying فلنذيقن and His saying ولنجزينهم; جزاء أعداء الله is a khabar; النار is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of جزاء. Some objected to this i'rab that the mark of the badal is the soundness of its taking the place of what it substitutes for, so that the implied form would become "that is the Fire" (ذلك النار), and this is not sound; therefore one should turn from the preferred i'rab to the less preferred one, namely that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar will come below.
(لَهُمْ فِيها دارُ الْخُلْدِ جَزاءً بِما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَجْحَدُونَ): لهم is a fronted khabar; فيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); دار الخلد is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The clause is either the khabar of النار, on parsing it as a mubtadaʾ; or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; or independently resumptive, confirming what precedes it — and this is more firmly seated in the place of eloquence, as will come. جزاء is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an implied verb, and it is an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they are requited with a requital"; or it is accusative by the maṣdar mentioned before it — a maṣdar can put a maṣdar like itself in the accusative, and parallels of it have preceded. You may also make جزاء a maṣdar occurring in the place of the ḥāl. بما is attached to the second جزاء or the first; the clause كانوا is the ṣila; the clause يجحدون is the khabar of كانوا; and بآياتنا is attached to يجحدون because it contains the sense of يكفرون — that is better than making it [the bāʾ] redundant.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّنا أَرِنَا الَّذَيْنِ أَضَلَّانا مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ): the wāw is resumptive; قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause كفروا is the ṣila; ربنا is a vocative in a genitive construct with the vocative particle omitted; أرنا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and نا is a first mafʿūl bihi; اللذين is a second mafʿūl bihi, because the seeing is visual and has been made doubly transitive by the hamza; the clause أضلّانا is the ṣila; and من الجن والإنس is a ḥāl. It has been said that the two are Iblīs and Qābīl: the first established the practice of disbelief, and the second established the practice of killing without right, because he killed his brother, as has preceded.
(نَجْعَلْهُما تَحْتَ أَقْدامِنا لِيَكُونا مِنَ الْأَسْفَلِينَ): نجعلهما is an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; the hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi; تحت أقدامنا: the adverb is in the position of the second object. ليكونا: the lām is causal, and يكونا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; the alif is its noun and من الأسفلين its khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb of seeing, because it gives the reason for it.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), whose working-out has preceded many times.
2- In His saying «لهم فيها دار الخلد» there is abstraction (tajrīd): that is, from a thing of consequence one extracts another thing like it in a certain quality, as an intensification of its perfection in that quality. He extracted from the Fire another abode which He named "the abode of eternity".
The divisions of tajrīd:
Know that tajrīd has divisions which the scholars of rhetoric have mentioned; we shall try to present briefly what they said about them:
1- Among them is that done with the من of tajrīd, as in their saying لي من فلان صديق حميم ("I have in so-and-so a close friend"), i.e. so-and-so has reached such a degree of friendship that one may properly extract from him another like him in it. An example from poetry is the saying of al-Qāḍī al-Fāḍil:
تمد إلى الأعداء منها معاصما ... فترجع من ماء الكلى بأساور
(It stretches out wrists from it towards the enemies, and they come back with bracelets of kidney-blood.)
2- Among them is that done with the bāʾ of tajrīd entering on what is extracted from, e.g. their saying: لئن سألت فلانا لتسألن به البحر ("If you ask so-and-so, you will be asking in him the sea"): he exaggerated his being characterised by liberality to the point of extracting from him a sea of liberality.
3- Among them is that done by the bāʾ of accompaniment entering on what is extracted, as in the saying of Ibn Hāniʾ:
وضربتم هام الكماة ورعتم ... بيض الخدور بكل ليث مخدر
(You struck the heads of armoured warriors and frightened the fair ones in their curtained chambers with every lion in its lair.)
and the saying of Abū Tammām:
هتك الظلام أبو الوليد بغرة ... فتحت لنا باب الرجاء المقبل
بأتم من قمر السماء إذا بدا ... بدرا وأحسن في العيون وأجمل
وأجل من قيس إذا استنطقته ... رأيا وألطف في الأمور وأجزل
(Abū al-Walīd tore through the darkness with a radiant face that opened for us the door of coming hope — with one more complete than the moon of the sky when it appears full, fairer to the eyes and more beautiful; and greater than Qays in judgement when you ask him to speak, subtler in affairs and more abundant.)
What is meant by «بأتم من قمر السماء» is Abū al-Walīd himself, as is obvious.
4- Among them is that done by في entering on what is extracted from, or on its pronoun, as in the verse we are dealing with: «لهم فيها دار الخلد», i.e. in Jahannam, which is the abode of eternity, but He extracted from it another abode for intensification; and the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
تمضي المواكب والأبصار شاخصة ... منها إلى الملك الميمون طائره
قد حرن في بشر في تاجه قمر ... في درعه أسد تدمى أظافره
(The processions pass with eyes fixed upon the king of auspicious fortune; they are bewildered by a man in whose crown is a moon, in whose coat of mail is a lion whose claws drip blood.)
For the lion is the one praised himself, but he extracted from him another lion, to make his affair awesome and to intensify his being characterised by courage.
5- Among them is that done by بين entering, as in the saying of Ibn al-Nabīh:
يهتزّ بين وشاحيها قضيب نقا ... حمائم الحلي في أفنانه صدحت
(Between her two sashes sways a willow-branch of the sand-dune, in whose boughs the doves of jewellery have sung.)
6- Among them is that done without the mediation of anything, as in the saying of Qatāda ibn Salama al-Ḥanafī:
فلئن بقيت لأرحلن بعزة ... تحوي الغنائم أو يموت كريم
(If I survive, I shall surely set out on a raid that gathers the spoils — or a noble man dies.)
By "a noble man" he means himself; it is as if he extracted from himself a noble man, as an intensification of his nobility, and for this reason he did not say "or I die". [Translator's note: the source prints «بعزة»; the verse is usually cited «بغزوة», "on a raid", which is translated here.] And the saying of Abū Tammām:
ولو تراهم وإيانا وموقفنا ... في مأتم البين لاستهلاكنا زجل
من حرقة أطلقتها فرقة أسرت ... قلبا ومن غزل في نحره عذل
وقد طوى الشوق في أحشائنا بقرا ... عينا طوتهن في أحشائها الكلل
(Had you seen them and us, and our standing at the mourning of parting, with the clamour of our raised voices — from a burning released by a separation that took a heart captive, and from a lover in whose throat was reproach; and longing had folded within our entrails wide-eyed wild cows, whom the curtained litters had folded within their insides.)
By "wide-eyed wild cows" he means those of whom he first gave report in his saying «ولو تراهم»; so it is as if he extracted from them ones described by this quality, as an intensification of it.
7- Among them is that a person extracts from himself another person like him in the quality for which the speech is brought, and then addresses him, as in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لا خيل عندك تهديها ولا مال ... فليسعد النطق إن لم تسعد الحال
(You have no horses to give, and no wealth; so let speech be generous, if circumstance is not.)
By الحال he meant wealth; it is as if he extracted from himself another person like him in lacking horses, wealth and means. Among it is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
ودّع هريرة إن الركب مرتحل ... وهل تطيق وداعا أيها الرجل
(Bid farewell to Hurayra, for the riders are departing — but can you bear a farewell, O man?)
and the delightful saying of Abū Nuwās:
يا كثير النوح في الدمن ... لا عليها بل على السكن
سنة العشاق واحدة ... فإذا أحببت فاستنن
(O you who lament much at the ruined campsites — not for them, but for the beloved who dwelt there: the way of lovers is one, so if you love, follow it.)
His intent is addressing himself, and for that reason he said after it:
ظنّ بي من قد كلفت به ... فهو يجفوني على الظّن
بات لا يعنيه ما لقيت ... عين ممنوع من الوسن
رشأ لولا ملاحته ... خلت الدنيا من الفتن
(The one I am infatuated with suspected me, so he shuns me on suspicion; he spent the night unconcerned with what an eye denied sleep endured — a fawn; were it not for his charm, the world would be empty of temptations.)
Another division of tajrīd:
Others divided it into two divisions only: pure tajrīd and impure tajrīd. The first, the pure, is that one produces speech that is an address to someone else while you mean yourself by it, as in the saying of al-Ḥayṣ Bayṣ at the opening of one of his odes:
إلام يراك المجد في زيّ شاعر ... وقد بخلت شوقا فروع المنابر
كتمت بعيب الشعر حلما وحكمة ... ببعضهما ينقاد صعب المفاخر
أما وأبيك الخير انك فارس ... المقال ومحيي الدارسات الغوابر
وأنك أعييت المسامع والنهى ... بقولك عما في بطون الدفاتر
(How long will glory see you in the garb of a poet, while the tops of the pulpits [Translator's note: the source has «بخلت»; perhaps «نحلت», "wasted away"] with longing for you? Through the stigma of poetry you have hidden forbearance and wisdom, by part of which the hardest glories are led. By your good father, you are the knight of discourse and the reviver of the effaced, bygone [lore], and you have wearied ears and minds with your speech about what lies in the bellies of books.)
This is among the beauties of tajrīd: do you not see that he directed the address to another while meaning himself, so that he could mention the surpassing qualities he mentioned and enumerate the matchless virtues he enumerated? Everything that comes of this kind is pure tajrīd.
As for the second division, the impure, it is an address to yourself, not to another. Between this division and the one before it there is an evident difference: that one is more deserving of being called tajrīd, because tajrīd befits it, while this is half a tajrīd, because by it you did not abstract anything from yourself; you only addressed yourself by yourself, as though you had separated it from you while it is part of you. Among what has come of it is the saying of ʿAmr ibn al-Iṭnāba:
أقول لها وقد جشأت وجاشت ... مكانك تحمدي أو تستريحي
(I say to it [my soul], when it surged and heaved: Stay in your place — you will be praised, or you will find rest.)
and the saying of another, whose brother had killed a son of his; his brother was brought to him so that retaliation might be taken from him, but he threw the sword from his hand and began to say:
أقول للنفس تأساء وتعزية ... إحدى يديّ أصابتني ولم ترد
كلاهما خلف من فقد صاحبه ... هذا أخي حين أدعوه وذا ولدي
(I say to my soul, for solace and consolation: one of my two hands struck me, without intending it; each of them is a replacement for the loss of the other — this is my brother when I call him, and that my son.)
Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī made a fine statement regarding tajrīd. He said:
«The Arabs believe that in a person there is a meaning latent in him, as if it were his reality and his substance; so they bring that meaning out into their expressions abstracted from the person, as though it were other than him while it is he himself, e.g. their saying: "If you meet so-and-so, you will meet in him the lion", and "If you ask him, you will be asking in him the sea", while he himself is the lion and the sea — not that there is something separate from him or distinct from him». Then he said: «Of this pattern is a person addressing himself, so that it is as if he were conversing with another, as al-Aʿshā said:
ودّع هريرة إن الركب مرتحل ... وهل تطيق وداعا أيها الرجل
— and he is the man himself, not another».
Ibn al-Athīr commented on what Abū ʿAlī mentioned, saying: «My view is that he was right in the second and not right in the first, because the second is tajrīd — do you not see that al-Aʿshā abstracted the address from himself while meaning himself? As for the first, namely his saying "If you meet so-and-so, you will meet in him the lion, and if you ask him, you will be asking in him the sea", this is a simile with an implied particle, since it is fitting to supply the particle of simile in it» — until he says: «Abū ʿAlī's statement is also invalidated from another aspect, namely that he said: "The Arabs believe that in a person there is a meaning latent in him, as if it were his reality and his substance, so they bring that meaning out into their expressions abstracted from the person, as though it were other than him while it is he himself". This is refuted by our saying: "If you see the lion, you will see in him his crushing force (haḍbatahu)", and "If you meet him, you will meet death from him". For the form he presented regarding the person, claiming that the Arabs believe it to be a meaning latent in him, we have presented the like of it regarding the lion; so restricting it to the person is invalid. Neither of the two forms is tajrīd; it is only a simile with an implied particle».
Our view is that Ibn al-Athīr was unfair to Abū ʿAlī, because this example's being a simile with an implied particle does not prevent its being tajrīd at the same time.
What has preceded is sufficient for us.

farraa:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾: he says: the Torah and the Gospel do not belie it, and they are [from] before it; ﴿ولا من خلفه﴾: he says: no Book will be sent down after it that belies it.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
He (Allah bless him) was distressed by their belying him, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down upon him: nothing of belying is said to you except as the messengers before you were belied.

farraa:44-44.t:
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: ﴿ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾.
As a question, and they made the ʿayn sukūn (vowelless); and the exegesis came: "Is this messenger to be an Arab while the Book is foreign (aʿjamī)?" Al-Ḥasan read it without a question: أعجمى وعربى, as though he made it part of their saying, meaning the unbelievers, i.e.: "Why have its verses not been set out in detail, some of them Arabic which the Arab understands, and some foreign which the foreigner understands?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ﴾.
And some of them read it: "أَعَجَمِىٌّ وعربى", asking a question and relating it to the ʿAjam (non-Arabs).
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: more than one of them narrated to me, [Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and] Mindal, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, from Sulaymān ibn Qatta, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: عَمٍ.
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
You say to the man who does not understand what you say: "You are being called from far away," and you say to the quick of understanding: "You certainly take a thing from close by." And it came in the exegesis: it is as though they are being called [from the sky], so they do not hear.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَةٍ مِّنْ أَكْمَامِهَا﴾.
The husk of the kufurrā (the palm spathe) is a kimm; and the people of the Ḥijāz read it: ﴿وما تخرج من ثمراتٍ﴾.
His saying: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ آذَنَّاكَ﴾.
This is from the saying of the gods whom they used to worship in this world. They said: "We have informed you that there is not among us any witness to what they said."

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَسْأَمُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: "من دعاء بالخير".

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَذُو دُعَآءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾: he says: possessing much supplication; if you describe it with length or with breadth, it is correct.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: [167/a] ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ﴾.
[As for أنه: if you wish, you make أنَّ in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) by repetition (takrīr): "Does it not suffice regarding your Lord that He is Witness over all things?"; and if you wish, you make it nominative (rafʿ), as in your saying: "Does it not suffice regarding your Lord] His witnessing over all things?"; and the nominative is dearer to me.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾.
You make [qurʾānan] accusative by the verb, i.e. its verses were set out in detail thus; and it may be accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment), because the speech is complete at His word (āyātuhu). Had it been nominative as an adjective of "Book", it would have been correct, as He said in another place: ﴿كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَاركٌ﴾. Likewise His words ﴿بَشِيراً ونذيراً﴾ admit what ﴿قرآنا عربيا﴾ admits.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ﴾.
He says: between us and you there is a separation in our religion, so work for our destruction; we are working for the same against you. And it is said: work according to what you know of your religion, for we are working according to our religion.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words: ﴿لاَ يُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَاةَ﴾.
The zakāt in this place: Quraysh used to feed the pilgrims and give them water, and they denied that to whoever believed in Muḥammad, Allah bless him; so this was revealed about them. Then He said: and in them there is something greater than this: their disbelief in the Hereafter.

farraa:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "wa-qasama fīhā aqwātahā" ("and He apportioned in it its provisions"): He put in this [land] what is not in that, so that they might live together and trade.
His words: ﴿سَوَآءً لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it in the accusative, and al-Ḥasan in the genitive, making it an adjective of "the days", or, if you wish, of "the four". Whoever makes it accusative makes it connected with "the provisions". It may also be nominative, as if a fresh start, as though He said: "That is equal for those who ask"; He says: for whoever wants to know it.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words: ﴿قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا﴾.
He made the heavens and the earths like two, as in His words: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُمَا﴾, and He did not say "[and what is] between them (pl.)"; had it been so, it would have been correct.
His words: ﴿أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ﴾.
He did not say ṭāʾiʿatayn (feminine dual) nor ṭāʾiʿāt (feminine plural). It was taken to refer to the heavens and those in them. It is also permissible to say, even though they are two: "we have come, willing (ṭāʾiʿīna)", so that they are treated like men since they spoke.

farraa:12-12.t:
His words: ﴿فَقَضَاهُنَّ﴾.
He says: He created them and perfected them.
His words: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمْرَهَا﴾.
He says: He placed angels in every heaven; that is its affair.

farraa:14-14.t:
His words: ﴿إِذْ جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلرُّسُلُ مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ﴾.
The messengers came to their forefathers and those who were before them; and "from behind them" — He says: and messengers came to them themselves after those messengers. So the hāʾ and mīm in (khalfihim) refer to the messengers. Or it may refer to them [the people], making "from behind them" mean those [messengers] who were with them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His words: ﴿رِيحاً صَرْصَراً﴾.
A cold [wind] that burns [as] fire burns.
His words: ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ﴾.
The common people read it heavy, with kasra on the ḥāʾ; some of the people of Medina made it light: (naḥsāt).
He said: [And I heard one of the Arabs reciting:
أبلغْ جذاما ولخما أن إخوتهم * طيا وبهراء قوم نصرهم نِحس
(Tell Judhām and Lakhm that their brothers, Ṭayyiʾ and Bahrāʾ, are a people whose help is ill-omened.)]
This is for whoever makes it heavy; and whoever makes it light bases it on His words: "fī yawmi naḥsin mustamirrin".

farraa:17-17.t:
His words: ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
The reading is with Thamūd in the nominative; ʿĀṣim, the people of Medina and al-Aʿmash read so. But al-Aʿmash used to make Thamūd declinable (yujrī, with tanwīn) throughout the Quran except His words: ﴿وآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ﴾, where he did not give it tanwīn, because it is written without alif. Whoever makes it declinable makes it the name of a man or a mountain, and whoever does not makes it the name of the nation to which he belongs. He said: and I heard one of the Arabs say: "You leave the Banū Asad, and they are eloquent", and he did not make Asad declinable. Whatever names that are [normally] declinable you mean by them the tribe, do not make declinable [Translator's note: the source reads «فلا تحرها», apparently for «فلا تجرها»]; but making them declinable is better in Arabic, like your saying: "Tamīmun came to you in its entirety" and "Qaysun in its entirety"; this is among what is made declinable, and it may be made indeclinable with the same explanation as for Thamūd and Asad.
Al-Ḥasan used to read: "wa-ammā Thamūda fa-hadaynāhum", in the accusative. It is an option, but the nominative is better, because ammā seeks nouns and refuses verbs, so it is like a ṣila for the noun. Had ammā been a particle that may be followed by a noun if you wish and by a verb if you wish, the nominative and the accusative would have been equal, as in His words: ﴿والْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناه مَنازِلَ﴾. Do you not see that the wāw goes with the verb and with the noun? You say: "ʿAbdallāh I struck him, and Zayd I left him", because you say: "and I left Zayd"; so the wāw is acceptable with the verb as it is with the noun. But you do not say: "ammā ḍarabta fa-ʿAbdallāh", as you say: "ammā ʿAbdallāh fa-ḍarabta". And whoever permits the accusative while recognizing this reason [165/ب] says: the natural order of what governs nouns in the accusative is that it precedes them, not that they precede it. And all is correct.
His words: ﴿فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
He says: We showed them the way of good and the way of evil, like His words: ﴿وهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجدينِ﴾: good and evil.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us:] al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Qays related to me from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqa, from Abū ʿUmāra, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said concerning His words ﴿وهَدَيناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: good and evil.
Abū Zakariyyā said: And likewise His words: ﴿إنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإمَّا كَفُوراً﴾.
And guidance in another sense is that which is right guidance (irshād), like your saying "We made him happy"; of that are
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّّذينَ هَدَى اللّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾, in much of the Quran.

farraa:19-19.t:
His words: ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾.
It is from wazaʿtu; the meaning of wazaʿtuhu is: I held him back and restrained him. It has come in the commentary: the first of them are held back for the last of them until they enter the Fire.
He said: and I heard one of the Arabs say: "I will certainly send against you someone who will restrain you (yazaʿukum) and bridle you (yuḥkimukum)" — from the ḥakama (bit-ring) of the riding animal. He said: and Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī recited to me:
فإنكما إن تُحكِمَانى وترسلا * علىّ غُواة الناس إِيبَا وتضلعاً
(For if you two bridle me and loose the misguided among people upon me, I will refuse and resist.)
This is of that kind. īb is from abaytu and ābā.

farraa:20-20.t:
His words: ﴿سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصَارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُم﴾.
"Skin" here — and Allah knows best — is the private part; it is something alluded to, as He said: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لاَ تُواعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾, meaning marriage [intercourse]; and as He said: ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِن الْغَائطِ﴾: al-ghāʾiṭ is the open ground, and what is meant by it is: or one of you has relieved himself.

farraa:22-22.t:
His words: ﴿وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ﴾.
He says: you did not fear that your limbs would bear witness against you so that you would hide from them, and you would not have been able to hide. And it may be by way of reproach (taʿbīr) [Translator's note: or "by way of expression"]: i.e. you did not hide from them.
His words: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن ظَنَنتُمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh, in place of ﴿ولكن ظننتم﴾: "wa-lākin zaʿamtum" ("but you claimed"). zaʿm and ẓann are one in meaning, though they may differ.

farraa:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾.
"dhālikum" is in the position of a nominative by "your thought" [as mubtadaʾ (subject) with khabar (predicate)], and you make "ardākum" in the position of an accusative, as if you said: "That is your thought, ruining you". It is also permissible to make the "ruining" the predicate that governs the nominative, on the view of whoever says: hādhā ʿAbdullāhi qāʾimun [166/ا], meaning "ʿAbdallāh — this one — is standing"; but this is disfavoured. And ardākum may be a fresh start; had it appeared as a noun, it would be nominative, like His words in [Sūrat] Luqmān: ﴿الم، تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتَابِ الْحَكِيمِ، هُدًى ورحمةٌ﴾ — Ḥamza read it so; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "a-alidu wa-anā ʿajūzun wa-hādhā baʿlī shaykhun"; and in [Sūrat] Qāf: ﴿هَذَا مَا لَدَىَّ عَتيدٌ﴾. All of this is as a fresh start; had you intended connection, it would be accusative. He said: and someone recited to me:
مَنْ يك ذا بَتٍّ فهذا بَتِّى * مُقيِّظٌ مصيِّف مُشَتِّى * جمعته من نعجات ست *
(Whoever has a cloak — this is my cloak, for summer, for the hot season and for winter; I gathered it from six ewes.)

farraa:25-25.t:
His words: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنَا لَهُمْ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾.
[What is before them is] of the affair of the Hereafter: so they said: there is no Paradise, no Fire, no resurrection and no reckoning. And what is behind them is of the affair of this world: they made pleasures attractive to them, and amassing wealth, and abandoning spending in the ways of righteousness; this is what is behind them. So the commentary came. It may also be that what is before them is the worldly affairs they are in, and what is behind them is the affair of the Hereafter.

farraa:26-26.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾.
The disbelievers of Quraysh said it. Abū Jahl said to them: When Muḥammad, Allah bless him, recites the Quran, make idle noise during it — make a din — perhaps he will change [something] or forget, and you will overcome him.

farraa:28-28.t:
His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُ﴾, then He said: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ﴾.
And it is the Fire itself. That is correct: [as] if you said: "The people of Kufa have in it a good abode", the abode being Kufa itself; and it is good when you said [with "the abode"] and "Kufa" — it is the abode — so their two wordings differ. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "dhālika jazāʾu aʿdāʾi Allāhi al-nāru dāru al-khuldi" ("that is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity"); this is clear, with nothing [problematic] in it, because the abode is the Fire.

farraa:29-29.t:
His words: ﴿رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلاَّنَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ﴾.
It is said: the one of the jinn who led them astray is Iblīs, [and] of mankind Cain (Qābīl), who killed his brother; He says: he was the first of mankind to lay down the practice of going astray.

farraa:30-30.t:
His words: ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ﴾.
At death, giving them good tidings of Paradise. In our reading it is "allā takhāfū" ("that you should not fear"), and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh "lā takhāfū" ("do not fear") without an, by way of reported speech (ḥikāya).

farraa:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ﴾.
He means: none is granted the repelling of evil with good except one who is patient, or one possessed of a great portion. He made it feminine because "the word" (al-kalima) is feminine; and had He meant "the speech" (al-kalām) [and made it masculine], it would have been correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His words: ﴿وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾.
He says: [if] he turns you away from Our command to you to repel evil with good, then seek refuge in Allah — take refuge in Him.

farraa:37-37.t:
His words: ﴿لاَ تَسْجُدُواْ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلاَ لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾.
He created the sun, the moon, the night and the day; and they are made feminine in His words "khalaqahunna" [166/ب] because every masculine thing other than people and the like is feminine in its plural. You say: "Some garments passed by me, and I bought them (ibtaʿtuhunna)", and "I had mosques, and I demolished them and built them (hadamtuhunna wa-banaytuhunna)". Build [on] this.

farraa:39-39.t:
His words: ﴿ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ﴾.
Its yield increased; and rabat means: it swells, then cracks open for the plants.

farraa:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾.
It may be asked: where is the predicate (jawāb) of inna? If you wish, you may make it ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾. And if you wish, it is in His words: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾ ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ﴾, so that its predicate is known and therefore left out. This seems the more Arabic of the two explanations and the closer to what has come in the Quran.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «تنزيل» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: this Quran; the preposition phrase «من الرحمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «تنزيل»; «الرحيم» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «كتاب» is a badal (substitute) from {تَنْزِيلٌ}; the clause «فُصِّلت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»; «قرآنا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «آياته»; the preposition phrase «لقوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فصلت»; and the clause «يعلمون» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «بشيرا» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {قُرْآنًا}; the clause «فأعرض» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {فُصِّلَتْ}; and the clause «فهم لا يسمعون» is conjoined to the clause «فأعرض أكثرهم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition phrase «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أكنَّة»; the clause «وفي آذاننا وقر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «قلوبنا في أكنة», and likewise the clause «ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب»; the clause «فاعمل» is conjoined to the clause «من بيننا وبينك حجاب»; and the clause «إننا عاملون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «مثلكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بشر»; the clause «يوحى» is a second naʿt of «بشر»; the interpreted maṣdar «أنما إلهكم إله واحد» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause «فاستقيموا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قل»; the clause «وويل للمشركين» is resumptive, and beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it indicates an imprecation.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «المشركين»; the clause «وهم.. كافرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative clause «لا يؤتون»; the second «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first; the preposition phrase «بالآخرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «لهم أجر» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and «غير» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أجر».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «تجعلون», and the clause «ذلك رب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «وجعل» is resumptive; conjoining it to the clause {خَلَقَ} is weak because of the separation between them by something foreign, namely {وَتَجْعَلُونَ}. This «جعل» is transitive to one object, because it is in the sense of "created". The preposition phrase «من فوقها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رواسي»; the preposition phrase «في أربعة» is attached to «قدر». «سواء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied (muqaddar) governor, i.e.: they were equal; the preposition phrase «للسائلين» is attached to the implied governor.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ثم استوى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قدَّر»; the clause «وهي دخان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «السماء»; «طوعا»: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl; the clause «قالتا» is resumptive; and «طائعين» is a ḥāl of the pronoun «نا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «فقضاهنَّ» is resumptive; «سبع» is the second object of «قضاهنَّ», which carries the meaning of "made them into"; the preposition phrase «في يومين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause «وأوحى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قضاهنَّ». His saying «وحفظا»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e.: and We guarded it with a guarding; the clause "وحفظناها" is conjoined to the clause «زينَّا»; and the clause «ذلك تقدير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «فإن أعرضوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {قُلْ} in verse (9); «صاعقة» is a second object; «مثل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «صاعقة».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ}; the maṣdar «ألا تعبدوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition (الباء); «أن» is the one that makes [the verb] accusative, and «لا» is prohibitive; the conditional clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause «فإنا.. كافرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the conditional clause; and the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «فأما عاد ...» is resumptive; «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing; the preposition phrase «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «استكبروا»; the preposition phrase «منا» is attached to «أشد»; «قوة» is tamyīz (specification); the clause «أولم يروا» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «يروا»; «هو أشد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «أن»; the clause «وكانوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قالوا»; and the preposition phrase «بآياتنا» is attached to «يجحدون».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «فأرسلنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَكَانُوا}; the preposition phrase «في أيام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا»; the maṣdar «لنذيقهم» is genitive, attached to «أرسلنا»; «عذاب» is a second object; the preposition phrase «في الحياة» is attached to «نذيقهم»; the clause «ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى» is parenthetical, the wāw is parenthetical, and the lām is of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); and the clause «وهم لا ينصرون» is conjoined to the clause «ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «وأما ثمود فهديناهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {فَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا}; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «فهديناهم» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ثمود»; the clause «فاستحبوا العمى» is conjoined to the clause «هديناهم»; the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أخذتهم», and «ما» is a relative noun in the genitive by the bāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «ونجينا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أخذتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The wāw is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) "remember"; the preposition phrase «إلى النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحشر»; and the clause «فهم يوزعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يحشر».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); the conditional clause is resumptive; and the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهد».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the conditional clause. «لِمَ»: the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهدتم»; its alif was dropped because it is preceded by the preposition. The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; the clause «وهو خلقكم» is conjoined to the clause «أنطقنا الله»; «أول» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its adjective standing in for it; and the clause «ترجعون» is conjoined to the clause «خلقكم».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «وما كنتم تستترون» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يشهد» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: for fear [that ... should testify]; the clause «ولكن ظننتم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما كنتم»; the interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «ظن»; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «وذلكم ظنكم ...» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَلَكِنْ ظَنَنْتُمْ}; «ظنكم» is a badal (substitute), and the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective); the preposition phrase «بربكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object, i.e.: you thought it to be concerning your Lord; the clause «أرداكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «ذلكم»; and the clause «فأصبحتم» is conjoined to the clause «أرداكم».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «فإن يصبروا» is resumptive, and «ما» operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «وحق عليهم القول» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «زينوا»; the preposition phrase «في أمم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «عليهم»; the clause «قد خَلَتْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أمم». The preposition phrase «من الجن» is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «خلت»; and the clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وقال الذين» is resumptive; the clause «لعلكم تغلبون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «فلنذيقنَّ الذين» is resumptive; the clause «نذيقن» is the answer to the oath; «عذابا» is a second object, and likewise «أسوأ»; and the clause «لنجزينَّهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نذيقن».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «النار» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is the clause «لهم دار الخلد», and the clause is resumptive. The preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «لهم»; «جزاء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is implied (muqaddar); the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to the maṣdar (جزاء); the preposition phrase «بآياتنا» is attached to «يجحدون».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «أَرِنا» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; it is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter, and the pronoun is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «الذين» is a relative noun, a second object; the preposition phrase «من الجن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أضلانا»; the clause «نجعلهما» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the adverb «تحت» is attached to the implied second object.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «ثم استقاموا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قالوا»; the clause «تتنزل» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the maṣdar «ألا تخافوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition (الباء), and «أن» is maṣdariyya, making [the verb] accusative; and the clause «وأَبْشِروا» is conjoined to the clause «لا تخافوا».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «نحن أولياؤكم» is parenthetical; the preposition phrase «في الحياة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولياء»; the clause «ولكم فيها ما تشتهي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {كُنْتُمْ}; the preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «نزلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of {مَا}, i.e.: and you will have in it whatever you call for, it being prepared [for you]. The preposition phrase «من غفور» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of «نزلا».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «ومَنْ أحسن» is resumptive; «قولا» is tamyīz (specification); the preposition phrase «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أحسن»; «صالحا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «عمل».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the clause «فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ادفع»; «الذي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the adverb «بينك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed before the mubtadaʾ «عداوة»; and the clause «كأنه ولي» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «الذي».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «وما يُلَقَّاها» is resumptive, and «الذين» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «يُلقَّاها».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «وإما ينزغنَّك ...» is resumptive. «إما» is composed of the conditional «إن» and the redundant (zāʾida) «ما»; [«ينزغنك» is] an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn, in the position of the jussive, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition phrase «من الشيطان» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «نزغ»; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه»; and «العليم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «ومن آياته الليل ...» is resumptive; the clause «لا تسجدوا» is resumptive; the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; and «إياه» is a detached accusative pronoun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «تعبدون» placed first.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «فإن استكبروا» is resumptive; the clause «فالذين عند ...» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: then leave them; and the clause «وهم لا يسأمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يسبِّحون».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The wāw is conjunctive; the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (the seeing of the earth is among His signs) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ اللَّيْلُ}; «خاشعة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «ترى»; the clause «إن الذي أحياها ...» is resumptive; «الموتى» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition phrase «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قدير».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition phrase «في آياتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يلحدون»; the clause «أفمن يلقى..» is resumptive; «من» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خير» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «في النار» is attached to «يلقى»; «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) conjunctive one; «من» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative noun «من يلقى»; «آمنا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يأتي»; the clause «اعملوا» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنه بصير»; and the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to «بصير».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «لما جاءهم» is parenthetical between the noun of «إن» and its implied (muqaddar) khabar (predicate), i.e.: are punished; and the clause «وإنه لكتاب عزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «لا يأتيه» is a second naʿt (adjective); «تنزيل» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it is a revelation; the preposition phrase «من حكيم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) «تنزيل».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «ما يقال لك» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الرسل»; and the clause «إن ربك لذو» is a badal (substitute) from «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); «أأعجمي» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise «عربي», the implied form being: is this Quran non-Arabic, while the tongue of the one to whom it was sent down is Arabic?! The clause «قل» is resumptive; «للذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «هدى»; the clause «والذين لا يؤمنون ...» is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause «في آذانهم وقر»; the preposition phrase «في آذانهم» is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «وقر»; the clause «وهو عليهم عمى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar clause; the preposition phrase «عليهم» is attached to a ḥāl of «عمى»; and the clause «أولئك ينادون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «سبقت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كلمة», and the khabar (predicate) of «كلمة» is omitted; the preposition phrase «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt of «كلمة»; the clause «وإنهم لفي شك» is resumptive; and the preposition phrase «منه» is attached to a naʿt of «شك».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition phrase «فلنفسه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the implied form being: his deed is for himself, and his evil-doing is against it. The clause «وما ربك بظلام» is resumptive, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما»; «للعبيد» is the object of «ظَلام», and the lām is redundant, for strengthening.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: His saying «وما»: the wāw is conjunctive, «ما» is negative, «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and «ثمرات» is the fāʿil (agent), and likewise «من أنثى»; the preposition phrase «بعلمه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تضع»; and the clause «وما تخرج من ثمرات» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «إليه يُرَدّ». The wāw in «ويوم» is resumptive, and «يوم» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) «اذكر» (remember); «أين» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of place attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «شركائي»; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, and this implied saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: He calls them, saying: «أين شركائي». The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; «من شهيد» is a mubtadaʾ, and «من» is redundant; the clause «ما منا من شهيد» stands in place of the second and third objects, because the verb here carries the meaning of «أَعْلَم» (to inform), even though the verb «آذن» is not one of the verbs transitive to three objects.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the clause «وضلَّ عنهم ما كانوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the earlier clause {قَالُوا}; the clause «وظنوا» is conjoined to the clause «ضل»; the clause «ما لهم من محيص» stands in place of the two objects of «ظن»; «محيص» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «وإنْ مسَّه الشر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يسأم»; «يؤوس» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: then he is despairing; and «قنوط» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «ولئن أذقناه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ}; the preposition phrase «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة»; the preposition phrase «من بعد» is attached to «أذقناه»; the clause {مَسَّهُ} is a naʿt of «ضراء»; the clause «ليقولن» is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath; the clause «وما أظن» is conjoined to the clause «هذا لي»; the clause «ولئن رجعت» is conjoined to the clause «وما أظن»; the clause «إن لي عنده للحسنى» is the answer to the oath; the preposition phrase «لي» is attached to the khabar (predicate); the adverb «عنده» is attached to the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; the clause «لننبئن» is the answer to the oath, and the oath together with its answer is a resumptive clause; and the clause «ولنذيقنَّهم» is conjoined to the clause «ننبئن».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {لا يَسْأَمُ الإِنْسَانُ} in verse (49), and the second conditional clause is conjoined to the first. His saying «فذو»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: then he is possessed of.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «أرأيتم» means "tell me"; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); it takes two objects: the first is omitted, its implied form being "yourselves", and its second object is the nominal clause «مَنْ أضل». The clause «إن كان من عند الله» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what follows it, i.e.: then no one is further astray. The preposition phrase «ممَّن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أضلّ».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أنه الحق» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يتبين»; the clause «أولم يكف بربك» is resumptive; «بربك» is the fāʿil of «يكف», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); and the interpreted maṣdar «أنه على كل شيء شهيد» is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «ربك».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The preposition phrase «من لقاء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مرية».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {تَنْزِيل من الرَّحْمَن الرَّحِيم}: تنزيل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); من الرحمن is its naʿt (adjective), الرحيم a second naʿt, and كتاب its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative by an implied هذا ("this is").

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {قُرْآنًا عَرَبيا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has also been said that it is accusative as praise (madḥ). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ did not allow it to be accusative as a ḥāl; rather, according to them it is accusative by فصّلت, i.e. "its verses have been detailed thus". In (ordinary) speech they both allowed the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {بشيرا وَنَذِيرا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الآيات, and what governs all the ḥāls is فصّلت. It is also possible that بشيرا ونذيرا are two ḥāls from كتاب, because it has been given an adjective; what governs the ḥāl is then the sense of the implied drawing of attention (tanbīh), or the sense of pointing, if you take the implied form to be "this is a Book whose verses have been detailed".

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {يُوحى إِلَيّ أَنما}: أنّ is in the nominative position, governed by يوحى.

His saying سواء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of استواء, i.e. "they were equal, an equalness". Whoever put it in the nominative took it as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with للسائلين as the khabar (predicate), in the sense of "equal for whoever asked and said: in how many (days) were they created?". It has also been said: "for whoever asks" means for all creation, because they ask for sustenance and other things from Allah, exalted be His mention. Whoever put it in the genitive made it a naʿt (adjective) of الأيام or of أربعة. The well-known readers have the accusative only.

[Translator's note: سواء is in āya 10, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying {أَتَيْنَا طائعين}: He reported about the heavens and the earths with the yāʾ and nūn (the masculine sound plural used for rational beings), according to the Kufans and al-Kisāʾī, only because the meaning is "we came, with those within us, obedient"; so He reported about rational beings with the yāʾ and nūn, which is the basic rule. It has also been said that since He reported about them with speech, which belongs to rational beings, He reported about them as about rational beings, with the yāʾ and nūn.

[Translator's note: the source has «السوات», evidently for «السماوات», and «أخبر عنها من يعقل», evidently for «أخبر عنها إخبار من يعقل».]

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {فقضاهن سبع سماوات}: سبع is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and nūn, i.e. "He completed seven heavens". السماء is treated as masculine in the sense of "roof", and is also treated as feminine. The Qurʾān came with the feminine, saying سبع سماوات; had it come with the masculine, it would have said سبعة سماوات.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {وَأما ثَمُود فهديناهم}: ثمود is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is definite, the name of the tribe. [Translator's note: the source has «اسم للصلة», evidently a misprint for «اسم للقبيلة».] Al-Aʿmash read it fully declined, making it the name of the clan. It is related from al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim that they read it in the accusative without full declension, putting it in the accusative by an implied verb which فهديناهم explains, because أمّا carries the meaning of condition and is therefore more suited to the verb. So the accusative, for him, is stronger; but the nominative is fully good, and it is the preferred view according to Sībawayh. The implied form of the accusative is "whatever may be the case, We guided Thamūd: We guided them".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {وَيَوْم يحْشر أَعدَاء الله إِلَى النَّار}: what governs يوم is a verb indicated by يوزعون, its implied form being "and people are driven on the day when (the enemies of Allah) are gathered", or "and remember the day…". يحشر does not govern it, because يوم is in construct with it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {تستترون أَن يشْهد}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "from (عن) that (your hearing) should testify" or "from (من) that it should testify".

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {وذلكم ظنكم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and أرداكم a second khabar. It has also been said that ظنكم is a badal (substitute) for ذلكم and أرداكم the khabar. Al-Farrāʾ said أرداكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); but according to the Basrans a past verb is not good as a ḥāl except with قد implied.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {ذَلِك جَزَاء أَعدَاء الله النَّار}: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جزاء its khabar (predicate), and النار is (a badal) from جزاء. It has also been said that النار is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, the clause being in the position of an explanation (bayān) of the first clause.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying نزلا: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t:
His saying {وَمن آيَاته أَنَّك}: أنّ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the prepositional phrase before it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that أنّ is nominative by the (implied) "being settled" (istiqrār). Beginning with the fatḥa-form (أنّ) is permissible because the genitive phrase precedes it.

His saying {خاشعة} is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأرض, because ترى is from seeing with the eye.

His saying {وربت}: the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) of the verb was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the feminine tāʾ. It is from ربا يربو, when something increases; from it comes الربا, (usury) in debt, which is forbidden. Abū Jaʿfar read وربأت with hamza, from الربيئة, which is elevation, so its meaning is "it rose". One says ربأ يربأ and ربؤ يربؤ when something rises.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين كفرُوا بِالذكر لما جَاءَهُم}: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ is أولئك ينادون. It has also been said that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them have lost" or "have been destroyed", and the like.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا قد قيل للرسل}: مَا with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the nominative position as the object whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) of يقال, because the verb reaches the maṣdar, so the maṣdar is made to stand in place of the agent. Even if (a verb) does not take an object, it does reach the maṣdar and adverbs.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين لَا يُؤمنُونَ فِي آذانهم وقر}: الذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is its khabar (predicate); وقر is a mubtadaʾ and في آذانهم its khabar, and لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

His saying {يتَبَيَّن لَهُم أَنه الْحق}: the hāʾ in أنه is for Allah the Exalted; it has also been said for the Qurʾān, and it has been said for the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace. أنّ is in the nominative position, governed by يتبيّن, because it is its fāʿil (agent).

[Translator's note: يتبين لهم أنه الحق is in āya 53, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {وَلَوْلَا كلمة}: كلمة is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted and is not made overt, according to Sībawayh.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {من أكمامها}: it is the plural of كِمّ; and whoever says أكمّة makes it the plural of كِمام.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {أولم يكف بِرَبِّك أَنه}: بربك is in the nominative position because it is the fāʿil (agent) of يكف, and أنه is a badal (substitute) for ربك according to its position, so it is in the nominative position; or it is in the genitive position as a badal according to the wording. It has also been said that it is in the accusative position by omission of the lām, i.e. "because He is over all things (a witness)".

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم﴾: تنزيل: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a revelation" (هو تنزيل). ومن الرحمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿تنزيل﴾. والرحيم: naʿt. Or ﴿تنزيل﴾ is mubtadaʾ, and His word ﴿كتاب﴾ in the following ayah is its khabar; beginning with ﴿تنزيل﴾ is permissible because it is specified by the adjective.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون﴾: كتاب: badal (substitute) of تنزيل, or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar. The clause ﴿فصلت﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتاب﴾; فصلت: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the tāʾ is for the feminine. وآياته: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). وقرآنًا: ḥāl (circumstantial) of كتاب. وعربيًّا: naʿt of ﴿قرآنا﴾. ولقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿فصلت﴾, or attached to an omitted second naʿt of ﴿قرآنا﴾. The clause ﴿يعلمون﴾ is a naʿt of ﴿قوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون﴾: ﴿بشيرا﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرآنًا﴾, or ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿كتاب﴾. ونذيرا: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿بشيرًا﴾. ﴿فأعرض﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أعرض is a past verb. وأكثرهم: fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is the sign of the plural. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿لا يسمعون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of هم.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive. وقالوا: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). وقلوبنا: mubtadaʾ (subject). وفي أكنة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate). ومما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted, the implied form being: "in coverings that prevent us from what you call us to" (في أكنة تمنعنا مما تدعونا إليه). The clause ﴿تدعونا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿وقالوا قلوبنا...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أعرض أكثرهم﴾ in the previous ayah, or resumptive with no grammatical position. وفي آذاننا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ووقر: delayed mubtadaʾ.
﴿ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ومن بيننا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. وبينك: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to بيننا. وحجاب: delayed mubtadaʾ. فاعمل: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and اعمل is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil. وإننا: إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun. وعاملون: its khabar.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد﴾: قل: an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). إنما: the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). وأنا: mubtadaʾ (subject). وبشر: khabar (predicate). ومثلكم: naʿt (adjective); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿يوحى﴾ is a second naʿt of بشر; ويوحى: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive). وإلي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿يوحى﴾. وأنما: kāffa wa-makfūfa. وإلهكم: mubtadaʾ. وإله: khabar. وواحد: naʿt. The interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنما إلهكم ...﴾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition). واستقيموا: an imperative verb and its fāʿil. واستغفروه: conjoined to فاستقيموا, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وويل: the wāw is a conjunction, and ويل is mubtadaʾ; beginning with it is permissible because of the meaning of imprecation in it. وللمشركين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة﴾: الذين: naʿt (adjective). The clause ﴿لا يؤتون الزكاة﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ولا: negative. ويؤتون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). والزكاة: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. وهم: mubtadaʾ (subject). وبالآخرة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿كافرون﴾. The second هم: tawkīd (emphasis) of the first. وكافرون: the khabar (predicate) of هم.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. وإن: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters). والذين: its noun. The clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; وآمن: a past verb, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). وعملوا: conjoined to آمنوا. والصالحات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra. ولهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). وأجر: delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). وغير: naʿt (adjective). وممنون: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The nominal clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين﴾: the hamza is interrogative. وإن: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿كم﴾ is its noun. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). The clause ﴿تكفرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن. وبالذي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿تكفرون﴾. The clause ﴿خلق الأرض﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. وفي يومين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خلق﴾.
﴿وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿تجعلون﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تكفرون﴾. وله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object of تجعلون. وأندادًا: its first object. وذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to الذي in view of its being described by what the ṣila indicated. ورب: its khabar. والعالمين: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to خلق الأرض. وفيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted second object. ورواسي: the first object of جعل. It is also valid to attach the preposition and its genitive noun to جعل, taking it in the sense of "created" (خلق), in which case it puts only one object in the accusative. ومن فوقها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رواسي. [Translator's note: the source does not parse ﴿وبارك فيها﴾.]
﴿وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. وقدر: a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). وفيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدر﴾. وأقواتها: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). وفي أربعة أيام: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿قدر﴾; وأيام: muḍāf ilayhi. وسواء: ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿أيام﴾, i.e. complete, with no deficiency or excess in them. وللسائلين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted verb [Translator's note: so in the source; no omitted verb has been named in this entry]. Or ﴿سواء﴾ is parsed [Translator's note: the source has «تعراب», apparently for «تُعرب»] as ḥāl of the pronoun in أقواتها.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان﴾: ثم: a conjunction. واستوى: a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو". وإلى السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿استوى﴾. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). و﴿هي﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ودخان: khabar (predicate).
﴿فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction. وقال: a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted. ولها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قال﴾. وللأرض: conjoined to ﴿لها﴾. وائتيا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is fāʿil. ﴿طوعًا وكرهًا﴾: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. willing or unwilling (طائعتين أو كارهتين). [Translator's note: the source writes «طوعًا وكرهًا» with wāw where the ayah has أو, and does not parse ﴿قالتا أتينا طائعين﴾.]

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction. وقضاهن: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وسبع: second object of ﴿قضاهن﴾, because it has been made to include the meaning of صيّر (to make into). وسماوات: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). وفي يومين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿قضاهن﴾. وأوحى: the wāw is a conjunction, and أوحى is a past verb with a latent fāʿil. وفي كل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أوحى﴾. وسماء: muḍāf ilayhi. وأمرها: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. وزينا: a verb and its fāʿil. والسماء: mafʿūl bihi. والدنيا: naʿt (adjective). وبمصابيح: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زينا﴾. وحفظًا: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding" (وحفظناها حفظًا); or it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) according to the meaning, as if He had said: ﴿وخلقنا المصابيح زينة وحفظًا﴾ (and We created the lamps as adornment and protection). وذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject). وتقدير: muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; تقدير is evidently the khabar (predicate) of ذلك and is itself the muḍāf]. والعزيز: muḍāf ilayhi. والعليم: naʿt of العزيز, genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إن is conditional. وأعرضوا: a past verb, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); the verb is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). فقل: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and قل is an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت". وأنذرتكم: a past verb, its fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وصاعقة: second mafʿūl bihi. ومثل: naʿt (adjective) of صاعقة. وصاعقة: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and it is itself muḍāf. وعاد: muḍāf ilayhi. وثمود: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿عاد﴾, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) of ﴿صاعقة عاد وثمود﴾, taking the meaning of الصاعقة to be the punishment; or it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of it; or ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb of ﴿قالوا﴾ after it, and the clause is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), as if it came in answer to a question whose implied form is: "What was their case?" (ما شأنهم؟). The clause ﴿جاءتهم الرسل﴾ is in the position of genitive by being put in construct (iḍāfa). ﴿من بين﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿جاءتهم﴾, and أيديهم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); or they are attached to an omitted ḥāl of الرسل, i.e. the messengers being from before ʿĀd and Thamūd. ﴿من خلفهم﴾: conjoined to ﴿من بين أيديهم﴾, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ألا تعبدوا إلا الله﴾: in ﴿أن﴾ there are three views:
The first: it is lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted; its original form is أنه لا تعبدوا, i.e. "in that the matter and the account is Our saying to you: do not worship anyone but Allah". The clause ﴿لا تعبدوا..﴾ is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the lightened أن, and أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) accusative by removal of the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl of الرسل, its implied form being "saying" (قائلين). ولا: prohibitive. وتعبدوا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا. وإلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). The Name of Majesty: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The second view: it is a maṣdar particle that puts into the accusative; ﴿لا﴾ is negative, and ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن. The interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾ and what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl of الرسل, its implied form being "saying" (قائلين). The clause ﴿لا تعبدوا...﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position.
The third view: it is [Translator's note: a word appears to be missing in the source here, presumably «تفسيرية» (explicative)], because the coming of the messengers carries the sense of saying, and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position.
﴿قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون﴾: قالوا: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ولو: a non-jussive conditional particle. و﴿شاء ربنا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil; the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, its implied form being: ﴿إنزال ملائكة بالرسالة إلى الإنس لأنزل إليهم بها ملائكة﴾ (the sending down of angels with the message to humans, He would have sent down angels to them with it). The lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of لو. وأنزل: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil. وملائكة: mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition). وإن: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun. و﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿كافرون﴾; the clause ﴿أرسلتم به﴾ is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿كافرون﴾. وأرسلتم: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). وبه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسل﴾. وكافرون: the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive. وأما: a particle of condition and detailing. وعاد: mubtadaʾ (subject). The fāʾ links the answer of ﴿أما﴾. The clause استكبروا is the khabar (predicate) of عاد. وفي الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿استكبروا﴾. وبغير: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); والحق: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿فأما عاد...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وقالوا من أشد منا قوة﴾: قالوا: conjoined to ﴿فاستكبروا﴾. ومن: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. وأشد: khabar; the clause is the quoted speech. ومنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أشد﴾. وقوة: tamyīz (specification).
﴿أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and the wāw is a conjunction. The clause ﴿لم يروا﴾ is conjoined to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Were they heedless and astray, and did they not see?" (أغفلوا وضلوا ولم يروا). أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of يروا, because it has the meaning of knowing. وأن: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun. والذي: naʿt (adjective). The clause ﴿خلقهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. وهو: mubtadaʾ. وأشد: khabar. ومنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أشد﴾. وقوة: tamyīz. The clause is the khabar of أن.
﴿وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. وكانوا: a deficient past verb, and the wāw is the noun of كان. وبآياتنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يجحدون﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
