And Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam ibn Abān narrated to us from ʿIkrima, attributing it to the Prophet (marfūʿ), he said: the first for whom mercy will be decreed on the Day of Resurrection are the muezzins, and the first of the muezzins are the muezzins of Mecca. He said: and the muezzins will be the people with the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection; and the muezzins, when they come out of their graves, will call the adhān and proclaim with the call to prayer; and the muezzins are not eaten by worms in their graves. ʿIkrima said: and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If I were a muezzin, I would not mind if I did not perform the ḥajj, nor the ʿumra, nor fight in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: and the angels, peace be upon them, said: "If we were dwelling on earth, no one would precede us to the adhān." And with his chain from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعا إِلَى اللَّهِ — meaning the muezzins — وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً — he said: he prayed and fasted. Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān said: and Jarīr narrated to us from Fuḍayl ibn Abī Rufayda, who said: ʿĀṣim ibn Hubayra — who was one of the companions of Ibn Masʿūd — said to me, when I was a muezzin: "When you finish the adhān and have said 'There is no god but Allah', then say: 'And I am one of the Muslims'"; then he recited this verse: وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً وَقالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. «إنّني» is according to the original form; and whoever says «إنّي» omits [a nūn] because of the coming together of the nūns. The implied form, according to a group of the scholars of Arabic, is: "and he said: I am a Muslim, one of the Muslims"; and Hishām said likewise about وَقاسَمَهُما إِنِّي لَكُما لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ, that is, a sincere adviser, one of the sincere advisers. And one of the theologians (ahl al-naẓar) said: this saying of His, Mighty and Majestic, indicates that it is good to say "I am a Muslim" without exception [i.e. without adding "if Allah wills"], that is, I have submitted to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and accepted His command, so He has judged me to be a Muslim.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
وَلا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ: ʿAṭāʾ said: the good deed is "There is no god but Allah", and the evil deed is polytheism (shirk). ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ: that is, by the manner that is best. كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ: Abū Zayd said:
«الحميم» among the Arabs is the near relative. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «الحميم» is the intimate, and from it is the saying of the Arabs: "with him are the intimates (al-ḥāmma) and the commoners". [Translator's note: the text reads «الخاصة والعامة»; the point of the saying requires «الحامّة والعامّة».]

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: وَما يُلَقَّاها إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا: the pronoun alludes to the manner [of conduct] and to this word.

nahhas-irab:36-38.t:
وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَزْغٌ: [يَنْزَغَنَّكَ] is in the position of the jussive (jazm) by the condition, and the nūn entered for emphasis (tawkīd). We have already mentioned خَلَقَهُنَّ and what the pronoun refers back to.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: يَسْأَمُونَ means "they grow weary", and he recited the verse of Zuhayr: [al-Ṭawīl] 397-
ومن لا يزل يستحمل النّاس أمره ... ولا يعفها يوما من الدّهر يسأم
("Whoever keeps making people bear his affairs, and never spares them for a single day of time, will grow weary [of them].")
— that is, he grows weary.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
إِنَّ [Translator's note: so in the text; the word discussed is «أَنَّكَ» in «وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى الْأَرْضَ خاشِعَةً»] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, even though he does not permit «أن» to be at the beginning of speech; but since there is something before it, it became fit to begin with it. The nominative, according to al-Māzinī, is by an implied verb, in what cannot be begun with, just as you say «كيف زيد؟» ("How is Zayd?"), the implied form according to him being «كيف استقرّ زيد» ("How is Zayd settled?").
«خاشعة» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَإِذا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ: from «ربا يربو»; the alif was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the tāʾ after it. In the dual of «ربا» one says «ربوان»; thus said Sībawayh verbatim. The Kufans say «ربيان» with yāʾ, and they write «ربا» with yāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: and I heard Abū Isḥāq say: it is not enough for them to err in the writing; they go beyond that to the dual. Abū Jaʿfar said: the Qurʾān indicates what the Basrans said; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ [al-Rūm: 39]. The reading of Abū Jaʿfar is «اهتزّت وربأت», and it is taken from «الربيئة» (the lookout): one says «ربأ يربأ», so he is «رابئ», and «ربؤ يربؤ», so he is «ربيء», and «ربيئة» by way of intensification, when one goes up to a high place to keep watch. So the meaning of «وربأت» is "it rose". إِنَّ الَّذِي أَحْياها لَمُحْيِ الْمَوْتى: the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: ويُلْحِدُونَ is from «ألحد», and with the alif [i.e. the form afʿala] it is more frequent and better known.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ: there are several views about the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» here. Among the positions of al-Kisāʾī is that something indicating the khabar may come before it, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: أَفَمَنْ يُلْقى فِي النَّارِ خَيْرٌ, and others. And it is said: the khabar is أُولئِكَ يُنادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ. And it is said: the meaning is: those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them have disbelieved in something inimitable; and what indicates this is that after it comes وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتابٌ عَزِيزٌ; and this is the position of al-Farrāʾ according to the meaning of his statement. And it is said: the khabar is omitted, and its meaning is: they were destroyed.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: لا يَأْتِيهِ الْباطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ: the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is that its meaning is: no book comes to it from before it so as to invalidate it, nor from after it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied meaning on this basis is: falsehood does not come to it from these two directions, or invalidation does not come to it, with the [form] fāʿil having the meaning of the maṣdar (verbal noun), like «عافاه الله جلّ وعزّ عافية» ("Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted him well-being"). And it is said: «الباطل» here is Satan; and we have already mentioned this view. تَنْزِيلٌ is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: ما يُقالُ لَكَ إِلَّا ما قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ: Abū Ṣāliḥ said: that is, of harm.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً أَعْجَمِيًّا: «جعلنا» here is transitive to two objects; we have already mentioned this verse. قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدىً وَشِفاءٌ: «هدى» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «هو», and «وشفاء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. وَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated to us from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz from Abū ʿUbayd from Ḥajjāj from Shuʿba from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha from Sulaymān ibn Qatta from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, and Muʿāwiya and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah have mercy on them, that they read «وهو عليهم عمٍ» ("and it is blind to them"). And it was read to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Isḥāq, who said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «وهو عليهم عمٍ». This reading contradicts the codex (muṣḥaf). If someone says: the chain of transmission (isnād) is sound, he is told: consensus takes precedence; moreover, there is something [wrong] in the chain, namely that ʿAmr ibn Dīnār did not say "I heard Ibn ʿAbbās", so it is feared that it is mursal (with a gap in the chain); and Sulaymān ibn Qatta is not the equal of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār. Furthermore, Yaʿqūb the reader, with his standing in precision, said about this ḥadīth: I do not know whether they read «وهو عليهم عمٍ» or وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى as a past verb [i.e. «عَمِيَ»]. And [there is] the consensus of the whole body [of readers], apart from those we have mentioned. What is in the codex — namely that the meaning is with «عمى» (blindness) — is more appropriate, because He, Mighty and Majestic, said: قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدىً وَشِفاءٌ, so what is more appropriate to this is «عمى». [Translator's note: the text reads «أعمى» at this point, apparently for «عمى».] وَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ: «الذين» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar is in the clause. Some of the Arabs say «اللذون» in the position of the nominative; «الذين» is more frequent, and we have already mentioned the reason for it. وَشِفاءٌ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is its khabar [Translator's note: so in the text; this appears to refer to «وَقْرٌ», which is a mubtadaʾ with «فِي آذانِهِمْ» as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «الذين»]. يُنادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ is by way of a likeness (tamthīl), that is, they do not understand what is said to them; and the Arabs say of one who understands: "he is addressed from near by". Mujāhid said: مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ, that is, far from their hearts.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ: two objects. فَاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ: «كلمة» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted and never made overt. Some of the Kufans say: «لولا» is one of the particles that govern the nominative. As for the meaning of «كلمة», it is said: it is the deferment of their punishment until the Day of Resurrection and refraining from seizing them for disobedience, because of the benefit Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew to be in that; for if they were seized for their acts of disobedience at the time of disobeying, they would desist and would not be rewarded nor tested in that. In the ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad): «Were it not that you sin, Allah would bring a people who sin, and He would forgive them», that is, you are being tested, and your punishment is deferred so that you may repent.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِنَفْسِهِ: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the fāʾ and what follows it.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
وَما تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَراتٍ: this is the reading of the people of Medina, and the reading of the people of Kufa is «من ثمرة» (singular). This is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because «ثمرة» stands for «ثمرات» — that is his argument; so he took it as figurative (majāz), but the literal (ḥaqīqa) is more fitting and more valid. Since it is [written] with tāʾ in the codices, the reading «ثمرات» is more fitting.
مِنْ أَكْمامِها: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is what covers it. He said: the singular is «كمّ»; and whoever says «أكمّة» in the plural says «كمام» in the singular. وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِي: that is, according to your claim. قالُوا آذَنَّاكَ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: «آذنّاك» — he says: we have informed you. ما مِنَّا مِنْ شَهِيدٍ: «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis (tawkīd), that is, there is no witness among us who would testify that there is a god with You.

nahhas-irab:48-51.t:
وَظَنُّوا ما لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ: al-Akhfash said: «ظنّوا» means "they were certain". He said: and «ما» is a particle, so «ظنوا» does not govern it, and therefore it was suspended (ulghiya). Abū ʿUbayda said: «حاص يحيص» when one turns aside. Others said:
«المحيص» is the way out in which escape is hoped for.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ: there is an omission in the speech, that is: if it is from Allah and then you disbelieve in it, are you right in that?

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ: there are three views on its meaning. Among them: We will show them what the Prophet ﷺ told them would come to pass — trials, corruption, the victory of the Romans, Persia, and other things he foretold — until it becomes clear to them that all that he foretold is the truth. That is one view. And it is said: the meaning is: We will show them the traces of Our workmanship in the horizons, which indicate that they have a wise Maker, وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ, in that they were drops of fluid, then clinging clots, then lumps of flesh, until they reached maturity, attained reason and discernment, so that it becomes clear to them that Allah is the Truth, not what they worship besides Him. The third view was reported by al-Thawrī from ʿAmr ibn Qays from al-Minhāl — and some of the ḥadīth transmitters say: from al-Minhāl from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr or someone else — concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ: he said: the Prophet's ﷺ prevailing over people; «وفي أنفسهم» — he said: his prevailing over them. Abū Jaʿfar said: the most correct of these views is this one, and the sequence of the discourse indicates it. The first view is not sound, because there has been no previous mention of the reports so that they could be alluded to — I mean [in] أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ. Regarding the pronoun there are three views besides that of whoever said it refers to the report: one of them is that it refers back to the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; the second is that it refers back to the Qurʾān, since mention of it has preceded in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ; and the third is that it refers back to the Prophet ﷺ, and this is the most consistent of them with the sequence of the discourse. أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ: there are three views on it. Among them is that the meaning is: is your Lord not sufficient, by what He has indicated through His wisdom and His creation? In that there is sufficiency. The second: is your Lord not sufficient in punishing these obstinate disbelievers? In Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is sufficiency against them. The third: the meaning is: is it not sufficient for you, O Muḥammad, that your Lord is a witness over the deeds of these people, knowing what they conceal? This suffices you. And this is the most consistent of the views with the sequence of the verse, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best. Concerning the grammatical position of «أنه» there are three views: its position may be nominative, with the meaning "is it not sufficient that He is a witness over all things?", as a badal (substitute) from «ربك» according to the position — and the position is that of the nominative by the consensus of the grammarians; its position may be genitive, according to the wording; and its position may be accusative, with the meaning "because He is a witness over all things".

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
أَلا إِنَّهُمْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ: that is, they are in doubt about meeting the punishment they were promised. «ألا» is a word of alerting (tanbīh) by which the truth of what follows it is emphasised. أَلا إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطٌ: that is, He encompasses it in knowledge, of what is witnessed and what is unseen. The implied order is: «محيط بكلّ شيء» (encompassing all things), Mighty and Majestic is He.
He said: in the original [manuscript]: Here ends the eleventh part of the parts of «إعراب القرآن» (The Iʿrāb of the Qurʾān), whose compilation, clarification and explanation were undertaken by Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Naḥḥās, may Allah have mercy on him; and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed: ﴿وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلاَ أَبْصَارُكُمْ وَلاَ جُلُودُكُمْ﴾ [Verses 22 to 24].
Bahz ibn Ḥakīm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ
concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿أَن يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلاَ أَبْصَارُكُمْ وَلاَ جُلُودُكُمْ﴾ that he said: "You will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection with your mouths muzzled by a muzzle (fidām), and the first thing that will speak out for a person is his thigh and his palm."

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمْ أَرْدَاكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلُخَاسِرِينَ﴾.
That is, when you thought that He does not hear you.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: Allah said, "I am as My servant thinks of Me…" And the meaning of ﴿أرداكم﴾ is: it destroyed you.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِن يَصْبِرُواْ فَٱلنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُعْتَبِينَ﴾.
But the Fire is an abode for them whether they are patient or not? There are two answers to this:
One of them is that the meaning is: if they are patient in this world in the deeds of the people of
the Fire — as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ — then the Fire is an abode
for them; ﴿وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ﴾ in the Fire.
And it was said: ﴿وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ﴾ in this world, while they persist in their disbelief.
The other answer: whether they are patient in the Fire or impatient, the Fire is an abode
for them; and His saying ﴿وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ﴾ indicates impatience (jazaʿ), because
the one who seeks to be pardoned (al-mustaʿtib) is impatient.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنَا لَهُمْ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: meaning the devils.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of "qayyaḍtu lahu such-and-such" is: I brought it about for him, from where
he does not expect it.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
That is, the sins they commit; ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾: and what they have resolved
to do.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لاَ تَسْمَعُواْ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾.
ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿والْغُوا﴾ with a ḍamma on the ghayn.
Al-Kisāʾī reported: laghā yalghū, and on this basis ﴿وَالْغُوا فِيهِ﴾.
And he reported: laghā yalghā, and laghiya yalghā; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) on this basis is maqṣūr (ending in short alif).
Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
When the Prophet ﷺ was in Mecca and recited, he would raise his voice, and Quraysh would drive people away from him, saying: ﴿لاَ تَسْمَعُواْ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ﴾. And when
he lowered his voice in recitation, those who wished to hear could not hear, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ
بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا، وابْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾:
He said: with whistling, clapping and creating confusion for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he recited; Quraysh used to do that.
Abū Jaʿfar said: laghw in the language is that which has no known reality and whose meaning
does not amount to anything; so the meaning of ﴿وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾ is: oppose it with idle noise (laghw).

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ﴾.
The meaning is: that severe punishment is the recompense of the enemies of Allah; then He explained the recompense,
saying: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ﴾.
The Fire is itself the abode of eternity, and the Arabs do this for emphasis (tawkīd), as
the poet said:
أَخُو رَغَائِبَ يُعْطِيهَا وَيُسْأَلُهَا * يَأْبَى الظُّلاَمَةَ مِنْهُ النَّوْفَلُ الزُّفَرُ
(A man of great gifts, who gives them and is asked for them; the generous one, the bearer of burdens in him refuses injustice.)
And he is he [i.e. the one described is the same person], just as it is said to you: "In this house there is a spacious dwelling," and it is the dwelling itself.
This is not permitted according to the Kufans unless the wording of the second differs from the wording of
the first; according to their view you do not say: "In this house there is a fine house," meaning that the second is
the first. According to the Basrans all of it is good.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ أَعْدَاءِ اللهِ النَّارُ دَارُ الخُلْدِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَال الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلاَّنَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِنَا﴾.
Ḥabba al-ʿUranī and ʿUqba al-Fazārī said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib,
peace be upon him, was asked about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلاَّنَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ﴾, and he said: They are Iblīs, the chief of the devils, and the son of Adam who killed his brother. The same was narrated from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: they said "There is no god but Allah" and then remained upright.
It is narrated that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said to them: What is the meaning of ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾? They said: They did not disobey Allah. He said: You have made the matter hard; it is only
that they remained upright in not associating anything with Allah.
And Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾: they did not associate partners.
Al-Zuhrī said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾ in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and did not dodge about as the fox dodges.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾, he said: in obedience to Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Be upright, and you will never
be able to do it fully (lan tuḥṣū)," that is, be upright in the command of Allah and obedience to Him.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ أَلاَّ تَخَافُواْ وَلاَ تَحْزَنُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ﴾ at death, saying: do not
fear and do not grieve.
Sufyān narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Do not fear the punishment that lies ahead of you,
and do not grieve over your dependants and your estates that you leave behind, for
you have been succeeded in them by good.
And in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ المَلاَئِكَةُ لاَ تَخَافُوا وَلاَ تَحْزَنُوا وَأبْشِرُوا بالجَنَّةِ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ تُوْعَدُونَ﴾.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: This is said to them at death.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
The position of al-Ḥasan is that it is general, for all the believers.
Hushaym narrated from ʿAwf, from Ibn Sīrīn, concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾, that he said: That is the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. he called to the oneness of Allah.
Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ said: ʿĀʾisha said: It was revealed about the muezzins:
﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً﴾.
Abū al-Zāhiriyya said: ʿĀʾisha said: I hope that
the muezzins are the ones about whom Allah said ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَوِي ٱلْحَسَنَةُ وَلاَ ٱلسَّيِّئَةُ﴾.
﴿لا﴾ is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid said: you say when you meet him: Peace be upon you.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾:
He said: They are two men exchanging words, and one of them says to the other: "You so-and-so!"
and the other says to him: "If you are truthful about me, then may Allah forgive me; and if you are lying, then may Allah forgive you."
And Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya, from
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾. He said:
"Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commanded the believers to be patient at times of anger, and to be forbearing and pardoning
when wronged; if they do that, Allah protects them from the devil, and their enemy submits
to them as though he were a devoted friend."

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَآ إِلاَّ ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
He said, meaning: those for whom Allah has prepared Paradise.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿كأنه وَليٌّ حَمِيمٌ﴾, he said: a relative.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ﴾.
That is, none is granted this deed except those who restrain their anger; ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَآ إِلاَّ ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ﴾, that is, of good.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: The great portion is Paradise.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, if the devil confronts you to turn you away from forbearance, then seek refuge in Allah
from him, and be forbearing.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ ٱللَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ لاَ تَسْجُدُواْ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلاَ لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾.
That is, among His signs which point to His power and His oneness are ﴿ٱللَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ لاَ تَسْجُدُواْ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلاَ لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and prostrate to Allah who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon.
And it is possible that the pronoun refers back to the sun and the moon, because
two are [treated as] a plural.
And it is possible that it refers back to the sense of "the signs".

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِنِ ٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ فَٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ يُسَبِّحُونَ لَهُ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَهُمْ لاَ يَسْأَمُونَ﴾.
That is, if they are too proud to affirm the oneness of Allah and to follow you, ﴿فَٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is, then the angels who are with your Lord ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ لَهُ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَهُمْ لاَ يَسْأَمُونَ﴾, that is, they do not grow weary.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He added further proof for them, saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى ٱلأَرْضَ خَاشِعَةً﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, dusty and crumbled.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿اهْتَزَّتْ﴾, that is, with plants.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is said "ihtazza al-insān", i.e. he moved; and from this is the poet's saying:
تَرَاهُ كَنَصْلِ السَّيْفِ يَهْتَزُّ لِلْنَّدَى * إذَا لَمْ تَجِدْ عِندَ امْرِئِ السَّوْءِ مَطْمَعاً
(You see him like a sword-blade, stirring to generosity, when you find nothing to hope for with a wicked man.)
Then He said: ﴿وَرَبَتْ﴾. Mujāhid said: that is, it rose up in order to sprout.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" and Khālid read
﴿وَرَبَأَتْ﴾, meaning: it grew great, from al-rabīʾa (the lookout).

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا لاَ يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنَآ﴾.
Mujāhid said: the whistling and what was mentioned along with it.
Qatāda said: ilḥād is denial.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of ilḥād is turning away from a thing and deviating from it; and from it comes laḥd (the niche-grave), because it is at the side of the grave.
So the meaning of "he committed ilḥād in the signs of Allah" is: he deviated from the truth in them, i.e. he made them bear
other than their meaning.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَفَمَن يُلْقَىٰ فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَيْرٌ أَم مَّن يَأْتِيۤ آمِناً يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
﴿أَفَمَن يُلْقَىٰ فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾ is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām; ﴿خَيْرٌ أَم مَّن يَأْتِيۤ آمِناً يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾ is ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir.
Then He said ﴿ٱعْمَلُواْ مَا شِئْتُمْ﴾, and He, Majestic and Mighty, has made that clear.
Mujāhid said: This is by way of threat.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, the Qurʾān.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning the khabar (predicate) there are two views:
One of them: that the meaning is: Those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them — those are called from a far place.
The other view: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. "they perished".
This view is the preferred one with all the grammarians, as far as I know.
And His saying ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾: that is, overpowering; no one is able to
produce the like of it.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلاَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
a- Among the best of them is that the meaning is: the devil does not come to it from before it so as to take away from it, nor from behind it so as to add to it.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ٱلْبَاطِلُ﴾ is the devil.
Al-Ḥasan said: Allah has protected the Qurʾān from the devil, so he is unable to
add to it or take away from it. Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿إنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكرَ وإنَّا
لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلاَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾: He said: The devil is unable to nullify any
truth in it, nor to establish any falsehood as true in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of "establish any falsehood as true in it" is: add falsehood to it so that it becomes truth; this is one view.
b- And it was said: the meaning of ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾ is: no book before it nullifies it,
and no book comes after it to nullify it. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, i.e. no
falsehood is found in it from either direction.
c- And it was said: the meaning of ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾ is: before its revelation was
complete; ﴿وَلاَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾: after its revelation was complete.
And ﴿مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾ may also be after all of it was revealed, and ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ before its completion.
d- And it was said: the meaning is: falsehood did not come to it before it was revealed, because the prophets had
given glad tidings of it, and the devil was unable to refute that; nor from behind it,
after it was revealed.
e- And it was said: the meaning of ﴿مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلاَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ is for comprehensiveness, i.e. falsehood does not come to it at all.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: that is, of harm.
* And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ﴾, that is, for whoever believes in you;
﴿وَذُو عِقَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾, that is, for whoever denies you.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً أعْجَمِيّاً لَّقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾.
That is, made clear.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The basis of this is that clear exposition (tafṣīl) belongs only to the Arabs, for they are the people of eloquence.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾? [Verse 44].
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: that is, a non-Arabic Qurʾān and an Arab prophet?
Qatāda said: that is, had We made the Qurʾān non-Arabic, they would have rejected that and said: Are Arabs addressed in a foreign tongue? And that would have been a stronger ground for their denial.
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and Abū al-Aswad read ﴿أَعْجَمِيٌّ﴾
without interrogation, with the ʿayn vowelless.
The meaning according to this reading is: Why were its verses not set out in detail, so that some of them were
non-Arabic, understood by the non-Arabs, and some Arabic, understood by the Arabs?
And ﴿أَعْجَمُيٌّ﴾ would be a badal (substitute) for ﴿آيَاتِهِ﴾.
And it is reported that it was read ﴿أَعَجَمِيٌّ﴾?, on the basis that the original is ʿajamī, with the interrogative alif prefixed to it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: al-aʿjamī is the one who does not
speak clearly, whether he is of the Arabs or of the non-Arabs; and al-ʿajamī is the one who is not of
the Arabs, whether he is eloquent or not eloquent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The other reading is far-fetched, because they are agreed on
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً أعْجَمِيّاً﴾!
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ فِيۤ آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾.
﴿وَقْرٌ﴾: that is, deafness, figuratively; and it is blindness for them.
Qatāda said: [it is] the Qurʾān.
And it was said: the deafness (al-waqr) is blindness for them.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Muʿāwiya and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ read ﴿وَهُوَ
عَلَيْهِمْ عَمِيَ﴾, as a past verb.
And ﴿وهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمٍ﴾ is also reported.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
The lexicographers report that it is said to one who understands: "You hear from nearby,"
and it is said to one who does not understand: "You are being called from a far place."
That is, as though he were being called from a place far from him, so he neither hears the call nor understands it.
And the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that they will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their ugliest names, from a far place, so that it is more severe for them in disgrace and reproach.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And the meaning of His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾
is that they have been deferred to a term that Allah knows, and that He does not hasten destruction upon them.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَاتٍ مِّنْ أَكْمَامِهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: when it emerges.
Someone else said: it is the spadix (ṭalʿa) coming out of its husk.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more general, i.e. no fruit comes out of
the sheath in which it was, and that is when it first emerges; and the sheath of everything is its kumm.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِي﴾.
That is, according to your claim.
﴿قَالُوۤاْ آذَنَّاكَ﴾: this is the saying of the gods, i.e. we have informed you.
It is said: "ādhantuhu fa-adhina", i.e. I informed him and he knew; and the root of this is from
al-udhun (the ear), i.e. I put it into his ear; and from it is:
 * "آذَنَتْنَا بِبَيْنِهَا أَسْمَاءُ" *
(Asmāʾ informed us of her departure.)
And from it is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ومِنْهُمُ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ
أُذُنٌ﴾, i.e. do whatever you wish, then apologise for it, for he will excuse you and accept
whatever you tell him. And from it is al-adhān, which is only an announcement of the prayer.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ﴾, that is, there is none of us who testifies that
You have a partner.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَظَنُّواْ مَا لَهُمْ مِّن مَّحِيصٍٍ﴾.
﴿وَظَنُّواْ﴾, that is, and they were certain.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَّ يَسْأَمُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلْخَيْرِ وَإِن مَّسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَيَئُوسٌ قَنُوطٌ﴾.
That is, he does not tire of good befalling him.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿مِنْ دُعَاءٍ بالخَيْرِ﴾.
﴿وَإِن مَّسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ﴾, that is, if some slight evil touches him, he despairs and loses hope.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ هَـٰذَا لِي وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, by my own deeds, and I am deserving of this.
This refers to the disbeliever; do you not see that after it comes ﴿وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةً﴾?
* And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿وَلَئِن رُّجِعْتُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّيۤ﴾, that is, according to what you say.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلإِنسَانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ﴾.
That is, he distanced himself and did not call on Us.
Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" read ﴿أَعْرَضَ وَنَاءَ
بِجَانِبهِ﴾, with the alif before the hamza.
Its meaning may be from "nāʾa", when one rises up [with effort];
or it may be by metathesis of the hamza, with the first meaning.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعَآءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾.
That is, abundant.
It is said: he has broad and long supplication, with one meaning.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي ٱلآفَاقِ وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾.
That is, in the horizons of the world and the changes of its conditions, ﴿وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ﴾ likewise.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي ٱلآفَاقِ﴾ is the conquest of the towns, ﴿وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ﴾
is the conquest of Mecca.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾.
The meaning is: Is it not sufficient for them with your Lord (bi-rabbika), i.e. does your Lord not suffice them, through what He has shown them
of the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that which is sufficient for them, because He is Witness over all
things?
And it is possible that the meaning is: that He has, over everything, a witness that it is
originated (muḥdath), and when He witnesses it He recompenses it.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَآءِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
That is, in doubt.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿فِي مُرْيَةٍ﴾.
﴿أَلاَ إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُّحِيطٌ﴾, that is, He has encompassed knowledge of the unseen and the seen, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حـمۤ تَنزِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾ [verses 1 and 2].
The khabar (predicate), according to the Basrans, is ﴿كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾.
And some of the Kufans said: [the implied form is] "this is a Book."
﴿فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾, i.e. it was sent down in separate parts.
And al-Ḥasan said: it was set out in detail with the threat [of punishment].
And Mujāhid said: ﴿فُصِّلَتْ﴾: it was explained.
And Qatāda said: its lawful and its unlawful, and obedience and disobedience, were made clear.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾, i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the state of being gathered together.
﴿لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, i.e. for whoever knows Arabic.
﴿بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ قُلُوبُنَا فِيۤ أَكِنَّةٍ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَا إِلَيْهِ﴾.
That is, in coverings, i.e. they do not take in what you say.
And al-waqr is deafness.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ فَٱعْمَلْ إِنَّنَا عَامِلُونَ﴾.
﴿حِجَابٌ﴾, i.e. a barrier.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Saʿīd, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd from his father from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām — the two of them said, and this is the sense of their words: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, began by creating the earths on Sunday; He created seven earths on Sunday and Monday.
Then ﴿جَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ مِنْ فَوْقِهَا وَبَارَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَا أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾: He anchored the mountains, split open the rivers, planted the trees and set the benefits in two days, Tuesday and Wednesday.
﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إلى السَّمَاءِ﴾, and He created it as seven heavens on Thursday and Friday.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: that is why it was named "the day of gathering" (yawm al-jumuʿa), because creation was gathered together in it.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: He completed them as seven heavens in the last hour of Friday, then created Ādam in it in haste, and it is the hour in which the Resurrection will take place.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿وَبَارَكَ فِيهَا﴾ according to the view of the two of them is: He split open its rivers and planted its trees.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿بَارَكَ فِيهَا﴾ is: He made provisions abundant in it.
And it is said: its meaning is as one says bāraktu ʿalayhi, i.e. I said: "may you be blessed."
[Translator's note: the commentary on verses 9–10 is included here under 41:5 as in the source.]

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
ʿIkrima said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾:
He placed Yemeni [cloth] in Yemen and Sābirī [cloth] in Sābūr.
Abū Jaʿfar said: so the meaning on this [view] is: He placed in it that by which people make a living and in which they trade.
And it is said: ﴿أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾ is what is taken as sustenance and eaten.
And the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Salām admits both meanings; and Allah knows best.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيۤ أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ سَوَآءً لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: in the completion of four days.
﴿سَوَاءً﴾, i.e. they were equal, an equalling [Translator's note: i.e. a maṣdar used as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].
And al-Farrāʾ said: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾, [i.e. He ordained them] equally.
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿سَوَاءٍ﴾ in the genitive, i.e. in four days, equal and complete.
And by the first chain, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ﴾: he said: whoever asks you, saying: "In how many [days] did Allah create the heavens and the earth?", say to him: "In this."
Abū Jaʿfar said: so the meaning on this view is: as an answer to those who ask.
And there is another view on it, namely that the meaning is: He ordained its provisions in it for those who ask, i.e. for the needy, i.e. for whoever asks, because people ask for their provisions; this is the position of Ibn Zayd. He said: He ordained that according to the measure of their requests; He knew that.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
It indicates that the creation of the heaven was after the creation of the earth; yet He said in another place ﴿والأرضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾?
There are several answers to this:
Hārūn ibn ʿAntara narrated from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah created the earth first, then created the heaven, then spread out the earth and the water after that. He said: "daḥā" means spread out.
And it is said: the meaning is: "then I inform you of this", as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, and this is frequent in the Qurʾān.
And it is said: ﴿ثمَّ﴾ here is in the sense of wāw; and this is neither sound nor permissible.
And the two [other] answers are good and fine.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ﴾.
There are several answers on this:
a- Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, placed in them [a faculty] by which they discern and answer what is said to them.
b- And Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is a report about the state [they were in], i.e. they became in the state of one who says [this]; i.e. it is as the poet said: "The cistern filled up and said: qaṭnī."
That is, "enough for me", i.e. it came to be in the state of one who says [so].
And it is said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed us in terms of what we know about the speed of answering; and we know that nothing is quicker than when a person is told: "Do it", and he says: "I have done it."
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed about the heavens and the earth answering His command, Mighty and Majestic is He.
As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿طَآئِعِينَ﴾, and not saying "ṭāʾiʿāt" (feminine plural), al-Farrāʾ said about it: its meaning is: "we have come, with whoever is in us, obedient."
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best on this — and it is the position of the eminent grammarians — is that since He, Mighty and Majestic is He, reported about them with the actions of rational beings, He brought for them [the form] that belongs to rational beings, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾.
As for al-Kisāʾī, he permitted pluralising anything with wāw and nūn and with yāʾ and nūn; and this is not to be paid attention to.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾.
﴿فَقَضَاهُنَّ﴾, i.e. He perfected them, as the poet said:
وَعَلَيْهِمَا مَسْرُودَتَانِ قَضَاهُمَا * دَاوُدُ، أَوْ صَنَعُ السَّوَابِغ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them are two coats of linked mail which Dāwūd perfected, or Tubbaʿ, skilled in ample mail.)
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمْرَهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: what He commanded and what He willed.
And Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: He created its sun, its moon, its stars and its orbits.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the two views are close; and it is as if the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: and He revealed in every heaven to the angels what He willed of its affair.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَحِفْظاً﴾.
That is: and We guarded it, a guarding, from the devils by means of the stars.
And the meaning [Translator's note: of the passage beginning ﴿قُلْ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾ in verse 9] is: Do you indeed disbelieve in One whose power is this, and set up equals to Him from what you carve with your hands?

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُواْ فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً مِّثْلَ صَاعِقَةِ عَادٍ وَثَمُودَ﴾.
That is: if they turn away from the affirmation of oneness and what you have brought, ﴿فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً مِّثْلَ صَاعِقَةِ عَادٍ وَثَمُودَ﴾, i.e. I have warned you that a punishment will descend upon you as it descended upon them.
﴿إذْ جَاءَتْهُمُ الرُّسُلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ means those who came before them, as He the Exalted said: ﴿مُصَدِّقاً لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Then He said ﴿ومِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾; there are two views on it:
One of them: that the meaning is: and after their existence.
And the other view: that the pronoun refers back to the messengers.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: of intensely hot blasts.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: cold.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's view is clearer, and so said ʿAṭāʾ, because ﴿صَرْصَراً﴾ is taken from ṣirr, and al-ṣirr in the speech of the Arabs is cold, as the poet said:
لَهَا غُدُرٌ كَقُرُونِ النِّسَا * ءِ رُكِّبْنَ فِي يَوْمِ رِيحٍ وَصِرّ
(She has plaits like women's tresses, set in place on a day of wind and bitter cold.)
And the two views are not contradictory, because it is narrated that it was a cold wind that burned as fire burns.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿صَرْصَرٌ﴾ is loud-sounding and tempestuous.
And it has been narrated from Mujāhid: of intense ill omen.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, ill-omened.
And Qatāda said: ill-omened and wretched.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَٱسْتَحَبُّواْ ٱلْعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: We made [it] clear to them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We made clear to them good and evil; He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿إنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ. إمَّا شَاكِراً وإمَّا كَفُوراً﴾, and as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: [the two highways are] good and evil.
And ﴿الهُونُ﴾ is humiliation.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أَعْدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾.
Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Abū Razīn, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, the first of them are held back for the last of them.
Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said: and when the number is complete, it begins with the greatest, then the next greatest, in crime.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says wazaʿahu, yaziʿuhu and yazaʿuhu when he restrained him; and from it is [the saying]: "What the ruler restrains is more than what the Qurʾān restrains", and from it: "People must have restrainers (wazaʿa)."

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصَارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the skin here — and Allah knows best — is the male organ, alluded to by a euphemism, as He the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الغَائِطِ﴾, and al-ghāʾiṭ is the open ground.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and others said: it is the skin itself.
And Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: the hypocrite will dispute at the Balance, rejecting the truth and claiming falsehood; then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will be made to speak, and they will testify against him; then he will be released, and he will say: Away with you and perdition! It was only on your behalf that I was disputing.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمْ عَلَيْنَا قَالُوۤاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
This is the end of the statement (tamām al-kalām).
Then He said: ﴿وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ﴾: he said: you were guarding yourselves.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: you were not concealing yourselves [for fear] that your hearing would testify against you.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: I was hiding behind the coverings of the Kaʿba, and there came a man of Thaqīf and two men of Quraysh, with much fat on their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. They talked among themselves, and one of them said: Do you think Allah hears what we say? The other two said: He hears us when we speak aloud, and does not hear us when we speak low. And the other said: If He hears us when we speak aloud, then He hears us when we speak low.

safi-cedvel:49-51.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative particle. (من دعاء) attached to (يسأم). (الواو) conjunction. (مسّه) a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الفاء) connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (يئوس) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" (he). (قنوط) a second khabar, nominative; it is for emphasis (tawkīd).
The clause «لا يسأم الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «مسّه الشّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «لا يسأم». The clause «(هو) يئوس ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, joined by the فاء.
50- (الواو) is a conjunction in the four places. (اللام) is the lām that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). (إن) a particle of jussive conditional. (أذقناه) like (مسّه). (منّا) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (رحمة). (من بعد) attached to (أذقناه). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (يقولّن) an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; the agent (fāʿil) is "he" (latent). (لي) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هذا). (ما) negative. (لئن) like the first. (التاء) in (رجعت) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Translator's note: the source says nāʾib al-fāʿil here, although (رجعت) is active, so the تاء is the fāʿil], and it is like (مسّه). (إلى ربّي) attached to (رجعت). (لي) attached to the fronted khabar of inna. (عنده) an accusative adverbial (ẓarf) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الحسنى). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (الحسنى) ism (subject) of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa. (الفاء) connects the apodosis of an implied condition. (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (ننبّئنّ) like (يقولّن). (ما) a maṣdar particle
, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (ننبّئنّ). [Translator's note: the source text has a stray closing quotation mark after «حرف مصدري» and a line break at this point; it is kept as it stands.]
(لنذيقنّهم) like (لننبّئنّ). (من عذاب) attached to (نذيقنّهم). The clause «أذقناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «مسّه الشرّ». The clause «مسّته ... » is in the position of the genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of (ضرّاء). The clause «يقولّن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «هذا لي ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «ما أظنّ الساعة قائمة» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of the saying. The clause «رجعت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «أذقناه».
The clause «إنّ لي عنده للحسنى» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «ننبّئنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath. The implied oath clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if the Hour comes to pass, We shall surely inform those who disbelieved ...".
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما) (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī). The clause «لنذيقنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «لننبّئنّ ...».
51- (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (على الإنسان) attached to (أنعمنا). (بجانبه) attached to (نأى), and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya). (إذا مسّه الشرّ فذو..) is like «إن مسّه الشرّ فيئوس».
The clause «أنعمنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement).
The clause «أعرض ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «نأى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «أعرض». The clause «مسّه الشرّ ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «(هو) ذو ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(قنوط): an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) of the active participle of the triliteral verb قنط; its wazn is فعول with fatḥa on the فاء.
(نأى): it has an ʿilāl (weakening) by substitution; its origin is نأي, with a ياء at the end; its maṣdar is النأي. The ياء was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into an alif. (عريض): a muśabbaha adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha, assimilated adjective) from the triliteral عرض, of the pattern (bāb) كرم; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
The makniyya takhyīliyya metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya, an implicit, imaginative metaphor): in the saying of the Exalted «فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ».
«عريض» means: abundant and continuous, borrowed from what has wide breadth. Its origin is from what bodies are described by; it is the shorter of the two extensions, and by convention "broad" is understood as spaciousness. The intensive form and the tanwīn of multiplicity strengthen this. Naturally, the metaphor of breadth is more eloquent than the metaphor of length, because if its breadth is such, what do you think of its length? Here supplication is likened to something described as having extension, and then breadth is affirmed for it.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the mubtadaʾ..
1- The omission of the mubtadaʾ is frequent in the answer to a question, as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ؟ نارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ» that is, "it is the Fire of Allah"; «وَأَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ ما أَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ؟ فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ» that is, "they are among thornless lote trees".
2- After the fāʾ of the apodosis, as in the saying of the Exalted: «مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها» that is, "his deed is for himself and his wrongdoing is against himself". Likewise in the verse we are now treating: «وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَيَؤُسٌ قَنُوطٌ» that is, "then he is despairing, hopeless".
3- After the saying (al-qawl), as in the saying of the Exalted: «قالُوا: أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ» that is:
"they are tales of the ancients".
4- After a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is, in meaning, an adjective of it, as in the saying of the Exalted: «التَّائِبُونَ الْعابِدُونَ» that is, "they are the repentant". So (التائبون) is the khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ (هم) in terms of i'rab, whereas in meaning it is an adjective of it. Likewise «صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ» that is, "they are deaf".
5- It has also occurred elsewhere, as in the saying of the Exalted: «لا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي الْبِلادِ مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ» that is, "their moving about is a little enjoyment"; and «لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ» that is, "this is a message"; and «سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْناها» that is, "this is a sūra which We have sent down".

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(أرأيتم) means "tell me"; the first object is omitted, its implied form being "أنفسكم" (yourselves). (كان) an incomplete past verb (kāna), in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its ism is a latent pronoun referring to the Qur'an, understood from the context. (من عند) attached to the khabar of kāna. (به) attached to (كفرتم). (من) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (أضلّ). (ممّن) attached to (أضلّ). (في شقاق) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أرأيتم ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «إن كان من عند ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the nominal clause after it, that is: "then you are the most astray" or "then no one is more astray than you". The clause «كفرتم به ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «كان».
The clause «من أضلّ ... » is in the position of the accusative, the second direct object, whose governor is (أرأيتم). The clause «هو في شقاق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(في الآفاق) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (آياتنا), and likewise (في أنفسهم), which is conjoined to the first. (حتّى) a particle of limit and genitive. (يتبيّن) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى. (لهم) attached to (يتبيّن)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتبيّن..) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to (نريهم). The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه الحقّ..) is in the position of the nominative, the fāʿil (agent) of (يتبيّن). (الهمزة) is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī). (الواو) conjunction. (ربّك) genitive in form by the باء, accusative in position, the object of (يكف). [Note: It is possible that it is the agent, nominative in position, with the interpreted maṣdar after it a substitute (badal) of it, or in the position of the genitive by an omitted باء, that is: "Does your Lord not suffice them, in that He is witness over everything".] (على كلّ) attached to (شهيد), the khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه على كلّ شيء شهيد) is in the position of the nominative, the fāʿil of (يكفى). The clause «سنريهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. The clause «يتبيّن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يكف بربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, that is: "Does your Lord not suffice them and avail them, in that ...".

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) a particle of alerting. (في مرية) attached to the khabar of inna. (من لقاء) attached to (مرية). (ألا) like the first. (بكلّ) attached to (محيط).
The clause «إنّهم في مرية ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّه بكلّ شيء محيط» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(53) (الآفاق): plural of (الأفق), meaning a region; its wazn is فعل with two ḍammas. The madda in (الآفاق) was originally two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second with sukūn, on the wazn أفعال, that is أأفاق..
(يكف): ʿilāl by deletion, for the sake of conformity with the jussive; it is a defective verb (muʿtall nāqiṣ), jussive after (لم); its wazn is يفع.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {تَنزِيلٌ}: It may be the khabar (predicate) of «حم» on the view that it is a name of the sūra; or the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a revelation"; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «كتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ».

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كِتَابٌ}: It has preceded that it may be the khabar (predicate) of «تَنْزيل»; it may be a second predicate; it may be a badal (substitute) for «تَنْزيل»; and it may be a fāʿil (agent) of the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely «تنزيلٌ», i.e. "a Book has been sent down" — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. And «فُصِّلَتْ آياتُه» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «كتاب».
His saying: «قُرْآناً»: There are six aspects in its accusative. First: it is itself a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «عربيَّاً» is its adjective. [Second:] or it is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), the ḥāl in reality being «عربيَّاً», and it is a non-transitory ḥāl; the possessor of the ḥāl is either «كتابٌ», because it is described by «فُصِّلَتْ», or «آياته». [Third:] or it is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "you recite it as a recitation." [Fourth:] or by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) and praise. [Fifth:] or it is a second object of «فُصِّلَتْ». [Sixth:] or it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We have set it out in detail as a Qurʾān."
His saying: «لقومٍ»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is attached to «فُصِّلَتْ», i.e. it has been set out in detail for these people and made clear to them, because they are the ones who benefit from it, even if it is in itself set out in detail for all people. Second: it is attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «قُرآناً», i.e. "being for these people in particular," for what has preceded regarding the meaning. Third: it is attached to «تَنْزِيلٌ»; this is when «من الرحمنِ» is not made an adjective of it, because if you make «من الرحمن» its adjective you will have made a described maṣdar govern; and when «كتابٌ» is neither a predicate of it nor a substitute for it, lest it entail predicating about the mawṣūl (the governing maṣdar, treated like a relative) or substituting for it before its ṣila is complete. Whoever is lenient with the adverbial and its equivalent (the prepositional phrase) pays no attention to any of that. As for when you make «من الرحمن» attached to it and «كتاب» its agent, that does no harm, because it is among its complements and not something extraneous. This passage is among those that display the beauty of the science of iʿrab and train you in many of its chapters.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً}: They may be two naʿts (adjectives) of «قُرْآناً», and they may be two ḥāls (circumstantials), either from «كتاب», or from «آياته», or from the pronoun intended in «قُرْآناً». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read both in the nominative, as adjectives of «كتاب», or as the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a bearer of good tidings and a warner."

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {في أَكِنَّةٍ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said 'on our hearts are coverings,' as it was said 'and in our ears is deafness,' so that the speech would be in one pattern? I say: it is in one pattern, because there is no difference in meaning between your saying 'our hearts are in coverings' and 'on our hearts are coverings'; the proof of this is His saying, Exalted is He: {وَجَعَلْنَا على قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً} [al-Anʿām: 25]; had it been said 'We have put their hearts in coverings,' the meaning would not have differed. And you see that those of them with natural talent do not regard correspondence and attentiveness except in meanings." The Shaykh said: "«في» here is more forceful than «على», because they intended an excess in non-acceptance through their hearts being in coverings that enclose them as a container encloses its contents, so that nothing can reach them, as you say 'the money is in the purse,' unlike your saying 'on the money is a purse,' which does not indicate enclosure and non-access the way a container does. As for «وجعلنا», it is part of Allah the Exalted's reporting, so it does not need exaggeration." The explanation of «الأَكنَّة» and «الوقر» has preceded.
Ṭalḥa read it with kasra on the wāw [«وِقْر»], and the difference between the two has preceded.
His saying: «ممَّا تَدْعُوْنا»: «مِنْ» in «ممَّا» and in «ومِنْ بَيْنِنا» is for the beginning of the extent. So the meaning is that the veil begins from us and begins from you, so the intervening distance between our side and your side is completely filled, with no gap in it. Had «مِنْ» not come, the meaning would be that a veil exists in the middle between the two sides, whereas the intent is exaggeration by excessive separation; for that reason «مِنْ» was brought — so said al-Zamakhsharī. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: in coverings veiled from hearing what you call us to. It is not permissible for it to be an adjective of «أكنَّة», because the coverings are veils, and veils are not among what they are called to."

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {قُلْ}: Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read «قال», a past verb, as a report about the Messenger. The written form allows both, and the like of this has preceded in al-Anbiyāʾ and at the end of al-Muʾminūn. Al-Aʿmash and al-Nakhaʿī read «يُوْحِي» with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. [the agent being] Allah the Exalted.
His saying: «فاسْتَقِيموا إليه»: It is made transitive with «إلى» because it implies the meaning of "turn yourselves," and the meaning is: direct your uprightness towards Him.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ}: It has been said: not diminished; they cited for Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī:
3946 - إني لَعَمْرُكَ ما بابي بذي غَلقٍ ... على الصديقِ ولا خَيْري بمَمْنُوْنِ
(By your life, my door is not locked against a friend, nor is my bounty diminished.)
It has been said: cut off, from «مَنَنْتُ الحَبْلَ», i.e. I cut the rope; they cited:
3947 - فَضْلَ الجوادِ على الخيلِ البِطاءِ فلا ... يُعْطِي بذلك مَمْنُوْناً ولا نَزِقا
(The excellence of the swift steed over slow horses: in that he gives [a run] neither cut short nor rash.)
And it has been said: «غيرُ ممنونٍ» is from al-mann (reproachful reminding of a favour), because Allah the Exalted's giving is not reproached with reminders; only a created being reminds of his favours.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَتَجْعَلُونَ}: It is conjoined to «لَتَكْفُرون», so it falls within the scope of the interrogation.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلَ}: It is resumptive. It is not permissible to conjoin it to the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, because of the separation between them by something extraneous, namely His saying «وتَجْعلون», which is conjoined to «لَتَكْفرون», as has preceded.
His saying: {في أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ}: Its implied form is: in the completion of four days, together with the two preceding days.
Al-Zajjāj said: "in the completion of four days," meaning by the completion the two days. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«في أربعة أيام» is a summing-up of the duration of Allah's creating the earth and what is in it, as if He said: all of that in four complete, even days, without increase or decrease." I say: this is like your saying "I built my house in one day and completed it in two days," i.e. including the first. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. in the completion of four days; were it not for this implied form, the days would be eight: two days in the first, namely His saying {خَلَقَ الأرض فِي يَوْمَيْنِ}, two days in the last, namely His saying {فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ}, [and four in the middle, namely His saying {في أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ}]."
His saying: «سواءً»: The majority read it in the accusative, and there are several aspects in it. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "they were made even, an evenness" — so said Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the «ها» in «أقواتها», or from the «ها» in «فيها» referring to the earth, or from the earth — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ.
This is questionable, because the meaning is only the description of the days as being even, not the description of the earth as such, and the exegesis came on this basis. This is indicated by the reading «سَواءٍ» in the genitive as an adjective of the muḍāf or the muḍāf ilayhi. Al-Suddī and Qatāda said: «سواءً» means: equal for whoever asks about the matter and inquires about the reality of its occurrence and seeks a lesson in it, for he will find it as Allah the Exalted said. However, Ibn Zayd and a group said something close to the meaning Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, for they said: its meaning is that the matter of these created things and their benefit is even and prepared for those of mankind who need them; so He expressed "those seeking" by "those asking."
Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, Yaʿqūb and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «سَواءٍ» in the genitive, according to what has preceded, and Abū Jaʿfar in the nominative. There are two aspects in it. First: it is the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are even, neither increasing nor decreasing." Makkī said: "It is nominative as a mubtadaʾ," with its predicate being «للسائلين». This is questionable, in that it begins with an indefinite noun without a justifying factor. Then he said: "in the sense of 'even ones,' for whoever asked, saying: in how many [days] was it created? And it has been said: «للسَّائلين» means for all creatures, because they ask for provision and other things from Allah the Exalted."
His saying: «للسَّائلين»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is attached to «سواء», in the sense of "even for those who ask." Second: it is attached to «قَدَّر», i.e. He determined its provisions in it for the sake of those who seek them, who need them and are nourished. Third: it is attached to an omitted [word], as if it were said: this limitation is for the sake of whoever asked: in how many [days] were the earth and what is in it created?

semin-durr:11-11.t:
Al-dukhān (smoke) is what rises from the flame of fire, and it is borrowed for the vapour seen [rising] from the earth in its drought. Its regular plural of paucity is «أَدْخِنة» and of abundance «دِخْنان», as in «غُراب», «أَغْرِبة» and «غِربان»; they deviated in pluralising it as «دواخِن». It has been said: it is the plural of an implied «داخِنة», by way of figurative attribution. Similar to it is «عُثان» and «عَواثِن».
His saying: «وهي دُخانٌ»: of the category of formal simile, because its form is the form of smoke to the eye.
His saying: «أَتَيْنا»: The majority read «ائْتِيا», an imperative from al-ityān (coming), and «قالتا أَتَيْنا» likewise from it. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read «آتِيا قالتا آتَيْنا» with madd in both. There are two aspects in it. First: it is from al-muʾātāh, which is concord, i.e. let each of you two accord with the other in what befits it; to this al-Rāzī and al-Zamakhsharī inclined. So the pattern of «آتِيا» is fāʿilā, like «قاتِلا», and the pattern of «آتَيْنا» is fāʿalnā, like «قاتَلْنا». Second: it is from al-īṭāʾ in the sense of giving, so the pattern of «آتِيا» is afʿilā, like «أَكْرِما», and the pattern of «آتَيْنا» is afʿalnā, like «أَكْرَمْنا». On the first, an object has been omitted; on the second, two objects have been omitted, since the implied form is: "give obedience from yourselves to the One who commanded you." They said: "we have given Him obedience."
Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī rejected the second aspect, saying: "«آتَيْنا» with madd is on the pattern fāʿalnā from al-muʾātāh, in the sense of 'we hastened,' with the direct object omitted; it is not from al-īṭāʾ, which is giving, because of the far-fetchedness of omitting both its objects." I say: this is what prevented al-Zamakhsharī from making it from al-īṭāʾ.
His saying: «طَوْعاً أو كَرْهاً»: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "obedient or compelled." Al-Aʿmash read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma. The discussion of that has preceded in al-Nisāʾ.
His saying: «قالتا»: i.e. the heaven and the earth said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He meant the two mentioned groups; He made the heavens one heaven and the earths one earth, and it is like the poet's saying:
3948 - ألم يُحْزِنْكَ أنَّ حبالَ قومي ... وقومِك قد تبايَنَتا انْقِطاعا
(Does it not grieve you that the ropes of my people and of your people have parted, severed?)
He expressed them with «تَباينتا» (dual)." The Shaykh said: "It is not as he mentioned, because only the earth in the singular and the heaven in the singular had been mentioned before, so the dual expression was good. As for the verse, it is as if he said 'the two ropes of my people and your people,' and he made «تبايَنَتا» feminine according to the meaning, because by the ropes he meant affection."
His saying: «طائِعِين»: Regarding its coming in the form of the plural of rational masculines there are two aspects. First: what is meant is "the two came with the rational beings and others in them," so He gave precedence to the rational over others; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. Second: since He treated them as rational beings in reporting about them and commanding them, they were pluralised as such beings are, as in His saying {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4]. Is this dialogue literal or figurative? And if figurative, is it a representation (tamthīl) or an imaginative figure (takhyīl)? There is disagreement.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {سَبْعَ}: There are four aspects in its accusative. First: it is a second object of «قَضاهُنَّ», because it is made to imply the meaning of "He made them, by His decree, seven heavens."
Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «قَضاهُنَّ», i.e. "He fashioned them numbered," with «قضى» in the sense of "made," as in the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
3949 - وعليهما مَسْرُوْدتان قَضاهما ... داوُدُ أو صَنَعُ السَّوابغِ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them were two coats of riveted mail that David fashioned, or Tubbaʿ, skilled maker of ample mail.)
i.e. made them. Third: it is a tamyīz (specification). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that [the pronoun] is a vague pronoun explained by «سبع سماوات» [as a specification]"; by "vague" he means that it does not refer back to «السماء» either in wording or in meaning, unlike its being a ḥāl or a second object. Fourth: it is a badal (substitute) for «هُنَّ» in «فقَضاهُنَّ» — so said Makkī. He also said: "«السَّماء» is masculine and feminine; the Qurʾān came with the feminine, and had it come with the masculine it would have been said «سبعة سماوات»." The verification of its masculine and feminine has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: «وحِفْظاً»: There are two aspects in its accusative. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "and We guarded it with the piercing stars, a guarding." Second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) according to the meaning, for the implied form is: "We created the stars as adornment and as protection." The Shaykh said: "This is strained and a departure from what is easy and clear."

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُواْ}: an iltifāt (shift of person) from addressing them in His saying «قل أئِنَّكم» to the third person: because they committed turning away, He turned away from addressing them; and this is a fine congruence. The majority read «صاعقَةً مثلَ صاعقةِ» with the alif in both, and Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Sulamī and Ibn Muḥayṣin «صَعْقَةً مثلَ صَعْقة» omitting it with sukūn on the ʿayn. The discussion of that has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. One says «صَعَقَتْه الصاعقةُ فصَعِقَ» (the thunderbolt struck him and he was struck senseless); this is among what comes with faʿaltuhu — with fatḥa — followed by faʿila with kasra; similar to it is «جَدَعْتُه فَجَدِعَ». «الصَّعْقَة» is the single instance.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {إِذْ جَآءَتْهُمُ}: There are several aspects in it. First: it is an adverb of «أَنْذَرْتُكم», as in "I met you when such-and-such was." Second: it is accusative by «صاعقة», because it is in the sense of punishment, i.e. "I have warned you of the punishment that befell at the time their messengers came." Third: it is an adjective of the first «صاعِقَة». Fourth: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the second «صاعقة». Abū al-Baqāʾ stated these two, and both are questionable, since the apparent sense is that the thunderbolt is a body, namely a piece of fire that descends from the sky and burns, as preceded in its explanation at the beginning of this work; so time does not occur as an adjective of it nor as a ḥāl from it, and interpreting it in the sense of punishment takes it out of its denotation without necessity. He made it a description of the first only because it is indefinite, and a ḥāl from the second because it is definite by its annexation to a proper name; had he made it a ḥāl from the first because it is particularised by annexation, it would have been permissible, and so the aspects would become five.
His saying: {مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ}: The apparent sense is that both pronouns refer to ʿĀd and Thamūd. It has been said: the pronoun in «خَلْفِهم» refers to the messengers. This was considered far-fetched in meaning, since the implied form would become: "the messengers came to them from behind the messengers," i.e. from behind themselves. It may be answered that it is of the category of «دِرْهمٌ ونصفُه» ("a dirham and half of it" [meaning half of another]), i.e. and from behind other messengers.
His saying: {أَلاَّ تعبدوا}: Three aspects are possible for «أَنْ». First: it is the lightened form of the heavy [«أنَّ»], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the prohibitive clause after it is the predicate; so the Shaykh parsed it. This is questionable in two respects. First: the lightened form does not occur after a verb except one of the verbs of certainty. Second: the predicate in the chapter of inna and its sisters is not a request; if anything of that sort occurs it is interpreted, and for that reason they interpreted [the poet's saying]:
3950 - إنَّ الذينَ قَتَلْتُمْ أمسِ سَيِّدَهُمْ ... لا تَحْسَبُوا ليلَهم عن ليلِكم ناما
(Those whose chief you killed yesterday — do not think their night has slept away from your night.)
and the other's saying:
3951 - ولو أصابَتْ لقالَتْ وَهْيَ صادِقةٌ ... إنَّ الرِّياضَةَ لا تُنْصِبْكَ للشِّيْبِ
(Had she been right, she would have said, and truthfully: "Exercise — let it not wear you out for grey hair.")
by implying [a verb of] saying.
