Second: it is the particle that puts the imperfect in the accusative, and the prohibitive clause after it is its ṣila, connected with the prohibition as it is connected with the imperative in «كَتبتُ إليه بأنْ قُمْ» ("I wrote to him to stand"); a difficulty has passed regarding connecting it with the imperative, and the like of it arises with the prohibition. Third: it is explicative (mufassira) of their coming, because it implies [a verb of] saying. «لا» in all these aspects is prohibitive; and it may be negating on the second aspect, with the verb accusative by «أنْ» after the negating «لا», for the negating «لا» does not prevent a governing word from governing what follows it, as in «جئتُ بلا زيدٍ» ("I came without Zayd"). Al-Ḥawfī mentioned nothing else.
His saying: «لو شاءَ»: Al-Zamakhsharī implied the object of «شاء» as: "had He willed the sending of messengers, He would have sent down angels." The Shaykh said: "I examined the Qurʾān and the speech of the Arabs, and I did not find the omission of the object of «شاء» occurring after «لو» except when it is of the same kind as its apodosis, as in:
{وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الهدى} [al-Anʿām: 35], i.e. had He willed to gather them upon guidance, He would have gathered them upon it; {لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَاماً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 65]; {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 70]; {وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لآمَنَ} [Yūnus: 99]; {وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ} [al-Anʿām: 112]; {لَوْ شَآءَ الله مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 35]. The poet said:
3952 - فلو شاءَ ربِّي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ خالدٍ ... ولو شاءَ ربي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ مَرْثدِ
(Had my Lord willed, I would have been Qays ibn Khālid; had my Lord willed, I would have been Qays ibn Marthad.)
And the rajaz poet said:
3953 - واللذِ لو شاءَ لكنْتُ صَخْراً ... أو جَبَلاً أشمَّ مُشْمَخِرَّا
(By the One who, had He willed, I would have been a rock, or a lofty, towering mountain.)"
He said: "So according to what has been established, the omitted item is not what al-Zamakhsharī implied; the implied form is only: 'had our Lord willed to send down angels with the message from Him to humans, He would have sent them down with it to them.' This is more forceful in refusing the sending of humans, since they made that conditional on the sending down of angels, and He did not will that, so how would He will it in the case of humans?" I say: Abū al-Qāsim's (al-Zamakhsharī's) implied form is more apt in meaning and freer from putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the implied form [of the Shaykh] becomes: "had He willed to send down angels, He would have sent down angels."
His saying: {بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ}: This is an address to Hūd, Ṣāliḥ and other prophets, peace be upon them, giving precedence to the one addressed over the absent, as in «أنت وزيدٌ تقومان» ("you and Zayd stand"). «ما» may be a relative in the sense of «الذي», its returning pronoun being «به»; or it may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "in your being sent." On this, «به» [refers] to that interpreted maṣdar, and it is of the category of emphasis, as if it were said: "disbelievers in your being sent with it."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {صَرْصَراً}: Al-ṣarṣar is the violent wind. It has been said: it is the cold one, from al-ṣirr, which is cold. It has been said: it is the one of intense scorching heat. And it has been said: it is the sounding one, from «صَرَّ البابُ», i.e. the door's creaking was heard. «الصَّرَّة» is the cry, and from it: {فَأَقْبَلَتِ امرأته فِي صَرَّةٍ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 29]. Ibn Qutayba said: "«صَرْصَر» may be from al-ṣirr, which is cold; or from «صَرَّ البابُ»; or from al-ṣarra, which is the cry, and from it: {فَأَقْبَلَتِ امرأته فِي صَرَّةٍ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 29]." Al-Rāghib said: "«صَرْصَر» is a word from al-ṣirr, and that goes back to tightness, because of the knotting [contraction] in coldness."
His saying: «نَحِساتٍ»: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the rest with sukūn. As for the kasra, it is an adjective on the pattern faʿil, and its verb is faʿila, also with kasra on the ʿayn; one says «نَحِس فهو نَحِسٌ», like «فَرِح فهو فَرِحٌ» and «أَشِرَ فهو أَشِرٌ». Al-Layth transmitted from al-Kisāʾī the imāla of its alif because of the kasra, but that is not well known from him, so that al-Dānī attributed it to error.
As for the reading with sukūn, it allows three aspects. First: it is lightened from faʿil in the preceding reading, and in this there is agreement between the two readings. Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective, like «رجلٍ عَدْلٍ» ("a just man"); but the plural weakens this, for the eloquent usage with a maṣdar used as an adjective is to keep it singular; it seems what permitted the plural is the difference of its kinds originally. Third: it is an independent adjective on the pattern faʿl with sukūn on the ʿayn. But the morphologists did not mention, among adjectives coming from faʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, other than limited patterns, among which there is no faʿl with sukūn; they mentioned: «فَرِحَ فهو فَرِحٌ», «حَوِرَ فهو أحورُ», «شَبعَ فهو شبعانُ», «سَلِمَ فهو سالمٌ» and «بَلي فهو بالٍ».
On the meaning of «نَحِسات» there are two views. First: they are [days] of ill omen. Al-Suddī said: i.e. ill-omened, from the well-known naḥs. Second: they are intensely cold. For the first meaning they cited the poet's saying:
3954 - يَوْمَيْنِ غَيْمَيْنِ ويوماً شَمْسا ... نَجْمَيْنِ سَعْدَيْنِ ونجماً نَحْسا
(Two cloudy days and a sunny day; two auspicious stars and an ill-omened star.)
And for the second meaning the other's saying:
3955 - كأنَّ سُلافَةً عُرِضَتْ لنَحْسٍ ... يُحِيْلُ شَفيفُها الماءَ الزُّلالا
(As if choice wine were exposed to a cold wind whose biting chill turns clear water [to ice].)
And from it:
3956 - قد أَغْتدي قبلَ طُلوعِ الشمسِ ... للصيدِ في يومٍ قليلِ النَّحْسِ
(I set out early before sunrise to hunt, on a day of little naḥs.)
It has been said that in this verse he means dust by it, i.e. of little dust; and it has been said likewise in the verse [of the Qurʾān] that they were days of dust. «نَحِسات» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أيَّام», and the plural with alif and tāʾ is regular in the adjective of what is not rational, as in «أيامٍ معدوداتٍ». Its verification has preceded in al-Baqara.
«لِنُذِيْقَهُمْ» is attached to «أَرْسَلْنا». It has been read «لِتُذِيقَهم» with the upper-dotted tāʾ.
On the pronoun [in this reading] there are two views; the first: it is the wind, i.e. "so that the wind, or the days, might make them taste," figuratively. [Translator's note: the source mentions only the first of the two views.] «عذاب الخِزْيِ» is an annexation of the qualified noun to its quality; for that reason He said {وَلَعَذَابُ الآخرة أخزى}, since it entails sharing [in the quality] plus excess. Attributing disgrace to the punishment is figurative, because it is its cause.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ}: The majority read it in the nominative as a diptote. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb [read it] fully declined, and likewise everything in the Qurʾān except His saying {وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ الناقة} [al-Isrāʾ: 59]; they said: because the written form there is «ثمود» without alif. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Aʿmash in one transmission and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «ثمود» in the accusative, fully declined; and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz and ʿĀṣim also in the accusative as a diptote. As for full declension and its absence, their justification has preceded in Hūd. As for the nominative, it is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause after it as the khabar (predicate), and that is necessary according to the majority, because «أمَّا» is followed only by a mubtadaʾ, so preoccupation (ishtighāl) is not permissible in what follows it except rarely, as in this reading. If you imply the verb that puts it in the accusative, imply it after the accusative noun, i.e. "as for Thamūd, We guided them — We guided them"; they said: because verbs do not follow it.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ}: There are two aspects regarding what governs this adverb. First: an omitted [verb] indicated by what follows, namely His saying «فهم يُوْزَعُون», its implied form being "people are driven on the day ... are gathered"; Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as "they are held back on the day of the gathering." Second: it is accusative by «اذْكُرْ», i.e. "remember the day." Nāfiʿ read «نَحْشُرُ» with the nūn of majesty and ḍamma on the shīn, with «أعداءَ» in the accusative, i.e. "We gather." The rest [read] with the yāʾ of absence with ḍamma and fatḥa on the shīn, as a verb whose agent is not named, with «أعداءُ» nominative as standing in place of the agent. Al-Aʿraj read the shīn of «نَحْشِر» with kasra. «حتى» is the limit of «يُحْشَر».

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {أَن يَشْهَدَ}: Several aspects are possible in it. First: "from [the fact] that [they] bear witness." Second: "for fear that [they] bear witness." Third: "for the sake of [their] bearing witness"; both [the second and third] are in the sense of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Fourth: "from [their] bearing witness," i.e. you could not hold back, and it was not possible for you to hide from your limbs and conceal yourselves from them. Fifth: it is made to imply the meaning of supposing, and that is far-fetched.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ}: There are several aspects in it. First: «ظنُّكم» is its khabar (predicate), «الذي ظَنَنْتُمْ» is its naʿt (adjective), and «أَرْدَاكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» implied with it on the view of the majority, contrary to al-Akhfash. Makkī's rejection of the ḥāl reading because of the absence of «قد» is not granted, for the reason I mentioned. Second: «ظنُّكم» is a badal (substitute) and the relative is its predicate, with «أَرْدَاكم» also a ḥāl. Third: the relative is a second predicate. Fourth: «ظَنُّكم» is a substitute or an explicative apposition (bayān), the relative is the predicate, and «أَرْداكم» is a second predicate. Fifth: «ظَنُّكم», the relative and the clause «أَرْداكم» are [all] predicates. However, the Shaykh rejected al-Zamakhsharī's statement "«ظنُّكم» and «أَرْدَاكم» are two predicates." He said: "Because His saying «وذلكم» points to their earlier supposition, so the implied form becomes: 'your supposition about your Lord that He does not know is your supposition about your Lord'; so from the predicate is gained what is gained from the subject, and that is not permissible. This is parallel to what the grammarians forbade in your saying 'the master of the slave-girl is her owner.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya forbade «أَرْداكم» being a ḥāl because «قد» is absent, and the disagreement about that has preceded.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the second tāʾ, active; and {فَمَا هُم مِّنَ المعتبين} with fatḥa on the tāʾ as a passive participle. Its meaning is: if they seek al-ʿutbā, which is being pleased with [i.e. reconciliation], they are not among those to whom it is granted. It has been said: the meaning is: if they seek the removal of what they are reproached for, they are not among those whose request to remove the reproach is answered.
The origin of al-ʿatab is a place remote [and hard] for one who alights there; from it the threshold of a door and the step are called «عَتَبة». Al-ʿatab is used to express the harshness a person finds in his breast against his companion. «عَتَبْتُ فلاناً» means I showed him harshness, and «أَعْتَبْتُه» means I removed his grievance, like «أَشْكَيْتُه»; and it has been said: I provoked him to reproach.
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «وإن يُسْتَعْتَبوا», passive, and {فَمَا هُم مِّنَ المعتبين} as an active participle, meaning: if they are asked to give satisfaction, they will not do that, because they have left the abode of moral obligation. It has been said its meaning is: if what they are not reproached for is sought, they are not among those who remove the grievance. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
3957 - أَمِنَ المَنُونِ ورَيْبِه تَتَوَجَّعُ ... والدهرُ ليسَ بمُعْتِبٍ مَنْ يَجْزَعُ
(Do you grieve at death and its vicissitudes? Time does not appease one who frets.)

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {وَقَيَّضْنَا}: The origin of al-taqyīḍ is facilitating and preparing. «قَيَّضْتُه له لكذا» means I prepared him and facilitated him. «هذان ثوبان قَيْضان» means each of the two garments is equivalent to the other in price. Al-muqāyaḍa is exchange (barter). His saying {نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً} [al-Zukhruf: 36] means: We make it easy for him to take hold of him as the shell (al-qayḍ) takes hold of the egg. Al-qayḍ originally is the outer shell of the egg.
His saying: «في أُمَمٍ»: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم», the meaning being: "being among the totality of nations." This is like the saying:
3958 - إنْ تَكُ عَنْ أَحْسَنِ الصَّنيعةِ مَأْ ... فُوْكاً ففي آخَرين قد أَفِكُوا
(If you have been turned away from the finest deed, then [you are] among others who were turned away.)
i.e. among a group of other people. It has been said: «في» is in the sense of "with."

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {والغوا}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the ghayn. It allows two aspects. First: it is from «لَغِي» with kasra, «يَلْغَى». In this there are two meanings: one, from «لَغِيَ» when one speaks idle talk (al-laghw), which is that in which there is no benefit; the other, from «لَغِي بكذا», i.e. he threw it, so «في» would be in the sense of the bāʾ, i.e. "throw it and cast it aside." The second of the two original aspects: it is from «لَغا» with fatḥa, «يَلْغَى» also with fatḥa, as al-Akhfash related; its regular form would have been ḍamma, like «غزا يَغْزو», but it was given fatḥa because of the guttural letter. Qatāda, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū al-Sammāl, al-Zaʿfarānī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā read it with ḍamma on the ghayn, from «لَغا» with fatḥa, «يَلْغُو», like «دَعا يَدْعُو». In the ḥadīth: «فقد لَغَوْتَ» ("then you have spoken idly"), and this accords with the reading of other than the majority.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: There are two aspects in it. First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «جزاءُ» is its khabar (predicate). Second: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "the matter is that," and {جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ الله النار} is an independent clause explaining the clause before it.
His saying: «النارُ»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is a badal (substitute) for «جزاء»; this is questionable, since the substitute takes the place of what it substitutes for, so the implied form would become "that is the Fire." Second: it is the predicate of an implied subject. Third: it is a mubtadaʾ, and {لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ} is the khabar. «دارُ» may be nominative as a fāʿil (agent) or as a mubtadaʾ.
His saying {فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ} requires that «دارُ الخلد» be other than the Fire, yet the matter is not so; rather the Fire is itself the abode of eternity. This was answered by saying that a thing may be made a container of itself with respect to what relates to it, by way of exaggeration, as if that related thing became a place of settlement for it; and this is more forceful than attributing the related thing to it by way of predication. Like it is the saying:
3959 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وفي اللَّهِ إنْ لم يُنْصِفُوا حَكَمٌ عَدْلُ
(… and in Allah, if they do not deal fairly, is a just judge.)
and His saying, Exalted is He: {لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ الله أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ} [al-Aḥzāb: 21], while the Messenger, peace be upon him, is himself the example. So they answered. This is questionable, since the apparent sense — and it is a sound, transmitted meaning — is that within the Fire there is an abode called the abode of eternity, with the Fire surrounding it.
His saying: «جَزاءً»: There are three aspects in its accusative. First: it is accusative by an implied verb, being an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense." Second: it is accusative by the maṣdar before it, namely {جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ الله}, a maṣdar being put in the accusative by its like, as in His saying: {فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً} [al-Isrāʾ: 63]. Third: it is accusative as a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). «بما» is attached to the second «جَزاء» if it is not emphasising, and to the first if it is. «بآياتِنا» is attached to «يَجْحَدون».

semin-durr:29-29.t: The disagreement over «أَرِنا» and over the nūn of «اللذَيْنِ» has preceded. Al-Khalīl said: "If you say «أَرِني ثوبَك» with kasra, its meaning is 'let me see it'; and with sukūn, 'give it to me.'" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. for what they used to talk idly," so He mentioned denial (al-juḥūd) because it is the cause of the idle talk — end of quote. He means it is of the category of putting the cause in place of the effect, and that is an acceptable figure of speech.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ استقاموا}: «ثم» is for the distance of rank in excellence.
His saying: {أَلاَّ تَخَافُواْ}: «أَنْ» may be the lightened [form of «أنَّ»], or the explicative, or the one that puts [the verb] in the accusative. «لا» is prohibitive on the first two aspects and negating on the third. The difficulty in that has preceded. The implied form is «بأنْ لا تَخافوا», i.e. with the absence of fear. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form is «بأَنْ لا تَخافوا», or 'saying: «أن لا تخافوا»'; on the first it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they descended with their saying 'do not fear'; on the second the ḥāl is omitted." I say: he means that the implied bāʾ is circumstantial, so the ḥāl is not omitted, while on the second the ḥāl is the implied [verb of] saying. There is laxity in this; otherwise the ḥāl is omitted in both places, and just as the thing said stands in the place of the ḥāl, so the prepositional phrase stands in its place.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «لا تَخافوا» dropping «أنْ», which is by implying [a verb of] saying, i.e. "saying: do not fear."

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {نُزُلاً}: There are several aspects in it. First: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun. What is meant by al-nuzul is the provision prepared for the one who alights [the guest], as if it were said: "and for you in it is what you request, being prepared." Second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَدَّعُوْن», or from the pronoun in «لكم», on the basis that «نُزُلاً» is the plural of «نازِل», like «صابِر» and «صُبُر», «شارِف» and «شُرُف». Third: it is an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun). This is questionable, because the maṣdar of «نَزَل» is «النزول», not «النُّزُل». It has been said: it is the maṣdar of «أَنْزَل».
His saying: «مِنْ غَفَورٍ»: It may be attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «نُزُلاً»; it may be attached to «تَدَّعون», i.e. "you seek it from the One who is Forgiving, Merciful"; and it may be attached to the [notion of] settledness to which the prepositional phrase in «لكم» is attached, i.e. "it is settled for you from the Forgiving, Merciful." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "So it would be a ḥāl from «ما»." I say: this inference of his is not clear; rather it is attached to the settledness as an adjunct (faḍla) like other adjuncts, and it is not a ḥāl from «ما».

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي}: The majority read «إنني» with two nūns, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Nūḥ with one nūn.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ السيئة}: There are two aspects regarding this «لا». First: it is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, as in His saying {وَلاَ الظل وَلاَ الحرور} [Fāṭir: 21] and His saying {وَلاَ المسياء} [Ghāfir: 58], because «استوى» is not satisfied with one [item]. Second: it is foundational, not emphatic, since what is meant by «الحسنة» and «السيئة» is the genus, i.e. good deeds are not equal among themselves, for they vary, nor are evil deeds equal either, for one may be greater than another; this is taken from the words of al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "If you take «الحسنة» and «السيئة» as a genus, its redundancy would not be like its redundancy in the preceding aspect." I say: so he made it redundant in the second meaning as well, and that is questionable for what has preceded.
His saying: «كأنَّه وليٌّ»: There are two aspects regarding this simile clause. First: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the relative noun being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «إذا» of surprise its khabar (predicate); what governs this adverb, namely the [notion of] settledness, is what governs this ḥāl, and the point of benefit in this speech is the ḥāl. The implied form is: "then, there present, is the enemy, resembling the affectionate close friend." Second: the relative noun is also a mubtadaʾ, the clause after it is its khabar, and «إذا» is governed by the meaning of the simile, an adverb being allowed to precede its abstract governor. This is if it is said that it is an adverb; if it is said that it is a particle, there is no governor.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا}: The majority read «يُلَقَّاها», from al-talqiya (being granted). Ibn Kathīr in one transmission and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif [read] «يُلاقاها», from al-mulāqāh (meeting). The pronoun refers to the trait, or the word, or Paradise, or the testimony of divine oneness.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {خَلَقَهُنَّ}: There are three aspects regarding this pronoun. First: it refers to the four conjoined items. As for the pronoun coming like the pronoun of feminines — as al-Zamakhsharī said — it is because the plural of what is non-rational takes the rule of the feminine singular or of feminines, as in «الأقلامُ بَرَيْتُها وبَرَيْتُهنَّ» ("the pens, I sharpened them [fem. sg. / fem. pl.]"). The Shaykh disputed this with him, in that he did not distinguish between the plural of paucity and the plural of abundance in that respect, because the most eloquent usage with the plural of paucity is to treat it as feminines, and with the plural of abundance to treat it as a feminine singular; so the most eloquent is to say «الأجذاعُ كَسَرْتُهُنَّ» and «الجذوعُ كَسَرْتُها». What preceded in this verse is not a plural of paucity — I mean in a single word — but He mentioned four conjoined items, so they were given the status of a plural expressed by a single word. I say: al-Zamakhsharī is not in the position of explaining the eloquent and the more eloquent, but rather how the pronoun came as a pronoun of feminines after three masculine things and one feminine thing had preceded, the rule being to give precedence to the masculine over the feminine. [Second:] or, since He said «ومِنْ آياته», they were in the sense of "the signs," so it was said «خلقهنَّ»; al-Zamakhsharī also mentioned this, that it refers to the word «الآيات». Third: it refers to the sun and the moon, because two is a plural, and the plural is feminine, and because of their saying «شموس وأقمار» (suns and moons).

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: There are six aspects regarding its khabar (predicate). First: it is mentioned, namely His saying «أولئك ينادَوْن». Bilāl ibn Abī Burda was asked about that in his recounted story, and he said: "I find no way through it." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said to him: "It is close to you: «أولئك ينادَوْن»." This was considered far-fetched from two respects. First: the many intervening separations. Second: the prior mention of one to whom the pointing in «أولئك» can soundly refer, namely His saying {والذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, and the demonstrative refers to the nearest thing mentioned.
Second: it is omitted because the meaning is understood, and it was implied as "will be punished," or "will be destroyed," or "are obstinate." Al-Kisāʾī said: "What preceded in the speech before «إنَّ» fills its place, namely His saying {أَفَمَن يلقى فِي النار}." I say: he means in indicating it, the implied form being "will abide forever in the Fire." ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar asked ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd about that, and he said: "Its meaning in exegesis is: those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it." So he implied the predicate from the same kind as the ṣila (relative clause). This is questionable, in that the predicate and what it is predicated of become one in meaning without added benefit, as in «سيدُ الجاريةِ مالكُها» ("the master of the slave-girl is her owner").
Third: the second «الذين» is a badal (substitute) for the first «إنَّ الذين», and what is predicated of the substitute is predicated of what it substitutes for, so it follows that the predicate is {لاَ يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنَآ}. This is extracted from the words of al-Zamakhsharī. [Translator's note: the second «الذين» meant here is that of {إِنَّ الذين يُلْحِدُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا} in the preceding verse.]
Fourth: the predicate is His saying {لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ الباطل}, the returning pronoun being omitted, its implied form being "falsehood does not come to it from them," as in «السَّمْنُ مَنَوان بدرهم» ("ghee: two manas for a dirham"), i.e. two manas of it. Or «أل» is a substitute for the pronoun on the view of the Kufans, its implied form being: "those who disbelieved in the Reminder — their falsehood does not come to it."
Fifth: the predicate is His saying {مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ}, the returning pronoun also being omitted, its implied form being: "those who disbelieved in the Reminder — nothing is said to you concerning them except what was said to the messengers before you." The Shaykh adopted these two aspects.
Sixth: some of the Kufans held that it is His saying {وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ}, and this is not intelligible.
The clause «وإنَّه لكتابٌ» is circumstantial, and {لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ الباطل} is an adjective of «كتاب». «تنزيلٌ» is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or an adjective of «كتابٌ», on the basis that «لا يأتيه» is parenthetical, or [that it is] an adjective as preceded, on the view of whoever allows a non-explicit adjective to precede an explicit one; its verification has preceded in al-Māʾida. «مِنْ حكيمٍ» is an adjective of «تَنْزيلٌ» or attached to it. «الباطلُ» is an active participle; and it has been said: a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «العافية» and «العاقبة».

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ}: It has been said: it explains what was said, as if it were said: "it was said to the messengers: indeed your Lord is the Possessor of ..." And it has been said: it is resumptive.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ}: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it with full pronunciation of the hamza, and Hishām dropping the first. The rest [read] with easing of the second, between-between (bayna bayna). As for the madd, its rule is known from His saying «أأنذَرْتَهم» at the beginning of this work. Whoever reads it as a question says: its meaning is "a non-Arabic Book and an Arab Messenger?" It has been said: "and an Arab [people] to whom it is sent?" And it has been said: its meaning is "is part of it non-Arabic and part of it Arabic?" Whoever does not keep the interrogative hamza may have omitted it in wording while intending it in meaning, and in that there is agreement of the two readings; but that is not permissible according to the majority unless there is «أم» in the speech, as in:
3960 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بسَبْعٍ رَمَيْنَ الجَمْرَ أم بثمان
(… did they throw the pebbles with seven or with eight?)
If there is no «أم», it is not permissible except according to al-Akhfash, and what is in that has preceded. It may be that he made it a pure statement, its meaning being: "why were its verses not set out in detail, so that part of them were non-Arabic, understood by non-Arabs, and part Arabic, understood by Arabs?"
Al-aʿjamī is one who does not speak clearly, even if he is of the Arabs; it is related to its quality, like «أحمرِيّ» and «دَوَّاريّ», so the yāʾ in it is for intensifying the description, and the relation in it is not real. Al-Rāzī said in his Lawāmiḥ: "It is like the yāʾ of «كُرْسِيّ» and «بُخْتِيّ»." The Shaykh distinguished between them, saying: "It is not like the yāʾ of «كُرْسِيّ», for in «كرسيّ» and «بُخْتيّ» the word is built upon it, unlike the yāʾ of «أعجميّ», for they say «رجل أَعْجم» and «أعْجميّ»."
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn read «أَعَجَمِيٌّ» with fatḥa on the ʿayn; it is related to al-ʿajam (non-Arabs), and the yāʾ in it is truly for relation; one says «رجل أعجميٌّ» (a man of non-Arab stock) even if he is eloquent. The discussion of the difference between them has preceded in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ.
There are three aspects for the nominative of «أَعْجميّ». First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "are a non-Arabic and an Arabic equal?" Second: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "it," meaning the Qurʾān, is non-Arabic while the one sent with it is Arab. Third: it is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb, i.e. "are a non-Arabic and an Arabic equal?" This is weak, since the verb is omitted only in places I have explained more than once.
His saying: {والذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: There are three aspects in it. First: it is a mubtadaʾ, with «في آذانِهم» its khabar and «وَقْرٌ» a fāʿil; or «في آذانهم» is a fronted predicate and «وقرٌ» a postponed subject, the clause being the predicate of the first. Second: «وَقْرٌ» is the predicate of an implied subject, and the clause is the predicate of the first, the implied form being: "and those who do not believe — it is deafness in their ears"; having reported of it that it is guidance for those, He reported of it that it is deafness in the ears of these and blindness upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī stated its meaning. There is no need for the implication when the speech is complete without it. Third: {الذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} is conjoined to «الذين آمنوا», and «وَقْرٌ» is conjoined to «هدىً»; this is of the category of conjunction to the governed words of two governors, and there are doctrines about it whose analysis has preceded.
His saying: «عَمَىً»: The majority read it with fatḥa on the mīm, with tanwīn; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «عَمِي يَعْمَى», like «صَدِي يَصْدَى صَدَىً» and «هَوِي يَهْوَى هَوَىً».
Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr and a group read «عَمٍ» with kasra and tanwīn, as a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), [the Qurʾān] being described with it figuratively. ʿAmr ibn Dīnār read — and it was transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās — «عَمِيَ» with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the yāʾ, as a past verb. There are two aspects regarding the pronoun, the more apparent being that it refers to the Qurʾān; the second, that it refers to the deafness, but the meaning rejects it. «في آذانهم» — if you do not make it the predicate — is attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it [«وقر»], because it was originally an adjective; it is not attached to it, because it is a maṣdar, so what it governs does not precede it. His saying {وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى} is likewise in the reading of the majority; as for the two preceding readings, «على» is attached to what follows it, since it is not a maṣdar.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {فَلِنَفْسِهِ}: It may be attached to an implied verb, i.e. "for himself is his work"; and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the righteous deed is for himself." His saying «فعليها» is like it.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَاتٍ}: This «ما» may be negating, which is the apparent sense, and it may be a relative; Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that without explaining its basis. Its explanation is that it would be in the position of the genitive by conjunction to «الساعة», i.e. "knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of that which comes out," and «مِنْ ثمرات» on this would be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or «مِنْ» would be for clarification. The second «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. As for the second «ما», it is negating only. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because «ولا تَضَعُ» is conjoined to it, then the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; had it been in the sense of «الذي», conjoined to «الساعة», that would not be permissible."
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «ثمرات», and what strengthens it is that it is written with the extended tāʾ.
The rest [read] «ثمرة» in the singular, meaning the genus. If «ما» is negating, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in the agent; if it is a relative, it is for clarification, as has preceded.
«الأَكْمام» is the plural of «كِمّ» with kasra on the kāf — so al-Zamakhsharī vocalised it — which is what covers the fruit, like the sheath of the palm spathe. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-kumm is what covers the hand of the shirt, and what covers the fruit, and its plural is «أكْمام»." This indicates that it has ḍamma on the kāf, since he made it shared between the sleeve of the shirt and the covering of the fruit, and there is no disagreement that the sleeve of the shirt is with ḍamma. So it may be that the container of the fruit has two dialectal forms, unlike the sleeve of the shirt, reconciling their two statements. As for «أَكِمَّة», its singular is «كِمام», like «أَزِمَّة» and «زِمام». Ibn Kathīr gave fatḥa to the yāʾ of «شُركائيَ».
His saying: {مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ}: This negative clause suspends (taʿlīq) «آذنَّاك», because it is in the sense of «أَعْلَمْناك» (We informed you). [The poet] said:
3961 - آذَنَتْنا ببَيْنِها أسماءُ ... رُبَّ ثاوٍ يَمَلُّ منه الثَّواءُ
(Asmāʾ informed us of her parting; many a one who stays is one whose staying is wearisome.)
A disagreement has preceded for us about suspending «أعلم» ...; the correct view is that it occurs, as heard from the Arabs. Abū Ḥātim allowed a pause on «آذنَّاك» and on «ظنُّوا», beginning with the negation after them by way of resumption. «مِنَّا» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مِنْ شهيد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also possible that «مِنْ شهيد» is a fāʿil (agent) of the prepositional phrase before it, because it is supported by the negation.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {مَا لَهُمْ مِّن مَّحِيصٍ}: like His saying {مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ}, without difference.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {مِن دُعَآءِ الخير}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, its agent being omitted, i.e. "he." ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «مِن دُعَآءِ بالخير».

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {لَيَقُولَنَّ هذا لِي}: the answer to the oath, because it precedes the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, as its establishment is known. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ليقولَنَّ» is the apodosis, and the fāʾ is omitted." I say: this is not permissible except in poetry, as in the saying:
3962 - مَنْ يَفْعلِ الحسناتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will appreciate them …)
so much so that al-Mubarrad forbids it even in poetry, and he transmits the verse as: «فالرحمن يشكرُه».

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: The discussion of it has preceded several times. Its first object here is omitted, its implied form being "have you considered yourselves," and the second is the interrogative clause.
«الآفاق» is the plural of «أُفُق», which is the region. The poet said:
3963 - لو نالَ حيٌّ مِن الدنيا بمنزلةٍ ... أفْقَ السماءِ لنالَتْ كفُّه الأُفُقا
(If any living being could reach, by rank in this world, the horizon of heaven, his hand would have reached the horizon.)
It is like «أَعْناق» from «عُنُق», its hamza changed into alif. Al-Rāghib transmitted that «أَفَق» is said with fatḥa on the hamza and the fāʾ, so it would be like «جَبَل» and «أَجْبال». «آفَقَ فلانٌ» means he went off into the horizons. «الآفِقُ» is one who has reached the limit of generosity, likening him in that to one who goes into the horizons. The relative adjective of «الأُفُق» is «أَفَقيٌّ» with fatḥa on both. I say: it is possible that it was related to the form with fatḥa, and they dispensed with that from relating to the form with ḍamma; and it has parallels.

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ}: There are two aspects in it. First: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the fāʿil (agent), and this is the preponderant view; the object is omitted, i.e. "does your Lord not suffice you?" In His saying {أَنَّهُ على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ} there are two aspects. One: it is a badal (substitute) for «بربك», so it is nominative in position and genitive in form, like what it follows. The other: the origin is «بأنَّه», then the preposition was omitted, so the [known] disagreement applies. The second of the two original aspects: «بربك» is the object, and «أنه» with what follows is the agent, i.e. "does His testimony not suffice your Lord?" It has been read {إِنَّهُ على كُلِّ} with kasra, by implying [a verb of] saying, or by way of resumption.

semin-durr:54-54.t: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan read «في مُرْيَة» with ḍamma on the mīm, and it has preceded that it is a dialectal variant of the form with kasra on the mīm. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حم (١) تَنْزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (٢) كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ (٣)).
His saying (تَنْزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ): it is like the beginning of al-Sajda. كِتَابٌ: i.e. "it is a Book". It may also be nominative by تَنْزِيلٌ, i.e. "a Book has been sent down"; or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or a badal (substitute). And (قُرْآنًا) is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa, circumstantial) of «آيَاتُهُ». It may also be a ḥāl of «كِتَابٌ», because it has been qualified [by an adjective].

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ مِنْ فَوْقِهَا وَبَارَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَا أَقْوَاتَهَا فِي أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ سَوَاءً لِلسَّائِلِينَ (١٠)).
His saying (وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا): it is resumptive, not conjoined to «خَلَقَ», because if it were conjoined to it, it would fall within the ṣila (relative clause); and that is not permissible, because the two have been separated by His saying (وَتَجْعَلُونَ...) to the end of the verse, which is in no way part of the ṣila.
His saying (فِي أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ): i.e. "in the completion of four days". Were it not for this implied wording, the days would be eight: two days in the first, which is His saying (خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ), and two days in the last, which is His saying (فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ).
(سَوَاءً), in the accusative: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they became equal, an equalling"; and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «أَقْوَاتَهَا», or of that in فِيهَا, or of الْأَرْضَ. It is also read in the genitive (سَوَاءٍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of الْأَيَّامِ, and in the nominative (سَوَاءٌ) on the implied wording "they are equal".

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ اِئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا قَالَتَا أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِينَ (١١)).
His saying (اِئْتِيَا): i.e. "come, both of you". And (طَوْعًا) and (كَرْهًا) are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (أَتَيْنَا) with the short vowel, i.e. "we have come"; and with the long vowel (آتَيْنَا), i.e. "we have given obedience from ourselves".
And (طَائِعِينَ) is a ḥāl; it is plural [in the masculine form of rational beings] because He described them with the attributes of those who have reason; or the implied wording is "we have come with whoever is in us", and for that reason it is plural.
It is also said: it is plural according to the multiplicity of the heavens and the earth.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t: Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ وَأَوْحَى فِي كُلِّ سَمَاءٍ أَمْرَهَا وَزَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَحِفْظًا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ (١٢)) (وَحِفْظًا): i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding" (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), or "for guarding".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ جَاءَتْهُمُ الرُّسُلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ قَالُوا لَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّنَا لَأَنْزَلَ مَلَائِكَةً فَإِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ (١٤)).
(إِذْ جَاءَتْهُمُ): it may be an adverb of time for أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ, as you say "I met you when such-and-such was the case"; or it may be a naʿt (adjective) of صَاعِقَةً, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second «صَاعِقَةِ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِي أَيَّامٍ نَحِسَاتٍ لِنُذِيقَهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَخْزَى وَهُمْ لَا يُنْصَرُونَ (١٦)).
His saying (نَحِسَاتٍ): it is read with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and there are two views on it:
The first: it is an active participle, like نَصِبٌ and نَصِبَاتٌ. The second: that it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْكَلِمَةُ. It is also read with sukūn (نَحْسَاتٍ), and there are two views on it:
The first: it has the meaning of the form with kasra, and was made quiescent only for an incidental reason.
The second: that it was originally an active participle, made quiescent for lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَى عَلَى الْهُدَى فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ صَاعِقَةُ الْعَذَابِ الْهُونِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (١٧))
His saying (وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ): it is in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate). And in the accusative (ثَمُودَ) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "as for Thamūd, We guided [them]", explained by His saying «فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أَعْدَاءُ اللَّهِ إِلَى النَّارِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ (١٩))
His saying (وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ): it is an adverb of time for what is indicated by what comes after it, which is
His saying «فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ»; as though He said: "they will be held back on the day We gather".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلَا أَبْصَارُكُمْ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمْ وَلَكِنْ ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَعْلَمُ كَثِيرًا مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying (أَنْ يَشْهَدَ): i.e. "from [the possibility] that it would testify" (مِنْ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ), because تَسْتَتِرُ is not transitive by itself.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ الَّذِي ظَنَنْتُمْ بِرَبِّكُمْ أَرْدَاكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٢٣)).
His saying (وَذَلِكُمْ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ظَنُّكُمْ» is its khabar (predicate); «الَّذِي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar, or a khabar after a khabar; and «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is a further khabar.
It may also be that all of them are naʿt or badal (substitute), and «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is the khabar.
It may also be that «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ يَصْبِرُوا فَالنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَهُمْ وَإِنْ يَسْتَعْتِبُوا فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying (يَسْتَعْتِبُوا): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the second tāʾ, i.e. "that they ask for the removal of what they are reproached for". (فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ): with fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. "among those whose request for the removal of reproach is granted".
It is also read «يُسْتَعْتَبُوا», with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. "what they are not reproached for is asked of them"; and then فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتِبِينَ with kasra on the tāʾ, i.e. "among those who remove reproach".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying (وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the ghayn, from لَغَا يَلْغَى, and with ḍamma on it (وَالْغُوا), from لَغَا يَلْغُو; the meaning is the same.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ النَّارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الْخُلْدِ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying (النَّارُ): it is a badal (substitute) of جَزَاءُ, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as the khabar. And (جَزَاءً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they were requited with that, a requital".
It may also be accusative by جَزَاءُ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying (أَلَّا تَخَافُوا): the implied wording may be "with [the message] that you should not fear" (بِأَنْ لَا تَخَافُوا), or "saying: do not fear". [On the first, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they descend with their saying "do not fear"; on the second, the ḥāl is omitted.]

ukberi-tibyan:31-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَاؤُكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِي أَنْفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ (٣١) نُزُلًا مِنْ غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ (٣٢))
His saying (نُزُلًا): there are two views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted hāʾ [i.e. the object pronoun of تَدَّعُونَ], or of مَا; i.e. "yours is what you call for, prepared", and the like; and «مِنْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it. The second: it is the plural of نَازِلٌ, like صَابِرٌ and صُبُرٌ; so it is a ḥāl of the wāw in «تَدَّعُونَ», or of the kāf and mīm in «لَكُمْ». On this view مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَدَّعُونَ, i.e. "they ask for it from One Forgiving"; or to the adverbial phrase, i.e. "that is settled from One Forgiving", so that it is a ḥāl of «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ (٣٤) وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ (٣٥)).
His saying (كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ): there are two views on it:
The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الَّذِي» together with its ṣila (relative clause), and «الَّذِي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إِذَا is [the إِذَا] of surprise, and «هِيَ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the text («هِيَ», "it"); evidently «إِذَا» is meant, i.e. إِذَا of surprise is the khabar]; i.e. "and there, present, is the enemy, resembling a friend"; and the benefit [of the statement] is obtained from the ḥāl.
The second: that it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «إِذَا» is an adverb of time for the meaning of likening; an adverb may precede an abstract governor (ʿāmil maʿnawī).
The pronoun in «يُلَقَّاهَا» refers to the trait or to the word.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ لَا تَسْجُدُوا لِلشَّمْسِ وَلَا لِلْقَمَرِ وَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ (٣٧)).
His saying (خَلَقَهُنَّ): the pronoun refers to the signs, which are the night, the day, the sun and the moon.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ (٤١)).
His saying (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» is omitted, i.e. "are obstinate" or "are perishing". It is also said: it is (أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ).

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا أَعْجَمِيًّا لَقَالُوا لَوْلَا فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ أَأَعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وَشِفَاءٌ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ (٤٤)).
His saying (أَأَعْجَمِيٌّ): it is a question.
It is also read with a single hamza and fatḥa on the ʿayn (أَعَجَمِيٌّ), as a relative adjective (nisba) to عَجَمٌ.
And (عَمًى) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عَمِيَ, like صَدِيَ صَدًى. It is also read with kasra on the mīm (عَمٍ), i.e. "obscure", so it is an active participle. It is also read عَمِيَ, as a past verb. So عَلَى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the active participle or to the verb.
As for the maṣdar, it cannot be attached to it because it precedes it; but it may be by way of clarification (tabyīn), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فَعَلَيْهَا وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ (٤٦)).
His saying (فَلِنَفْسِهِ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then it is for his own self".

ukberi-tibyan:47-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَرَاتٍ مِنْ أَكْمَامِهَا وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنْثَى وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِي قَالُوا آذَنَّاكَ مَا مِنَّا مِنْ شَهِيدٍ (٤٧) وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٤٨))
His saying (وَمَا تَحْمِلُ): «مَا» is negating, because «وَلَا تَضَعُ» is conjoined to it and then the negation is broken by إِلَّا; if it had the sense of الَّذِي (that which), conjoined to السَّاعَةِ, that would not be sound. As for
His saying (وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَرَاتٍ), it may have the sense of الَّذِي, but the stronger view is that it is negating.
His saying (آذَنَّاكَ): this verb is transitive to one object by itself and to another by a preposition; here the negation and what falls in its domain occupy the place of the preposition and its genitive noun. Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at آذَنَّاكَ and then begins anew; so the negation has no grammatical position.
As for His saying (وَظَنُّوا): its two objects are dispensed with by (مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ). Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at «ظَنُّوا», and then a statement is made about them with the negation.

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَيَئُوسٌ قَنُوطٌ (٤٩) وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذَا لِي وَمَا أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنَى فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ (٥٠)).
And (دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its object, the agent being omitted. And (لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذَا لِي) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with the fāʾ omitted.
It is also said: it is the answer to an omitted oath.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا قُلُوبُنَا فِي أَكِنَّةٍ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَا إِلَيْهِ وَفِي آذَانِنَا وَقْرٌ وَمِنْ بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ فَاعْمَلْ إِنَّنَا عَامِلُونَ (٥)).
His saying (مِمَّا تَدْعُونَا): it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «فِي أَكِنَّةٍ» is "veiled from hearing what you call us to". It cannot be a naʿt (adjective) of أَكِنَّةٍ, because الْأَكِنَّةُ are the coverings, and the coverings are not part of what you call us to.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (٥٣)).
His saying (بِرَبِّكَ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and it is the fāʿil (agent) of يَكْفِي, with the object omitted, i.e. "does your Lord not suffice you?". On this view «أَنَّهُ» is in the position of a badal (substitute) of the agent, either according to the wording or according to the position; i.e. "does your Lord — His witnessing — not suffice you?".
It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative [or the genitive, on the implied wording بِأَنَّهُ ("in that He…"). It is also said: «بِرَبِّكَ» is in the accusative position], as the object of يَكْفِي; i.e. "does His witnessing not suffice your Lord?".

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ (٨)).
And (مَمْنُونٍ) is a passive participle, from مَنَنْتُ الْحَبْلَ, i.e. "I cut the rope".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
﷽
﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 2] — "تَنْزِيلٌ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿كِتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3]; this is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is permissible that "تَنْزِيلٌ" be made nominative by "حـم", and it is permissible that it be nominative by implying "هَذا", the meaning being: "This is a revelation from the Mighty, the Merciful", that is: "It is a revelation". ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3] — "قُرْآنًا" is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "its verses have been made clear as a Quran", that is: "its verses have been made clear in the state of its being gathered as Arabic". ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3], that is: We have made it clear for whoever knows.
﴿بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 4] are among its attributes.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — on Tuesday and Wednesday, so the total became four days. That is His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ مِن فَوْقِها وبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها في أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾, that is: in the completion of four days. ﴿سَواءً لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾ — and "سَواءٍ"; the nominative is also permissible. Whoever reads the genitive makes it an attribute of the days, the meaning being: "in four equal days". Whoever reads the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "they were equal, equally (سَواءً، واسْتِواءً)". Whoever reads the nominative takes it in the sense: "they are equal". And "لِلسّائِلِينَ" is attached to His saying: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — for everyone in need of sustenance; it was said "لِلسّائِلِينَ" (for those who ask) only because everyone seeks sustenance and asks for it. It is also possible that "لِلسّائِلِينَ" means: for whoever asked "In how many [days] were the heavens and the earths created?", so it was said: "The earth was created in four equal days, with no addition and no shortfall", as an answer to whoever asked.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إلى السَّماءِ وهي دُخانٌ فَقالَ لَها ولِلأرْضِ﴾ (the verse) — the meaning of "اسْتَوى" is: He turned to the heaven and directed [His will]. ﴿قالَتا أتَيْنا طائِعِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It was said "طائِعِينَ" rather than "طائِعاتٍ" only because they were treated like beings that reason and discern, as it was said of the stars: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40]. It has also been said: "they said: we come — that is, we and whoever is in us — willingly". And the meaning of "طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا" is in the sense: "obey what I have commanded willingly", in the position of "obey with obedience, or be compelled with compulsion".

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ﴾: He created them and made them. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما ∗∗∗ داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them are two coats of linked mail which David made, or Tubbaʿ fashioned the ample [mail].)
Its meaning is: "he worked them and made them". ﴿وَأوْحى في كُلِّ سَماءٍ أمْرَها﴾ — it was said: "what sets it right", and it was said: "its angels". ﴿وَزَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِمَصابِيحَ وحِفْظًا﴾ — its meaning is: "and We guarded it with the stars from the eavesdropping of the devils, a guarding". So He said: say, do you disbelieve in the One whose power is this, and assign rivals to Him — that is, idols which you carve with your own hands? ﴿ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ العَزِيزِ العَلِيمِ﴾, that is: the One whose attribute this is, and who has this power, the Lord of the worlds.

zajjaj:13-13.t: Then He said: ﴿فَإنْ أعْرَضُوا﴾, that is: if they do not accept your message after this clarification and affirm the oneness of Allah, ﴿فَقُلْ أنْذَرْتُكم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾, that is: I have warned you that there will befall you what befell those nations before you that disbelieved.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He related the story of their disbelief and the cause of their insolence and their persistence in their misguidance, saying: ﴿فَأمّا عادٌ فاسْتَكْبَرُوا في الأرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ وقالُوا مَن أشَدُّ مِنّا قُوَّةً﴾. So Allah sent upon them a furious wind, and He said: ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا في أيّامٍ نَحِساتٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16] — and "نَحْساتٍ" is also transmitted. Abū ʿUbayda said: "الصَّرْصَر" is the one with a violent sound, and it has come in the commentary: the intensely cold one. "نَحِساتٍ" means ill-omened; its singular is "نَحِسٌ"; and whoever reads "نَحْساتٍ", its singular is "نَحْسٌ". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 19]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿وَأمّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْناهُمْ﴾ — the good [reading] is dropping the tanwīn. It is read "ثَمُودٌ" with tanwīn, and "ثَمُودًا" in the accusative is permissible, by an implied verb which the overt one explains. As for the meaning of "هَدَيْناهم", Qatāda said: "We made clear to them the path of guidance and the path of misguidance." ﴿فاسْتَحَبُّوا العَمى عَلى الهُدى﴾. The preferred choice is the nominative of "ثَمُودُ", as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is the view of all the grammarians — preferring the nominative — and all of them allow the accusative.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهم صاعِقَةُ العَذابِ الهُونِ﴾ — "الهُون" is the abasement and disgrace which humiliates them and disgraces them.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أعْداءُ اللَّهِ إلى النّارِ فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — "إلى النّارِ" is read with fatḥa on the nūn and full (tafkhīm) pronunciation, and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is "إلى النِّارِ" with imāla (inclination) towards kasra. He prefers that — meaning the kasra — only with the rāʾ, because it is a letter with repetition (takrīr) in it; for that reason Abū ʿAmr preferred the kasra. ﴿فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary: "the first of them are held back for the last of them". Its origin is from "وَزَعْتُهُ", when you restrain him. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said when he took up the judgeship: "People must have restrainers (وَزَعَة)", that is: they must have helpers who restrain people from transgression.
﴿شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهم وأبْصارُهم وجُلُودُهُمْ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 20] — it has come in the commentary that "جُلُودُهم" (their skins) is a euphemism for the private parts; the meaning is: their private parts will testify to their sins.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿وَقالُوا لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنا قالُوا أنْطَقَنا اللَّهُ﴾, that is: Allah made us witnesses.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿وَذَلِكم ظَنُّكُمُ﴾ — it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and "أرْداكم" is a second khabar. It is also permissible that "ظَنُّكُمُ" be a badal (substitute) for "ذَلِكم", the meaning being: "and your thought which you thought about your Lord has ruined you". The meaning of "أرْداكم" is: it has destroyed you.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنا﴾: "and We arranged", from where they did not reckon, ﴿لَهم قُرَناءَ﴾ (the verse). He is saying: they made attractive to them their deeds which they do and witness, and what is behind them, and what they resolve to do.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذا القُرْآنِ والغَوْا فِيهِ﴾, that is: oppose it with speech that is not understood, that speech being idle talk (لَغْو). One says: "لَغا، يَلْغُو، لَغْوًا", and one says: "لَغِيَ، يَلْغى، لَغْوًا", when one speaks idle talk, which is speech that yields nothing and whose reality you do not understand.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿ذَلِكَ جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ النّارُ﴾ — what indicates its nominative is His saying: ﴿فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَذابًا شَدِيدًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 27]; the meaning is: "that severe punishment is the recompense of the enemies of Allah". "النّار" is nominative, a badal (substitute) for "جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ". If you wish, you may make "النّار" nominative as an explanation, as though it were said: "What is it?" and it was said: "It is the Fire". ﴿لَهم فِيها دارُ الخُلْدِ﴾, that is: they have in the Fire the abode of eternity, and the Fire is the abode itself, just as you say: "you have in this house a house of joy", while you mean the house itself. As the poet said:
أخُو رَغائِبَ يُعْطِيها ويَسْألُها ∗∗∗ يَأْبى الظُّلامَةَ مِنهُ النَّوْفَلُ الزُّفَرُ
(A man of great desires, who gives them and asks for them; from him the generous, burden-bearing one refuses injustice.)

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّنا أرِنا﴾ — with kasra on the rāʾ, and with it made quiescent because of the heaviness of the kasra, as they said "فَخْذٌ" for "فَخِذٌ" (thigh). Whoever gives it kasra follows the original, and the kasra is better, because originally it is "أرْئِنا": the hamza was dropped and the kasra remained as an indication of it; and the kasra is better. The meaning of the verse, according to what has come in the commentary, is that by the two He means the son of Adam, Qābīl, who killed his brother, and Iblīs: Qābīl is of mankind and Iblīs is of the jinn. And the meaning of ﴿نَجْعَلْهُما تَحْتَ أقْدامِنا﴾ is: that they be in the lowest depth.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا﴾, that is: they affirmed the oneness of Allah and were steadfast, acted in obedience to Him and kept to the sunna of His Prophet. ﴿تَتَنَـزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾ as bearers of good news, giving them good news at death and at the time of resurrection, so that the terrors of the Resurrection do not alarm them.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿نُـزُلا مِن غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ﴾ — its meaning is: and rejoice in the Garden, in which you will be lodged as a hospitable lodging. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: "نُزُلًا" is accusative in two ways. One of them is that it be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "you will have in it whatever your souls desire; We have lodged it as a lodging". It is also permissible that it be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense: "you will have in it whatever your souls desire, as a lodging", just as you say: "جاءَ زَيْدٌ مَشْيًا" (Zayd came walking), in the sense of "جاءَ زَيْدٌ ماشِيًا".

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿وَمَن أحْسَنُ قَوْلا﴾ — [قَوْلًا] is accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz), just as you say: "زَيْدٌ أحْسَنُ مِنكَ وجْهًا" (Zayd is more handsome than you in face). It has come in the commentary that Muḥammad ﷺ is meant by it, because he called to the oneness of Allah. And it has also come in the commentary from ʿĀʾisha and others that it was revealed about the muezzins.

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿وَلا تَسْتَوِي الحَسَنَةُ ولا السَّيِّئَةُ﴾ — "لا" is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic; the meaning is: "the good deed and the evil deed are not equal". ﴿ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾ — its meaning is: "repel the evil deed with that which is better". ﴿كَأنَّهُ ولِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ﴾ — "الحَمِيم" is the near relative.

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿وَما يُلَقّاها إلا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾, that is: none is granted the reward of this — that is, none is granted this deed — except those who are patient, that is: except those who restrain anger. ﴿وَما يُلَقّاها إلا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — "الحَظّ" here is the Garden, that is: none is granted it except one for whom the Garden has become due. And the meaning of "ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ" is: "a great share in good".

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿وَإمّا يَنْـزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَـزْغٌ﴾ — He is saying: if there comes to you from Satan an incitement by which he turns you away from forbearance, seek refuge in Allah from his evil and continue in your forbearance.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ اللَّيْلُ والنَّهارُ﴾, that is: among His signs which indicate that He is One.
And His saying: ﴿واسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾ — He has said "the night, the day and the moon", which are masculine, and He said "خَلَقَهُنَّ", and the hāʾ and nūn indicate the feminine. There are two aspects to it. One of them is that the pronoun for what does not reason follows the form of the feminine: you say "هَذِهِ كِباشُكَ فَسُقْها" (these are your rams, so drive them [fem. sing.]), and if you wish, "فَسُقْهُنَّ" [fem. pl.]; "خَلَقَهم" [masc. pl.] would only be for what reasons, nothing else. It is also permissible that "خَلَقَهُنَّ" refer back to the meaning of "the signs", because He said: "and among His signs are these things", ﴿واسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿فَإنِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا فالَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ — this is an address to Muḥammad ﷺ, and "الَّذِينَ" here means the angels. So the meaning is: "if they are arrogant and do not affirm the oneness of Allah, worship Him and believe in His Messenger, then the angels glorify Him by night and day". ﴿وَهم لا يَسْأمُونَ﴾: they do not weary.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
Then He added to the proof for them, saying: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنَّكَ تَرى الأرْضَ خاشِعَةً﴾, that is: crumbled and changed; it is like "هامِدَةً" (barren).
﴿فَإذا أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْها الماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ ورَبَتْ﴾ — and it is read "وَرَبَأتْ" with hamza. The meaning of "رَبَتْ" is: it swelled, and the meaning of "رَبَأتْ" is: it rose, because when a plant is about to appear the earth rises for it.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ في آياتِنا لا يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنا﴾ — and "يَلْحَدُونَ" with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ. The explanation of "يَلْحَدُونَ" is: they put speech in other than its proper direction. From this is "اللَّحْد" (the niche-grave), because it is the digging in the side of the grave. One says "لَحَدَ" and "ألْحَدَ" with one meaning. ﴿اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ﴾ — the wording of this speech is the wording of a command, and its meaning is threat and menace; He has already made clear to them the requital for good and evil.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَكِتابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾ ﴿لا يَأْتِيهِ الباطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ولا مِن خَلْفِهِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 42] — there are two aspects to it. One of them is that the books which preceded do not nullify it, and no book comes after it to nullify it. The second aspect is that it is guarded against anything being taken away from it, so that falsehood would come to it from before it, or anything being added to it, so that falsehood would come to it from behind it. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نَـزَّلْنا الذِّكْرَ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 9]

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿ما يُقالُ لَكَ إلا ما قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾, that is: you are denied as the messengers before you were denied, and it was said to them just as the disbelievers say to you. Then He said: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ﴾ — the meaning is: for whoever believes in you; ﴿وَذُو عِقابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ for whoever denies you.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا أعْجَمِيًّا لَقالُوا لَوْلا فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾, that is: made clear. ﴿أأعْجَمِيٌّ وعَرَبِيٌّ﴾ — it is read "أأعْجَمِيٌّ" with two hamzas, and "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with one hamza, and with a hamza followed by a lightened one that resembles alif; it is not permissible for it to be a pure alif, because after it comes the ʿayn, which is quiescent. It is also read "أعَجَمِيٌّ وعَرَبِيٌّ" with one hamza and fatḥa on the ʿayn. Al-Ḥasan read "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with a hamza and a quiescent ʿayn. What has come in the commentary is that the meaning is: "Had We made it a non-Arabic Quran, they would have said: Why — why not — have its verses been made clear? A non-Arabic Quran and an Arab prophet?!" Whoever reads "آعْجَمِيٌّ", with hamza and alif, [takes it as] a relative adjective (nisba) attributed to the non-Arabic tongue (al-aʿjam). You say "هَذا رَجُلٌ أعْجَمِيٌّ" when he does not speak clearly, whether he is of the non-Arabs or of the Arabs; and you say "هَذا رَجُلٌ عَجَمِيٌّ" when he is of the non-Arabs, whether he speaks clearly or not. Similar to that is "هَذا رَجُلٌ أعْرابِيٌّ" (a Bedouin man), when he is of the people of the desert, whether his stock is Arab or non-Arab. The best in the Quran is "آعْجَمِيٌّ", with hamza and alif, by way of attribution to al-aʿjam. Do you not see His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا أعْجَمِيًّا﴾, and no one read "عَجَمِيًّا"? As for the reading of al-Ḥasan — I mean "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with the ʿayn quiescent — it is not in the sense of a question, but in the sense of "why have its verses not been made clear", so that part of it would be a clarification for the non-Arabs and part of it a clarification for the Arabs. All of these four aspects are acceptable in Arabic, and its commentary goes accordingly.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هو لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وشِفاءٌ﴾, meaning the Quran; ﴿والَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ في آذانِهِمْ وقْرٌ﴾, that is: in refusing to accept, they are in the position of one who has deafness in his ear. ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾ — and it is read "وَهو عَلَيْهِمْ عَمٍ" with kasra on the mīm and tanwīn; "وَهو عَلَيْهِمْ عَمِيَ" with the yāʾ retained and given fatḥa is also permissible, but it is not permissible to make the yāʾ quiescent and drop the tanwīn. ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُنادَوْنَ مِن مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, meaning that, because of the hardness of their hearts, what is recited to them is far removed from them.

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ — the word is: their being promised the Hour. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَمَن أساءَ فَعَلَيْها﴾, that is: against himself. And what indicates that the word here is the Hour

zajjaj:47-47.t:
is His saying: ﴿إلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ السّاعَةِ﴾.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَراتٍ مِن أكْمامِها﴾ — like the emergence of the palm spathe from its husk. ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ أيْنَ شُرَكائِي﴾ — the meaning is: "Where is your saying that I have partners?!", and Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, is One, having no partner. He has made that clear in His saying: ﴿أيْنَ شُرَكائِي قالُوا آذَنّاكَ ما مِنّا مِن شَهِيدٍ﴾ — "آذَنّاكَ": we have informed You; there is none among us who bears witness for them.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَظَنُّوا ما لَهم مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾, that is: they were certain.

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿لا يَسْأمُ الإنْسانُ مِن دُعاءِ الخَيْرِ﴾: he does not weary of the good that befalls him, and when he is tested with something of evil he despairs and loses hope.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالُوا قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ﴾ — "in coverings", that is: "what you call us to does not reach our hearts, because they are in coverings". The singular of "الأكِنَّة" is "كِنان". ﴿وَفِي آذانِنا وقْرٌ﴾, that is: deafness, and a lock which prevents listening to your speech; that is: in refusing to accept from you we are in the position of one who does not hear your speech. ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنا وبَيْنِكَ حِجابٌ﴾, that is: a barrier in creed and religion. It is like "قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ", except that the meaning of this is that we do not join with you in any doctrine. ﴿فاعْمَلْ إنَّنا عامِلُونَ﴾, that is: [we are working] according to our doctrine, and you are working according to your doctrine. It may also be: "work at nullifying our doctrine; we are working at nullifying your cause".

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أذَقْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنّا مِن بَعْدِ ضَرّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذا لِي﴾, that is: this is due to me; I have earned it by my work. The disbelievers are meant by this, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَما أظُنُّ السّاعَةَ قائِمَةً ولَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إلى رَبِّي إنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنى﴾. He is saying: I am not certain of the resurrection and the coming of the Hour; but if the matter is so, then I will have with Him the best.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَإذا أنْعَمْنا عَلى الإنْسانِ أعْرَضَ ونَأى بِجانِبِهِ﴾ — and it is read "ناءَ", and the meaning is close. He is saying: when he is in blessing, he distances himself from remembering Allah and calling on Him. ﴿وَإذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾ — "عَرِيضٍ" here means: great; and likewise if it were "ذُو دُعاءٍ طَوِيلٍ" (of long supplication), its meaning would be: "great".

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا في الآفاقِ وفي أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, that is: We will show them the landmarks which indicate the oneness [of Allah] in the horizons — its singular is "أُفُق". He is saying: We will show them the traces of those who passed before them among the nations that denied the messengers, and the traces of Allah's creation in all lands; and in themselves: that they were drops of semen, then clots, then lumps of flesh, then bones clothed with flesh, then they were brought on to discernment and reason. All of that is proof that the One who did it is One, there is nothing like Him. ﴿أوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — "إنَّهُ" is also permissible, but the reading is "أنَّهُ" with fatḥa. The position of "بِرَبِّكَ" is nominative in meaning; the meaning is: "Is your Lord not sufficient...?!" The position of "أنَّهُ" is accusative, or if you wish it is nominative. The meaning with the accusative is: "Is your Lord not sufficient in that He is Witness over all things?" And whoever takes it as nominative does so as a badal (substitute); the meaning is: "Is it not sufficient that your Lord is Witness over all things?", that is: "Does the testimony of your Lord not suffice them?!" The meaning of sufficiency here is that He has made clear to them what suffices as proof of His oneness, and His messengers have made it clear.

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿ألا إنَّهم في مِرْيَةٍ مِن لِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: in doubt. "ألا" is a word with which [speech] is begun; the one addressed is alerted by it, as an emphasis indicating the soundness of what follows it. ﴿ألا إنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطٌ﴾, that is: Knower of all things, with a knowledge that encompasses what is manifest and what is hidden.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿وَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 7], that is: they do not consider it obligatory upon them, and they do not give it.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿قُلْ أإنَّكم لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَ الأرْضَ في يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ — had He, Majestic and Exalted is He, willed to create it in an instant, He would have done so, and that would have been well within His power; but He loved that creation should see the aspects of deliberateness, and of power to create the heavens and the earth in many days and in a single instant, because all created beings and the angels brought near, if they gathered together to create the weight of a speck of it, would not create it. And it has come in the commentary that the beginning of the creation of the earth was on Sunday, and its creation was completed on Monday.
